title.rendered: How to see parts and service history on iPhone (iOS 27)

content.rendered:
When you send your iPhone for a repair or plan to buy a refurbished one, its service history is more important than most people realise. Apple’s Parts and Service History feature makes it easy to see whether key components like the screen, battery, display, camera, or Logic Board have been replaced.

In this guide, you’ll learn how to check Parts and Service History on your iPhone and understand what each label really means, so you can make smarter decisions with confidence.

What is parts and service history on iPhone?

Parts and Service History is a built-in iOS feature that logs any component that has been replaced or serviced. It indicates whether the part is genuine Apple hardware, an unknown third‑party component, or a used part that was previously installed in another device.

Apple introduced this feature to:

  • Improve repair transparency.
  • Protect users from poor-quality components.
  • Help buyers verify that the repair used genuine Apple parts.
  • Check the used or refurbished iPhone is original, avoiding scams.

Having genuine parts is important as they work better and last longer. Also, it helps keep up the resale value of your iPhone.

How Apple’s parts and service history works

Apple uses software and repair-calibration processes to identify and configure replaced components. When a supported repair is completed, Apple’s systems can verify the component and install the calibration data required for it to work correctly.

For supported repairs, Repair Assistant can finish the calibration process after a part is replaced. On supported devices, it can also calibrate a previously used part from another device of the same model.

The best part is:

  • You cannot edit or reset this section. If a component has been serviced more than once, only the most recent service appears.
  • Apple does not track personal data.
  • It is strictly read-only information.

Note: If your iPhone has never been repaired, the Parts and Service History section will not appear at all.

When you should check parts and service history

You should check this section in several situations:

  • Before buying a used or refurbished iPhone: Verify repair claims, confirm genuine parts, and avoid hidden issues.
  • After screen, battery, or camera replacement: Ensure the repair was completed correctly.
  • When troubleshooting performance issues like battery draining fast, Face ID or camera problems, or display issues.
  • Before selling or trading in your iPhone: Buyers may check it for genuine parts, which increases trust and value.

iPhone models that support parts and service history

Apple gradually rolled out this feature across models starting from iOS 15.2 and later:

If you have an iPhone 15 or later, you can also see if the replaced Apple hardware was previously used in another iPhone.

How to see parts and service history on iPhone (step by step)

Follow these simple steps:

  1. Open Settings and go to General.
  2. Tap About.
  3. If your iPhone has been repaired, you will see Parts and Service History.
  4. Tap it to see the list of replaced components like Display, Battery, Camera, etc.
  5. Each part shows a status label such as Genuine, Used, Unknown, and Unverified.
  6. Tap the component for more information about it, including the date of service. Ensure your iPhone is connected to the internet.

If the repair was not completed, it shows a Finish Repair message. It means the repair has not yet completed the required calibration process.

Understanding parts and service history labels

  • Genuine: Official Apple component properly paired and calibrated.
  • Used (iPhone 15 and Later): Genuine Apple part previously used in another iPhone. Still verified by Apple.
  • Unknown: Apple cannot verify the part. May be third-party or improperly installed.
  • Unverified: Logic Board was previously replaced as part of a repair. This may affect certain features, such as Apple Pay.
  • Finish Repair Message: If the setup or calibration was not done after the replacement, you will see it. You can’t use Face ID or Touch ID to unlock your device or to sign in to apps until it’s done.

To finish the repair, connect the iPhone to Wi-Fi and make sure the battery is above 20 per cent. Then open Settings > General > About > Parts & Service History. Tap Restart & Finish Repair. Finally, follow the on-screen instructions.

What genuine Apple part means

A Genuine Apple Part means the repair was completed using genuine Apple parts and Apple’s repair/calibration processes.

It does not necessarily mean the repair was performed only by Apple or an Apple Authorised Service Provider. Apple also provides genuine parts to Independent Repair Providers and, where supported, through Self Service Repair.

Benefits

  • Proper calibration and compatibility with supported iOS features.
  • Repairs meet Apple’s performance, security, privacy, and safety expectations.
  • A clearer repair record for buyers and trade-in providers.
  • Higher resale and trade-in value.
  • Safer long-term use.

What used part means

A Used label means the part was already used or installed in another iPhone.

On supported iPhone models, Repair Assistant can calibrate compatible reused parts from another device of the same model. A used part may function differently from a new part because of prior use or modification.

What unknown part or non-genuine part means

This label appears when Apple cannot verify the replacement part or its repair status. It can appear when a part is non-genuine, isn’t functioning as expected, hasn’t been verified and linked after the repair, or has been modified or otherwise cannot be verified.

An Unknown label does not automatically prove that a part is counterfeit or that the iPhone is unsafe. It means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. An Unknown part might affect the trade-in value of the device.

Possible downsides

  • Battery health issues.
  • Face ID or camera problems.
  • Lower resale value.
  • The part may not perform as expected.
  • Some repaired functions may require further diagnosis or calibration.
  • The Unknown label may affect trade-in value.

Messages about replaced parts or multiple repairs

To help you combat poor-quality servicing, your iPhone shows a notification the first time you unlock it after a repair and again in five days if an unknown part is found.

This indicates the replacement part:

  • Is non-genuine.
  • Isn’t functioning as expected.
  • Hasn’t been verified and linked to your iPhone after the repair was done.
  • Has been modified or can’t be verified.

You can contact the repair service provider about this.

For display and battery repairs, you may also see the message “Apple has updated the device information for this iPhone.” Apple says this indicates that it has updated device information maintained for safety analysis and to improve future products.

If a component problem significantly affects the device’s functionality and needs attention, your iPhone can show a one-time notification that remains in Parts and Service History until dismissed.

What to do if your iPhone shows unknown or unverified parts

You have a few options:

  • Visit Apple, an Apple Authorised Service Provider, or a reputable Independent Repair Provider with access to genuine Apple parts.
  • Ask the repair provider to diagnose the part and complete any required calibration.
  • Replace the part with a genuine Apple component. If the issue involves a previously used part, check whether it is protected by Activation Lock.
  • If buying a used iPhone, ask the seller about the repair and consider the potential effect of an Unknown part on trade-in value.

If buying a used iPhone, you may negotiate the price or consider returning the device to avoid future hassles and security issues.

Note that repairs performed by Independent Repair Providers are not covered by Apple’s warranty or AppleCare plans, although the provider may offer its own repair warranty.

Best Practices to Keep Service History Clean

  • Choose Apple, an Apple Authorised Service Provider, Apple’s Self Service Repair program, or an Independent Repair Provider with access to genuine Apple parts where supported.
  • Complete repairs properly and check everything before accepting the device.
  • If Finish Repair appears, complete the repair with Repair Assistant.
  • Check Parts & Service History after the repair.
  • Keep service receipts and repair documentation.
  • Before a trade-in, make sure there are no unfinished repairs and prepare the device using the current iOS 27 Ready for Repair or Trade In workflow when applicable.

Note: If you have multiple repairs for the same component, your iPhone will show the status of the most recent repair.

Final thoughts

Checking Parts and Service History on iPhone is simple but extremely powerful. It helps buyers avoid scams, owners verify repair quality, and sellers understand what a future buyer or trade-in provider may see.

For iOS 27, the feature is more useful than ever because Apple now distinguishes between Genuine, Used, Unknown, and Unverified parts and provides Repair Assistant for completing calibration on supported repairs.

If you are preparing an iPhone for repair or trade-in, iOS 27 also gives you a new Ready for Repair or Trade-In workflow through Find My, making the preparation process different from older iOS versions.

If you found this guide helpful, save it and share it with anyone buying or selling an iPhone.

FAQs

How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?

Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?

An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

Can I reset parts and service history?

No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

Do third-party repairs affect warranty?

Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

Does service history affect resale value?

Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?

Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

step.text: Scroll down and tap on the General option to proceed.

itemListElement.text: Scroll and select the General menu in Settings.

step.name: Tap About
step.text: In the General menu, tap on About to view your device information.

itemListElement.text: Tap About to open your iPhone's basic details.

step.name: Check Parts and Service History
step.text: If your iPhone has been serviced, you’ll see a Parts and Service History section. Tap it to view more details.

itemListElement.text: Look for the Parts and Service History section and tap on it.

step.name: Review component details
step.text: You’ll see a list of replaced components with labels like Genuine, Used, or Unknown. Tap a component to get more info, including service date.

itemListElement.text: Tap any listed component to see more information and service details.

blockGraphs.question: How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?
blockGraphs.answer: Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

blockGraphs.question: Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?
blockGraphs.answer: An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

blockGraphs.question: Can I reset parts and service history?
blockGraphs.answer: No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

blockGraphs.question: Do third-party repairs affect warranty?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

blockGraphs.question: Does service history affect resale value?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

blockGraphs.question: Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?
blockGraphs.answer: Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

title.rendered: iOS history: Every version from iPhone OS 1 to iOS 27 explained

content.rendered:
Since its debut in 2007 alongside the first iPhone, iOS has come a long way. Each new version has brought fresh features, design changes, and performance improvements. iPhone OS 2 brought the App Store, while iOS 14 incorporated 5G connectivity, iOS 18 introduced Apple Intelligence features, and iOS 27 finally brings Siri AI.

In this editorial, we will revisit history and discuss different versions of iOS, from the initial iPhone OS to the recently launched iOS 27. You will learn about the key updates of various versions and the turning points in the evolution of the iOS operating system.

iOS 27 – September 14, 2026

Apple released iOS 27 with a strong focus on Apple Intelligence, making the iPhone more intelligent, personal, and capable of taking actions across apps. Apple’s headline feature is Siri AI, a redesigned version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence.

Siri AI can understand personal context, understand what is on your screen, perform actions in supported apps, answer questions using online information, and maintain conversations through a new dedicated Siri app. Apple is also bringing Siri-powered writing tools, Camera-based Visual Intelligence, smarter Shortcuts, AI-powered photo editing, and more.

Apple has also expanded iOS 27 features beyond AI. The update introduces new child-safety controls, refinements to Liquid Glass, faster app and photo loading, quicker AirDrop transfers, a redesigned Health experience, new accessibility tools, improved iCloud Shared Albums, AirPods Custom EQ, and GymKit support on iPhone.

Key features of iOS 27

  • Siri AI transforms Siri into a conversational AI assistant that can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, follow-up conversations, and more natural requests.
  • Dedicated Siri app stores conversations so you can revisit previous discussions, continue them later, pin important ones, and pick them up across Apple devices.
  • Siri mode in Camera combines Siri and Visual Intelligence so you can point your camera at something, ask questions about it, search for information, and take actions based on what you see.
  • Write with Siri can create drafts, provide feedback on existing writing, and adjust writing style and tone. In Messages and Mail, it can also adapt to your writing style.
  • AI-powered photo editing adds Spatial Reframing, Extend, and an upgraded Clean Up tool for making more extensive edits to photos.
  • Image Playground improvements allow you to create and transform images using descriptions, including photorealistic styles.
  • Apple Intelligence Suggestions in Messages and Mail can recommend contextual actions, such as creating a reminder, adding a calendar event, or finding a photo.
  • Call Context can surface relevant information from your other apps while you are on a call, such as finding a confirmation code stored in Mail.
  • Smarter Safari in iOS 27 can automatically organize tabs into related topics. Also, Notify Me can monitor webpages and notify you when something changes, such as product restocks.
  • Password improvements allow the Passwords app to identify weak or compromised passwords and help update them.
  • AI-powered Shortcuts introduces Describe a Shortcut, allowing you to create automations simply by explaining what you want the shortcut to do in natural language.
  • New child-safety controls give parents more control over which apps children can use during initial setup. Time Allowances allow parents to set usage limits for categories such as Games, Entertainment, and Social Media.
  • Ask to Browse requires children to request parental permission before accessing new websites.
  • New Liquid Glass appearance controls let users adjust the interface between a clearer and more tinted appearance.
  • Smarter Mail Search uses a new ranking system to bring more relevant messages to the top of search results.
  • Improved iCloud Shared Albums makes it easier for Android and Windows users to participate through iCloud.com, while adding full-resolution sharing and new filtering and reaction options.
  • Enhanced Apple Maps Flyover combines aerial imagery with Visual Intelligence models to produce more detailed views of locations.
  • Smarter Home app features use Apple Intelligence to combine related activity notifications, describe what happened in HomeKit Secure Video footage, and search video clips using event descriptions.
  • GymKit on iPhone lets compatible gym equipment connect to the iPhone for real-time workout metrics.
  • Health app redesign introduces a new Insights tab that brings together information such as heart health, sleep, readiness, etc. AI-powered Health insights provide easier-to-understand summaries and guidance.
  • Perimenopause and menopause support expands Cycle Tracking with notifications based on cycle patterns, symptom tracking, and educational resources.
  • FaceTime improvements include Dual Capture, allowing compatible iPhones to capture video from the front and rear cameras simultaneously.

iOS 26 – September 15, 2025

Apple unveiled iOS 26 during WWDC 2025 on June 9, marking a significant shift in the iPhone’s software journey. It introduced a bold redesign and a new naming convention—aligning the version number with the calendar year of intended use (2026). This change brought uniformity across all Apple platforms, including macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and tvOS.

The standout feature of iOS 26 is the Liquid Glass design language, inspired by visionOS. This aesthetic replaces the long-standing flat design introduced in iOS 7 with translucent, curved, and refractive UI elements that feel more fluid and immersive. Apps like Camera, Photos, Messages, and Phone received major interface upgrades, creating a more cohesive user experience.

Apple also supercharged its Apple Intelligence suite. With improvements to Visual Intelligence, Image Playground, and Shortcuts, iOS 26 introduced new capabilities like Live Translation, Call Screening, and DJ-style Audio Mix. Even CarPlay saw enhancements, with support for Live Activities and Tapbacks.

Apple released the developer beta of iOS 26 on June 9, 2025, followed by the public beta in July. The full version rolled out in September alongside the launch of the iPhone 17 series.

Key Features of iOS 26

  • A striking new Liquid Glass design language featuring translucent, refractive UI elements—widgets, icons, controls.
  • The clock resizes based on Lock Screen wallpaper subjects and the notification stack.
  • 3D Spatial Scene wallpapers make images pop when tilted.
  • Live Translation offers real‑time language translation in Messages, FaceTime, and Phone calls.
  • Visual Intelligence analyzes screenshots or on-screen content to search for objects or text, allowing for interaction across multiple apps.
  • Genmoji lets you create personalized emojis by combining existing ones.
  • Image Playground received a new ChatGPT-style for image creation.
  • Shortcuts include Apple Intelligence tools in workflows.
  • AI auto‑suggest reminders from messages/emails.
  • Adaptive Power Mode saves battery when usage peaks, without entering Low Power Mode.
  • The Lock Screen displays charging time estimates; battery settings provide color-coded usage statistics.
  • Call Screening asks for the caller’s identity and intent.
  • Hold Assist automatically waits on hold during phone calls until a real person answers.
  • The Messages app now features real-time typing indicators, built-in poll creation in group chats, custom backgrounds, and spam-sorting filters.
  • Safari in iOS 26 received a compact layout style, web app support for all websites, and improved link tracking protection.
  • The new Games app organizes recently played titles and provides personalized recommendations.
  • The Music app gets a live radio widget, DJ-Style AutoMix, and Lyric Translations.
  • The Photos app introduced separate Library and Collections tabs, as well as support for 3D spatial photos.
  • Apple Maps in iOS 26 included tracking preferred routes and Visited Places.
  • Use AirPods to control iPhone camera—press or hold to snap a photo or start a video.
  • CarPlay now features a compact call view, Tapbacks, and pinned conversations in Messages.
  • Digital U.S. Passport support in Wallet.
  • Recovery Assistant introduced restoration using another iPhone or iPad.
  • You can now set custom snooze durations in the Alarm app.

iOS 18 – September 16, 2024

Apple gave iPhone users a preview of iOS 18 at WWDC 2024 and officially launched it on September 16, 2024, along with the iPhone 16 series. This major update significantly boosts personalization options across the system and apps. You can customize the Home Screen layout and change the app icon theme.

Additionally, the Control Center can be customized to accommodate new quick controls. For advanced privacy, iOS 18 allows users to lock apps and select which apps can access specific contacts.

The native apps, especially the Photos, Notes, and Mail apps, also received a major overhaul. Further, the company introduced a powerful AI-powered feature called Apple Intelligence. Last but not least, the iOS 18 Accessibility features make it easier to navigate the iPhone.

Key features of iOS 18

  • Apple Intelligence features such as Genmoji, Math Notes, etc.
  • Call recording
  • Customizable Home Screen
  • Redesigned Control Center
  • New controls on the Lock Screen
  • Lock and hide apps
  • A new Passwords app
  • Collections and Clean Up tool in the Photos app
  • iPhone Game mode
  • Text effects in Messages
  • New emojis in Tapback
  • Schedule messages with Send Later
  • Messages via Satellite
  • Categories in the Mail app
  • Highlights in Safari
  • Redesigned Reader in Safari
  • Calculator history
  • Download topographic maps
  • Tap to Cash in the Wallet app
  • Live audio transcription in Notes
  • Integrated Reminders in Calendar
  • Enhanced Journal app

iOS 17 – September 18, 2023

iOS 17 was announced at WWDC 2023. The focus of iOS 17 was on redesigning and upgrading the system apps and features. The Message, FaceTime, and Phone apps have several enhancements. Additionally, Apple enhanced connectivity by introducing NameDrop and FaceTime on Apple TV.

The most highlighted features of iOS 17:

  • Personalized Contact Posters 
  • Live Voicemail 
  • Video voicemail and Reactions on FaceTime 
  • Search Filter, Catch up arrow, Swipe to reply, Transcription of voice messages, Check-in features in the Messages app
  • Live Stickers 
  • StandBy feature 
  • Share a contact card using NameDrop 
  • Journal app
  • The mindfulness feature on the Health app
  • Create Profiles on Safari 
  • Collaborated playlist on CarPlay
  • Upgraded Autocorrect and Dictation abilities 

iOS 16 – September 12, 2022

iOS 16 was announced at the WWDC event in June 2022 and released in September 2022.

The most noticeable upgrade in iOS 16 was the addition of supported features for the Dynamic Island on iPhone 14 Pro models. It made the new notch design more fun by displaying animated notifications and offering controls around the camera. 

Also, Crash Detection, Always-on display, Emergency SOS via Satellite, and other exclusive features of the iPhone 14 series are supported with iOS 16. 

Key features of iOS 16:

  • Customizable Lock Screen
  • Live Activities
  • Better Focus Filters
  • New Message features
  • Redesigned Apple Maps
  • Apple Pay Later
  • Apple Order Tracking
  • iCloud Shared Photo Library
  • Live Texts on videos
  • Passkeys
  • Safety Check function
  • Improvements to Spatial Audio
  • Voice Isolation in phone calls
  • Advanced Data Protection for iCloud
  • Apple Music Sing karaoke

iOS 15 – September 24, 2021

Unlike iOS 16, the iOS 15 update focused more on software bug fixes, system improvements, and refining the features of built-in apps.

Additionally, the pandemic era influenced the introduction of these feature upgrades. Apple focused on enhancing security and privacy, preventing ad tracking, and improving Siri, Camera, FaceTime, Messages, and other features. 

As of writing, iOS 15 is supported on the iPhone 6S series and later, as well as the iPod touch 7th generation.  

Key features of iOS 15:

  • New FaceTime features – Spatial audio, SharePlay, FaceTime Link, Mic modes, Portrait modes, etc.
  • iMessage Share with you 
  • Better Focus Filters with Notification Summary, Signal your status, etc.
  • Live Text and Memory features in the Photos app
  • Advanced Spotlight search
  • App Privacy Report
  • Mail Privacy Protection
  • On-device Siri
  • Digital Legacy program
  • Redesigned Safari tabs
  • Detailed Maps  
  • Improved Health and Wallet app

iOS 14 – September 17, 2020

The iOS 14 version lists similar system improvements, very much like iOS 15. There were no significant changes. Apple added several enhancements, including privacy controls, Home Screen widgets, and customization options. 

Key features of iOS 14:

  • Widgets on the Home Screen
  • App Library
  • Improved call notifications
  • Picture in Picture Mode
  • Redesigned Siri 
  • Translation, Password monitoring, and Website Privacy Report in Safari
  • Pinned Conversations and improved group texting in Messages
  • New Memoji Styles and Stickers
  • Cycling directions and Electric vehicle routing in Maps
  • Translate app
  • App Clips

iOS 13 – September 19, 2019

Before iOS 13, iPad also ran iOS. However, Apple took a significant step by introducing a new iPadOS, designed to make the iPad more productive and potentially serve as a laptop replacement. Since then, iOS and iPad OS have always been rolled out simultaneously.

The most noticeable new feature was the introduction of Dark Mode. Additionally, iOS 13 improved essential functions, such as faster app start-up, Face ID, Portrait Lighting, and the redesign of pre-installed apps.

Key features of iOS 13: 

  • System-wide Dark Mode
  • 30% faster Face ID unlocking
  • Revamped Apple Maps
  • Smarter HomeKit
  • Sign In With your Apple user account
  • New privacy and security options
  • Portrait Lighting Effects
  • New, improved Siri voice
  • Overhauled system apps like Photos, Mail, Reminders, and Notes

iOS 12 – September 17, 2018

The 12th iteration of the iPhone software had just a few new additions. Primarily, it improved regularly used functionality for providing a better user experience. Apple introduced Siri Shortcuts, ARKit 2, Screen Time tracking, etc.

Key features of iOS 12:

  • Grouped Notifications
  • Screen Time
  • ARKit 2 for enhanced Augmented Reality
  • Siri improvements
  • Memoji

iOS 11 – September 19, 2017

iOS 11 has special features to support the iPod touch, iPad, Apple Watch, and Apple TV.

Therefore, its primary features included more iPad-specific features, such as split-screen apps, drag-and-drop functionality, a file browser app, and support for Apple Pencil handwriting. 

Key features of iOS 11:

  • iPad functions
  • AirPlay 2 
  • Support for Augmented Reality

iOS 10 – September 13, 2016

The release of iOS 10 was a watershed moment for the Apple ecosystem. It offered several APIs to integrate third-party solutions into the system apps. Thus, the iPhone gained a boost in interoperability and customization through its UI and applications. Additionally, Siri has become more accessible to third-party apps. The best part was that Apple allowed users to uninstall built-in apps.

Key features of iOS 10:

  • Embedded ​iMessage apps
  • Delete built-in apps
  • Split Control Center into multiple panels
  • Integration of Siri with third-party apps
  • Smarter QuickType keyboard
  • 3D Touch displayed widgets 

iOS 9 – September 16, 2015

iOS 9 prioritized building a solid base for the operating system to improve the speed, responsiveness, stability, and performance of older devices. After significant modifications to iOS’s design and technological base, users started to feel that iOS was no longer the reliable, trustworthy, and competent it had previously been. 

So, Apple decided to focus on strengthening the OS’s foundation rather than introducing new features, laying the groundwork for the larger enhancements in the next iOS updates. To garner public reaction and acceptance, iOS introduced the Public Beta feature. So, before the actual release of the upcoming iOS version update, people can get a taste of it.

Key features of iOS 9:

  • Night Shift
  • Low Power Mode
  • Public beta program

iOS 8 – September 17, 2014

In iOS history, iOS 8 was a significant update as it introduced the contactless payment system Apple Pay and the Apple Music subscription service. It also polished the iCloud features for more reliable and consistent performance. The most useful feature unveiled was the Handoff feature, which allows for seamless switching between Apple devices.

Apple walked in with a Dropbox-like iCloud Drive and the addition of an iCloud Picture Library and an iCloud Music Library. To save subscription costs, Apple offered Family Sharing, which allows users to enjoy content individually with a single subscription. Moreover, the HealthKit and HomeKit features focused on users’ daily lives.

Key features of iOS 8:

  • Apple Music
  • Apple Pay
  • iCloud Drive
  • Handoff
  • Family Sharing
  • Spotlight Suggestions
  • QuickType on keyboard
  • HomeKit and HealthKit
  • Extensibility framework for third-party extensions

iOS 7 – September 18, 2013

iOS 7 was a troublesome update, and users were dissatisfied as things didn’t operate as expected. The update included a significant redesign of the user interface, opting for a flat look. However, some users found it difficult to read due to the tiny, thin letters, and others experienced motion sickness from the constant animations. 

Additionally, Apple provided quick access to the most frequently used features through Control Center and introduced AirDrop, Activation Lock, and CarPlay. Additionally, Siri got new voices and a redesigned look.

Key features of iOS 8:

  • Activation Lock
  • AirDrop
  • CarPlay
  • Control Center
  • Thumbnails in App Switcher
  • Improved Notification Center
  • Smarter Siri
  • Touch ID

iOS 6 – September 19, 2012

In the history of iOS versions, iOS 6 saw the most controversy due to Apple’s escalating rivalry with Google. Although the newly launched Siri was a significant breakthrough in technology, issues with it led to substantial revisions.

Besides, from iPhone OS version 1.0, Google has included the Maps and YouTube applications pre-installed. But this time, Apple replaced Google Maps with a new Apple Maps. It fell short due to glitches, inaccurate instructions, and issues with other functionalities. 

Sidelining the flaws, iOS 6 features a Podcast app, a more capable Siri, a Panoramic mode in the Camera, and the ability to make FaceTime calls over cellular data.

Key features of iOS 6:

  • Apple Maps
  • Do Not Disturb
  • Passbook (now Wallet)
  • New features in Siri, like launching apps
  • Panoramic photos
  • FaceTime over cellular data

iOS 5 – October 12, 2011

iOS 5 was a turning point for Apple, as it introduced crucial new features, including Siri, iCloud, wireless iPhone activation, and Wi-Fi iTunes syncing. Users could download and install software updates on their iPhones without a computer. Additionally, for a better user experience and accessibility, the iPhone features Notification Center and iMessage.

Key features of iOS 5:

  • Siri
  • iCloud
  • iMessage
  • Notification Center
  • Redesigned Reminders and Newsstand apps
  • Wireless syncing and activation

iOS 4 – June 22, 2010

With iOS 4, the futuristic iOS began to take form as Apple renamed the “iPhone OS” to “iOS” for the first time. Many revisions to this version included features such as FaceTime, multitasking, iBooks, Game Center, organizing programs into folders, custom wallpapers, Personal Hotspot, AirPlay, and AirPrint.

Moreover, Apple included Bing as a search engine for Safari and enabled users to consolidate multiple email accounts into a single inbox. It was the first iteration of iOS to stop supporting all iOS devices. It was incompatible with the first-generation iPod touch or the iPhone.

Key features of iOS 4:

  • FaceTime
  • Multitasking
  • AirPlay
  • AirPrint
  • iBooks
  • Game Center
  • Personal Hotspot
  • System-wide spell checking
  • 5x digital zoom

iPhone OS 3 (iOS 3) – June 17, 2009

iOS 3 was the first operating system for the iPad and came pre-installed on the iPhone 3GS without any additional charge. Users could copy and paste text system-wide. Besides, Spotlight search, MMS support in the Messages app, and the capability to shoot films using the Camera app are just a few of the new features it includes.

Key features of iOS 3;

  • Copy and paste​
  • Spotlight​ search​
  • Voice Memo app
  • Recording videos

iPhone OS 2 (iOS 2) – July 11, 2008

iPhone OS 2 was meant for the iPhone 3G model, which included support for the 3G network. As the iPhone became a huge hit, app developers attempted to jailbreak it to install third-party apps. So, Apple introduced development tools like APIs and SDKs for software companies to launch apps in the App Store, thereby preventing the installation of apps from the web.

The App Store had around 500 applications when it debuted. Podcast support, walking and public transportation instructions in Maps, an iTunes Genuine playlist, and enhancements to Mail, Calculator, and Contacts using Microsoft Exchange support were other significant additions to iPhone OS 2.

Key features of iOS 2:

  • App Store​
  • Developer APIs and SDKs
  • Support for Microsoft ActiveSync and Microsoft Exchange
  • Improved Maps app​

iPhone OS 1 (iOS 1) – June 29, 2007

iOS debuted with the release of the first iPhone in June 2007. Nevertheless, it was mostly powered by OS X, the Mac software. It featured a core iOS UI, iTunes integration, Multi-touch gestures, Mobile Safari, iPod, Visual Voicemail, and Maps, which were advanced smartphone capabilities at the time.

However, it lacked support for third-party applications and came with basic pre-installed apps, including Calendar, Pictures, Camera, Notes, Mail, and Phone.

Key features of iOS 1:

  • Visual Voicemail​
  • Multitouch interface
  • Calculator
  • Calendar
  • Camera
  • Clock
  • iPod
  • iTunes
  • Mail
  • Maps
  • Music (iPod Touch)
  • Notes
  • Phone
  • Photos
  • Safari
  • Settings
  • Stocks
  • Text
  • Videos (iPod Touch)
  • Weather
  • YouTube

A Look Back—and Forward—at the History of iOS

From its humble beginnings as iPhone OS to the powerful and intelligent iOS 27, Apple’s mobile operating system has consistently led innovation in the smartphone world. Each update has not only refined the user experience but also anticipated what’s next in mobile technology.

As Apple moves forward with Siri AI, Apple Intelligence, spatial design, and deeper device integration, iOS continues to set the standard for what a modern mobile OS can achieve.

mainEntity.name: How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

mainEntity.name: Can I reset parts and service history?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

mainEntity.name: Do third-party repairs affect warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

mainEntity.name: Does service history affect resale value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

mainEntity.name: Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

About Ava Biswas

  • Ava is a die-hard Apple aficionado and loves testing the latest tech gadgets.
  • She is always on the lookout for issues Apple users are facing, finds solutions, and crafts troubleshooting guides.
  • Her goal to make tech easy for everyone encouraged her to break down complex concepts into easily digestible content.

title.rendered: How to remove the iOS 27 beta and install the official version

content.rendered:
The wait is finally over! Apple just dropped the stable iOS 27 update, right alongside the new iPhone 18 Pro lineup. If you’ve been running the iOS 27 beta to test its features, now’s the perfect time to switch over to the official release. Because beta builds can contain bugs, compatibility problems, and unfinished features.

The good news is that Apple makes it relatively easy to stop receiving future beta updates. However, there’s an important distinction: turning beta updates off doesn’t uninstall the beta version already running on your iPhone.

In this step-by-step guide, I’ll walk you through how to remove iOS 27 beta from your iPhone and install the polished, bug-free version.

Why you should remove iOS 27 beta

The answer is simple: betas are buggy.

Depending on the build, these can include:

  • Apps crashing unexpectedly
  • Quick battery draining
  • Performance glitches
  • Features behaving differently between beta versions
  • Compatibility issues with third-party apps
  • Unexpected interface changes

Apple constantly tweaks features in each beta based on feedback. That’s the trade-off for getting access to upcoming iOS features before the general public.

On the other hand, the official iOS 27 update is stable, polished, and designed for everyday users. You can fully enjoy the new iOS 27 features, including all the Apple Intelligence-powered tools such as Siri AI, Notify Me in Safari, Describe a Shortcut, automatic password fixing, Extend and Reframe in Photos, and much more. 

So, if you no longer need early access to upcoming features, switching back to the public release channel can make your iPhone experience more predictable.

What happens when you turn off beta updates?

This is the part I would pay the most attention to.

Turning off Beta Updates doesn’t instantly remove the beta version from your iPhone. Instead, it tells your iPhone that you don’t want to receive future beta updates.

For example, if you’re currently running an iOS 27 beta that is newer than the available public version, turning beta updates off won’t magically replace that software with an older public build.

You’ll generally have two options:

  1. Wait for the public release to catch up: If the next public iOS release is newer than the beta currently installed on your iPhone, you can install it normally.
  2. Restore the iPhone: If you want to leave the beta immediately and the public version is older than your installed beta, you’ll need to erase the device and install the current public iOS version using a Mac or PC.

This distinction is important because many users assume that switching Beta Updates to Off automatically downgrades the iPhone. It doesn’t.

Preparations before updating

Before upgrading from iOS 27 beta to the stable release, do some prep work. Trust me, it saves time and avoids frustration.

  • Backup Your Data: Make a manual backup via Finder or iTunes. iCloud backups from a beta iPhone can’t be restored to the stable version. Encrypt it if you want to keep Health data and passwords.
  • Check Storage: The update file is a few GBs. Free up space and aim for at least 15 GB available.
  • Connect to Wi-Fi: Updates are large. Use Wi-Fi to avoid draining your mobile data.
  • Charge Your iPhone: Ensure 50% battery or keep it plugged in throughout the process.

These steps keep everything smooth and stress-free, so you’re all set for the fun part! 

How to remove iOS 27 beta

Apple makes it super easy to stop beta updates.

  1. Open the Settings app and tap General.  
  2. Select Software Update.  
  3. Tap Beta Updates. You’ll see options like Developer Beta or Public Beta.  
  4. Simply choose Off to prevent receiving iOS 27 beta updates on your iPhone.
     

Your iPhone will no longer receive future beta updates through the beta channel. However, remember that your current beta version remains installed.

How to install the iOS 27 official version

Once beta updates are turned off, your iPhone will automatically fetch the stable iOS 27 release.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Wait for your iPhone to detect iOS 27.
  3. Tap Download and Install.
  4. Agree to the terms and enter your passcode.
  5. Let it download (10–30 minutes depending on Wi-Fi).
  6. Tap Install Now when prompted.

Your iPhone will restart a couple of times. Once it boots up, you’ll see the setup screen. Unlock your device, and you’re officially on the stable iOS 27!

If you see “Unable to Check for Update,” don’t panic. Apple’s servers get busy right after launch. Just try again later.

What if I don’t see the public iOS 27 update?

Don’t assume something is wrong.

If your beta build is newer than the current public release, the public version may not appear as an available downgrade through Software Update.

In that situation, you can either:

  • Stay on the current beta until a newer public release becomes available, or
  • Use a Mac or PC to erase and restore the iPhone to the current public iOS version.

How to downgrade from iOS 27 beta using a Mac or PC

If you don’t want to wait for the public release to catch up with your beta, you’ll need to restore the iPhone.

Important: This process erases the iPhone.

Before continuing, make sure you have a backup that can be restored to the public iOS version you’re installing.

  1. Turn off your iPhone.
  2. Now, press and hold the Power button and immediately connect your iPhone to your Mac or PC via an MFi-certified cable.
  3. Keep holding the Power button even after the Apple logo appears until a lightning cable icon and an arrow pointing towards a laptop appear on the screen. Your iPhone will enter Recovery mode.
  4. Now, open Finder on your Mac or Apple Devices on PC and click the Restore button on the pop-up dialogue box that appears.
  5. Then, click the Restore and Update button.
  6. Next, follow the on-screen instructions to restore your iPhone to the available lower stable version.
  7. Wait for the process to complete.

Once the restore finishes, your iPhone will run the latest stable iOS version. Then you can download iOS 27 and restore your backup.

Enjoy iOS 27 bug-free

And that’s it! You’ve successfully switched from iOS 27 beta to the official release. Now you can enjoy all the new features—minus the bugs.

Pro tip: Always back up your iPhone before major updates. It’s your safety net in case something goes wrong.

If you hit a snag, drop a comment below or reach out to Apple Support for help. Happy updating!

mainEntity.name: How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

mainEntity.name: Can I reset parts and service history?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

mainEntity.name: Do third-party repairs affect warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

mainEntity.name: Does service history affect resale value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

mainEntity.name: Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

keyPoints.title: Why Removing iOS 26 Beta Is Necessary
keyPoints.explanation: Beta versions are often buggy, causing battery drain, app crashes, and glitches, so updating to the stable official release provides a more reliable experience.

keyPoints.title: Preparations Before Updating to iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Back up your data, check available storage, connect to Wi-Fi, and ensure your device is charged to avoid issues during the update process.

keyPoints.title: How to Remove iOS 26 Beta
keyPoints.explanation: Navigate to Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates and switch off beta updates to stop receiving iOS 26 beta builds.

keyPoints.title: Installing the Official iOS 26 Version
keyPoints.explanation: Disable beta updates, then go to Settings > General > Software Update, and follow prompts to download and install the stable iOS 26.

keyPoints.title: Downgrading from iOS 26 Beta via Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Enter recovery mode, connect your iPhone to Mac, then restore via Finder to revert to a lower stable iOS version, and restore your backup afterward.

title.rendered: How to turn off in-app purchases on iPhone and iPad

content.rendered:
I’ve had more than one reason to keep in-app purchases under control on an iPhone. A game can make a purchase look like a harmless upgrade, or a child using the device can tap through a payment prompt without realizing that it involves real money.

The good news is that Apple gives you a simple way to block in-app purchases completely. In this guide, I’ll show you how to disable in-app purchases on an iPhone or iPad, along with other ways to prevent unwanted purchases, including using a password and Ask to Buy for children.

What does ‘In-app purchases’ mean?

In-app purchases are things you buy from inside an app after downloading it. They can unlock additional features, content, subscriptions, virtual items, or other extras.

For example, a game might let you buy virtual currency, while a photo-editing app could offer a premium feature through an in-app purchase.

There are three common types of in-app purchases:

  • Subscriptions: These are recurring payments that give ongoing access to content or services, often set to auto-renew. Examples include Apple Music and Netflix subscriptions.
  • Non-consumable: One-time purchases that stay with you permanently. These don’t expire but can sometimes be upgraded. Examples include removing ads, unlocking extra game content, or adding features in a photo editing app.
  • Consumable: Items that can be used up and purchased again. Examples include game currency, extra lives, power-ups, or other virtual items.

How to disable In-app purchases on iPhone and iPad

Apple changed the location of the in-app purchase restriction in iOS 27. First, ensure that Screen Time is enabled on your iPhone to prevent unintentional or unauthorized purchases from the App Store and other Apple services. 

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Go to Screen Time and tap it.
  3. Tap Apps & Websites.
  4. Select App Store from the list.
  5. Tap In-app Purchases and choose Blocked from the dropdown.

That’s it! Once you select Blocked, in-app purchases are restricted on that device. Now, whenever someone tries to make a purchase on the iPhone or iPad, they’ll get an error message. This helps keep those impulse buys in check.

Note: If you don’t see the Apps & Websites option, make sure you’re running iOS 27 or later and that Screen Time is enabled. Apple has redesigned its parental controls in iOS 27. In previous versions, you needed to go to Content & Privacy Restrictions > iTunes & App Store Purchases.

How do I stop my child from making In-app purchases on iPhone and iPad

If your child has their own iPhone or iPad, I recommend using Apple’s Family Sharing and Ask to Buy features rather than simply disabling in-app purchases.

With Ask to Buy, your child can request eligible purchases or downloads, and you can review the request before deciding whether to approve it. Apple has integrated these controls into the updated iOS 27 parental-control system.

Set up Ask to Buy

If your child is part of your Family Sharing group, you can configure purchase approval from your own iPhone or iPad.

To use this feature, ensure Family Sharing is set up with your child, then follow these steps:

  1. Open Settings and tap Family.
  2. Select your child’s name.
  3. Tap Apps & Websites.
  4. If prompted, enter your Screen Time passcode.
  5. Tap Restrictions and select Ask to Buy.
  6. Turn on Require Purchase Approval.

After you enable it, your child can send a request when they want to make an eligible purchase or download. Request notifications appear in Messages. You can then review the request and approve or decline it.

Important: Apple’s new iOS 27 parental controls work best when the devices in your Family Sharing group are updated to the latest software versions.

Require a password for every purchase

If you don’t want to completely block purchases, another option is to require authentication before purchases are made. I use this method because I occasionally make in-app purchases myself, but I don’t want someone else to buy subscriptions using my iPhone without my knowledge.

The important part is to avoid sharing the password or authentication method that authorizes purchases.

Here is how to set this up:

  1. Go to Screen Time settings.
  2. Tap Apps & Websites and select App Store.

  3. Tap the dropdown next to Require Password and select Always.

If you’re primarily trying to prevent a child from buying something while using your own device, requiring authentication for purchases can be more practical than completely disabling purchasing.

Disconnect the payment method from the device

Another effective way to prevent kids from making In-app purchases on the App Store is to remove the payment method. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Tap your Apple ID at the top, then select Payment & Shipping.

  3. Tap Edit in the top-right corner.
  4. Tap the red Delete button, then confirm with Remove.

Signing off

With these steps to turn off In-app purchases on your iPhone or iPad, you can prevent kids or anyone else with access to your device from making unnecessary purchases—and even keep your own impulse buys in check. You can also use the other methods we covered to restrict In-app purchases on your device or your child’s. Hope you found this guide helpful!

FAQs

How do I hide In-app purchases on my iPhone?

You can’t hide In-app purchases from your purchase history on an iPhone, but you can hide apps from your purchase list in the App Store. To learn how, check our guide on hiding App Store purchases.

How do I cancel an app purchase on my iPhone?

To cancel an app purchase, go to Settings > tap on Apple ID > Subscription > select the subscription you want to cancel > tap on Cancel Subscription.

Can I see what was purchased?

Yes. Apple provides purchase history so you can review purchases made through your Apple Account. This is especially useful if you’re trying to identify an unexpected charge or check whether a family member made a purchase.

mainEntity.name: How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

mainEntity.name: Can I reset parts and service history?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

mainEntity.name: Do third-party repairs affect warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

mainEntity.name: Does service history affect resale value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

mainEntity.name: Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

mainEntity.name: How do I cancel an app purchase on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: To cancel an app purchase, go to Settings > tap on Apple ID > Subscription > select the subscription you want to cancel > tap on Cancel Subscription.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: Local Capture on iPad: what it is, how it works, and how to use it

content.rendered:
When Apple introduced Local Capture in iPadOS 26, I immediately saw its potential for anyone who records interviews, podcasts, meetings, or other video calls.

In iPadOS 27, the feature remains one of the most useful built-in tools for creators because it lets you record high-quality audio and video locally while you’re on a video call, no matter which app you’re using.

In this guide, I’ll explain what Local Capture does, how to set it up in iPadOS 27, where recordings are saved, how to use an external microphone, and what you need to know to get the best results.

What is Local Capture on iPad?

Local Capture is a feature introduced with iPadOS 26 that enables users to record their own audio and video locally on the iPad during an active video call. Unlike a normal screen recording, Local Capture isn’t designed to capture everything happening on your display. It records your own camera video and microphone audio locally.

This makes it particularly useful for:

  • Remote podcast interviews
  • Online interviews
  • Video meetings
  • Webinars and presentations
  • Educational sessions
  • Content creation
  • Remote video production
  • Recording your own side of a conversation for later editing

Once the video call ends, your recording is automatically stored in the Files app for safekeeping and easy sharing. Apple designed the feature around a workflow similar to a double-ender: each person records their own high-quality audio and video locally, and the recordings can then be combined in apps such as Logic Pro or Final Cut Pro.

Key Benefits of Local Capture:

  • Records directly from your iPad—no third-party apps required.
  • Compatible with any videoconferencing platform.
  • Captures uncompressed, high-quality audio and video.
  • Echo cancellation ensures only your voice is prioritised.
  • Also available on iPhones running iOS 26 and later.

How Local Capture works

Local Capture works independently of the videoconferencing app’s own recording system. For example, I can join a FaceTime, Zoom, Google Meet, or another supported app and use Local Capture from iPadOS itself.

Moreover, the feature is not enabled by default. You must turn it on manually whenever you want to record during a call.

When activated, Local Capture:

  • Records your microphone audio and camera video.
  • Uses echo cancellation to remove other participants’ voices.
  • Doesn’t apply Voice Isolation and Wide Spectrum filters. If your recording contains unwanted background noise, you’ll need to clean it up during post-production.
  • You can use supported AirPods to remotely start and stop recording during a videoconference.
  • Recordings are saved to the Downloads folder in Files by default. You can choose a different save location from Settings > General > Local Capture.

If another app is already using your camera, Local Capture records audio only. You can also deliberately choose Audio Only when starting a Local Capture session.

Note: It records only your audio and video, not the other participants’, to maintain privacy and clarity.

What you need to use Local Capture on iPad

Before you start, I recommend having:

  • An iPad running iPadOS 26 or later
  • Any videoconferencing app (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meet, etc.)
  • Camera and microphone access enabled for the calling app
  • Sufficient storage on your iPad
  • An external USB microphone if you want higher-quality audio

Apple also supports using compatible AirPods for recording audio and capturing video remotely during a videoconference.

How to set up Local Capture on iPad

Before using Local Capture, you need to add its button to Control Centre:

  1. Swipe down from the top-right corner of the iPad screen to open Control Center.
  2. Tap the + button to enter Control Center editing.
  3. Now, tap Add a Control.
  4. Next, use the search bar to find the Local Capture control button.
  5. Tap the Local Capture button to add it to the Control Center.
  6. Rearrange the control if you want it in a more convenient position.

Now, Local Capture will be accessible during any video call from the Control Center.

How to enable and use Local Capture on iPad

Once Local Capture is available in Control Center, recording is straightforward. Here’s how to start using Local Capture during a call:

  1. Join a video call using FaceTime, Zoom, Google Meet, or any other video calling app.
  2. Now, pull down the Control Centre.
  3. Touch and hold the Local Capture control. This opens the Local Capture options.
  4. By default, Local Capture records both audio and video. If you don’t need video, choose Audio Only.
  5. Tap Start Recording. Your iPad now records your local audio and video while you continue participating in the call.
  6. To stop the recording manually, go to Control Centre, tap the Local Capture control, and select End Recording, or wait until the call ends.
  7. In both cases, you’ll see a notification that the recording has been saved in the Files app.

Note that if your camera is already in use by another app, Local Capture records only audio.

How to choose a microphone for Local Capture

One of the more useful iPadOS 27 improvements is the ability to choose the input source used by an app or website. If I’m recording an interview or podcast, I’d generally choose a good external microphone instead of relying on the iPad’s built-in microphone.

To select a microphone:

  1. Open the app or website you’re using for the call.
  2. Open Control Center.
  3. Tap the button for the active app or browser at the top of Control Center.
  4. Tap Input.
  5. Select the microphone you want to use.

This is especially useful if you’re using an external USB microphone, headset, or another supported audio input. With a supported external USB microphone, iPadOS can also provide an input gain control to attenuate the incoming volume when starting Local Capture.

Can you use Voice Isolation with Local Capture?

Yes, but there’s an important distinction.

Voice Isolation can be used during the live session, but it isn’t applied to the Local Capture recording.

For a normal app audio session, you can:

  1. Open the video-conferencing app.
  2. Open Control Center.
  3. Tap the app or browser control at the top.
  4. Tap Voice Isolation.

Voice Isolation reduces background noise during the live call.

However, if your goal is the cleanest possible Local Capture file, plan to do noise reduction or other audio processing during editing.

Where are Local Capture recordings saved?

By default, Apple saves the recordings in the Downloads folder in the Files app.

To find a recording:

  1. Open the Files app.
  2. Tap Browse if necessary.
  3. Open Downloads.
  4. Look for your Local Capture recording.

The exact file location can be changed, so if you can’t find your recording in Downloads, check the Local Capture save location configured in Settings.

Change the Local Capture save location

iPadOS 27 lets you choose where Local Capture recordings should be saved.

Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Scroll down and select Local Capture.
  4. Tap Save Location.
  5. Browse to the folder where you want your recordings saved.
  6. Select the folder.
  7. Tap Open.

From then on, Local Capture uses the location you’ve selected instead of the default Downloads folder.

For example, if I were using Local Capture regularly for podcast interviews, I’d create a dedicated folder in Files, such as “Podcast Recordings,” and set that as my save location. That saves me from having to dig through Downloads every time I finish a recording.

How to share a Local Capture recording

After the recording has been saved:

  1. Open Files.
  2. Navigate to your Local Capture save location.
  3. Select the recording.
  4. Tap the Share button.
  5. Choose AirDrop, Messages, Mail, or another compatible sharing option.

Apple also notes that Local Capture recordings can be shared with other participants and combined with their recordings in post-production software such as Logic Pro or Final Cut Pro.

Can Local Capture record only audio?

Yes. If you don’t need a video recording, choose Audio Only when configuring Local Capture from Control Centre.

This is useful when:

  • You’re recording a podcast and only need audio.
  • You want to reduce storage requirements.
  • Your camera is already being used elsewhere.
  • You don’t need a video file for post-production.

Apple has also included a dedicated Audio Only toggle in Settings > General > Local Capture.

Use AirPods to Control Local Capture remotely

If you have supported AirPods or AirPods Pro, you can use them to remotely start and stop audio and video recording during a videoconference.

Simply press the AirPods stem to start and stop recording. This can be particularly useful when your iPad is positioned several feet away from you.

For example, if I’m recording an interview with the iPad on a tripod, I don’t necessarily want to reach over to the screen every time I need to start or stop recording.

Tips for getting better Local Capture recordings

Make your recordings shine with these pro tips:

  • Use a Good Microphone: The microphone has a bigger impact on perceived recording quality than many people expect.
  • Check Your Input Before Recording: Open Control Center and verify the input source before starting. This helps prevent accidentally recording with the wrong microphone.
  • Free Up Space: High-resolution recordings take space. Clear unused files before a long session.
  • Watch Your Input Gain: Avoid setting the microphone input unnecessarily high because distorted audio can be difficult to repair later.
  • Frame Your Shot: Place the iPad at eye level with proper lighting to improve video quality.

Troubleshooting Local Capture issues on iPad

Although Local Capture in iPadOS is effortless and quick to use, you may still encounter some issues. Here are some common issues users face, along with quick fixes.

Transform your iPad workflow with Local Capture

Local Capture turns your iPad into a mobile content creation studio. No more dependency on external apps or devices—record interviews, presentations, podcasts, or video logs effortlessly and professionally.

The biggest thing to remember is that Local Capture isn’t a conventional meeting recorder. It records your own high-quality audio and video locally, making it ideal for the double-ender workflow rather than for capturing everything in a video call.

Have you used Local Capture on your iPad? Share your experience or favourite tips in the comments!

mainEntity.name: How do I see parts and service history on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History. It will only appear if your iPhone has been repaired before.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to buy an iPhone with non-genuine parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Unknown label means Apple could not verify the part or repair status. The phone may still work, but you should understand what was repaired and consider that the Unknown part might affect trade-in value.

mainEntity.name: Can I reset parts and service history?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This information cannot be erased or changed.

mainEntity.name: Do third-party repairs affect warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Unauthorised repairs may void parts of your warranty.

mainEntity.name: Does service history affect resale value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iPhones with genuine parts usually sell for more.

mainEntity.name: Can AppleCare+ be used with unknown parts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple may require replacement with genuine parts before providing coverage; otherwise, the warranty may be void.

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't hide In-app purchases from your purchase history on an iPhone, but you can hide apps from your purchase list in the App Store. To learn how, check our guide on hiding App Store purchases.

mainEntity.name: How do I cancel an app purchase on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: To cancel an app purchase, go to Settings > tap on Apple ID > Subscription > select the subscription you want to cancel > tap on Cancel Subscription.

title.rendered: Blue Lock Farm codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Blue Lock Farm Codes on October 06, 2026

There’s no denying that Blue Lock Farm is one of the most unique games on Roblox. Taking inspiration from the popular Blue Lock anime, the title lets you collect characters and build your very own farm, with each player helping you generate Soccer Balls and Cash. These resources can be used to expand your farm and unlock rarer characters to level up your team. With the help codes, you can make progression much easier, as they give you free rewards. So, let’s take a look at all the active Blue Lock Farm codes you must redeem right now.

All working Blue Lock Farm codes

  • ADMINABUSE2: 1 Monster Ball and Traits (NEW)
  • BALLS: 1 Monster Ball, 1 Beach Ball, and 1 Supercharged Ball (NEW)
  • WEATHER: Redeem this code for 5 Grade Tokens and 1 Luck Potion
  • COMMUNITY: Redeem this code for 3 Cash Potions, 3 Luck Potions, and 3 Grade Speed Potions
  • TRAITS: Redeem this code for 25 Trait Tokens
  • ADMINABUSE: Redeem this code for 20 Trait Tokens, 20 Grade Tokens, and 1 Variant Token
  • POLISHER: Redeem this code for 1 Jackpot Token

As of now, these are the only active Blue Lock Farm codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired or unverified Blue Lock Farm codes

Currently, all available codes are valid and can be redeemed. Keep in mind that developers may remove them when new codes are issued, so it’s best to redeem them promptly.

How to redeem Blue Lock Farm codes

Knowing the active codes isn’t enough, gamers! You also need to know how to redeem them and claim your free rewards. Thankfully, the process only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Blue Lock Farm codes:

  1. Fire up Blue Lock Farm on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Shop button on the left side of the screen.
  4. Scroll to the bottom and find the Code box
  5. Paste a working code and click Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more Blue Lock Farm codes

Unfortunately, the developers don’t have a fixed release schedule for Blue Lock Farm codes. Most of the codes are dropped to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Blue Lock Farm Discord server for announcements.
  • Follow the game’s Roblox page for update notifications.
  • Bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated whenever new codes are released.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Soccer Zero codes, Sell Ores codes, and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

Why are my Blue Lock Farm codes not working?

Make sure you’ve entered the code exactly as shown in the list above. If the code still doesn’t work, it might’ve expired, or you’ve already redeemed the rewards.

What do Blue Lock Farm codes do?

Blue Lock Farm codes give players free rewards such as Trait Tokens, Grade Tokens, Cash, and other in-game items.

title.rendered: How to get Vampire Sprite in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Vampire Sprite is among the four different sprites introduced in Fortnite with the arrival of the Fortnitemares update. Among the current batch, it is one of the two Halloween-themed sprites, besides Spooky Dash Sprite. The other two new sprites include Deer Sprite and Dumpster Dive Sprite, the latter of which can even help you unlock Jimothy the Raccoon sidekick in Fortnite.

When it comes to variants, the Vampire Sprite is currently available in five different flavours, namely base, gold, cheat master, loot hacker, and bounty hunter. To get your hands on any one of these variants, you can follow the different methods mentioned below, ranging from using in-game items to befriending other players who already have this sprite.

Ways to get Vampire Sprite in Fortnite

1. Smash Halloween pumpkin chests

Pumpkin Chests are something new that Fortnite introduced in its October 1 update, which coincided with the kickoff of the month-long Fortnitemares event. This particular type of chest needs to be smashed to open and always gives a sprite to the player. The sprites this chest offers are mostly one of the aforementioned Halloween-inspired ones, making this item a solid way to hunt for a Vampire Sprite.

There are certain locations where these Pumpkin Chests usually spawn. However, it isn’t guaranteed that they will spawn in those locations in every match, as the appearance is more random than consistent. Some of the spots on the Fortnite map where you can find these chests are Freaky Fields, Nightmare Neighbourhood (especially Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria), Green Hills Zone, Lifty Lodge, and Stone Sanctum.

2. Go for the pink or golden cheat codes

Because it’s a Legendary-tier item, you are most likely to get a Vampire Sprite from golden cheat codes, aka Legendary Cheat Codes. But these are extremely rare and don’t spawn all that often. In that case, your next best bet is using as many pink cheat codes, aka Epic Cheat Codes, as you can. While they are geared towards offering Epic-tier sprites, they also have a small chance of offering a higher-tier sprite.

As a matter of fact, it becomes imperative for the player to scour the places with the most cheat codes on the Fortnite island. These key locations include Cluster Coast, Green Hill Zone, Heatwave Harbour, Reality’s Reign, and Shaken Sanctuary, all of which have a variety of different cheat codes.

3. Look for the blue chests

Rare Chests, which appear blue in colour, used to be the most common way of obtaining sprites in the previous season. But in Chapter 7 Season 4, these chests have become a secondary way of expanding your sprite collection. However, that doesn’t mean they don’t work at all; they still do.

To boost your chances of getting a Vampire Sprite, it’s still reasonable to open every blue chest that you come across on the map. Some of the most highly rated POIs for finding these special chests are Nightmare Neighbourhood, Stone Sanctum, and the three Pac-Man islands.

4. Ask a Vampire Sprite owner to help

If nothing else is working at the pace that you want it to, the recommended way is to find someone who already has a Vampire Sprite to share the same with you. You can find such like-minded players on Fortnite’s official Discord server.

Once you do connect with someone willing, you and him will have to enter two Fortnite Battle Royale matches together. In the first match, the other player should drop his sprite for you to pick and extract. In the successive match, do the same thing, but vice versa.

Afterwards, you can visit the Override tab and then the Sprites tab, from where you can recall the desired sprite using Sprite Dust. If you are falling short of this in-game commodity, you can use a corresponding Fortnite lobby hack to get some for free.

What Vampire Sprite does in Fortnite

When equipped, the Vampire Sprite boosts your health whenever you are dealing damage to an opponent. As a result, it emerges as a useful sprite option for those who play on the offensive and get involved in firefights frequently during a Fortnite match. That bit of regenerated health, given you manage to hit the target enough, can prove to be the difference between survival and elimination.

As you gain XP while having the Vampire Sprite equipped, the health buff it provides will also increase with each of the five upgrade levels. Hence, in the endgame stages, a fully maxed-out Vampire Sprite can significantly swing the match in your favour.

Wrapping up

Since Vampire Sprite is a Legendary-rarity item, it won’t be as commonplace as, say, the Morgana Sprite in Fortnite. However, given the Halloween theme of the ongoing event, there is a bigger chance of coming across such spook-oriented items. So, all in all, the Vampire Sprite should be relatively more obtainable than other Legendary Sprites in Fortnite.

Find out more:

  • How to get the Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite
  • Morgana Sprite in Fortnite: What it does and how to claim it
