title.rendered: How to Reduce Loud Sounds on your iPhone With iOS 27

content.rendered:
The iPhone has separate controls for softening loud sounds from its built-in speaker, setting a maximum speaker volume, and reducing headphone audio. Reduce Loud Sounds applies to the built-in speaker. It is a toggle, not a slider, and it is different from the setting that caps maximum volume. The names are easy to mix up, so use the control that matches the audio you want to change.

Turn on Reduce Loud Sounds

Open Settings > Sounds & Haptics. Under Built-In Speaker, turn on Reduce Loud Sounds. There is no level slider for this control; the switch enables the speaker setting.

This setting is for playback through the iPhone’s built-in speaker. It does not control headphones or AirPods, and Apple describes it as a way to soften loud speaker sounds. It does not set a chosen decibel level or a maximum volume. If you want a specific output cap, use Volume Limit instead.

Set a maximum speaker volume

Go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Built-In Speaker > Volume Limit. Turn on Limit Maximum Volume, then drag the slider to choose the highest speaker output you want.

Use this option when you want a cap that applies to speaker playback overall. You can use it alongside Reduce Loud Sounds; one softens loud sounds, and the other limits the maximum level. Set the slider where you want it, then play audio at your usual level to see whether the cap feels right. For a separate walkthrough, see how to set a limit on iPhone speaker volume.

Reduce loud audio in headphones

For headphones or AirPods, open Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Headphone Safety. Turn on Reduce Loud Audio, then adjust its slider to set the level at which headphone audio is reduced. This control is separate from the built-in speaker settings. If the option is missing, connect your headphones and check again; the headphone controls apply to supported headphones.

If you are trying to raise the volume of music that sounds unusually quiet, check our guide to fixing low music volume on iPhone or making AirPods louder.

Keep media and alert volume separate

The side volume buttons adjust media while audio is playing. When nothing is playing, they adjust ringer and alert volume. To prevent the buttons from changing alert volume, go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics and turn off Change with Buttons. You can still change media volume from Control Center or while a song or video is playing. If an alert is too loud, use the Ringtone and Alert Volume slider in Sounds & Haptics; Reduce Loud Sounds does not control notification volume.

Is Reduce Loud Sounds a headphone safety feature?

No. It applies to the iPhone’s built-in speaker. To reduce headphone audio, use Headphone Safety > Reduce Loud Audio. The speaker’s Volume Limit is a third, separate control for capping maximum output. If you hear low music volume after changing these settings, check the media slider first, then review your headphone or speaker limit.

keyPoints.title: What is Reduce Loud Sounds on iPhone?
keyPoints.explanation: Reduce Loud Sounds is a feature in iOS 26 that automatically compresses the dynamic range of audio played through your iPhone’s built-in speaker to prevent sudden loud noises.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Enabling Reduce Loud Sounds
keyPoints.explanation: Enabling this feature protects your hearing, offers a comfortable listening experience, maintains audio clarity, works automatically, and reduces stress on your iPhone's speakers.

keyPoints.title: How to Enable Reduce Loud Sounds
keyPoints.explanation: You can turn on Reduce Loud Sounds by going to Settings > Sounds & Haptics and toggling it on under the 'Built-In Speaker' section.

keyPoints.title: Alternative Control with Volume Limit
keyPoints.explanation: For more control or to save battery, you can set a maximum volume limit in Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Volume Limit, and combine it with Reduce Loud Sounds for optimal safety.

keyPoints.title: Final Thoughts on Managing iPhone Audio
keyPoints.explanation: With Reduce Loud Sounds, you can enjoy media without worries about loud spikes, and combining it with Volume Limit gives you complete control over your audio experience.

title.rendered: How to Send Photos Faster in iMessage on iPhone (iOS 27)

content.rendered:
When a connection is slow, a full-resolution photo can take a while to appear in a conversation. The Send Low Quality Photo Previews setting lets Messages send a smaller preview first, so the recipient can see what you sent while the original-resolution image arrives. It is useful when you want the other person to identify a photo before the full file finishes transferring. It does not make the network faster or promise that the original will arrive by a specific time.

Turn on photo previews

On your iPhone, open Settings > Apps > Messages. Turn on Send Low Quality Photo Previews.

That’s all you need to do. You can keep sending photos from Messages as usual; the setting changes how a preview is delivered over a slow connection. The label and location may differ in older iOS versions. The option is in the Messages section of Settings, not in the Photos app or the attachment menu for an individual photo.

What the recipient sees

Messages sends a smaller preview before the full-resolution image arrives. The preview gives the other person an early look at the photo, but it is not the same as sending only a low-resolution copy in normal conditions.

There is one important exception: when Low Data Mode is on, Apple says only the preview is sent. If the recipient needs the original-quality image, check that Low Data Mode is off before sending. Do not use this setting as a way to guarantee an exact delivery time; the full image still depends on the connection. You can turn the preview option off later in Settings > Apps > Messages if you do not want this behavior for future photos.

When to use the setting

Turn it on if you often send photos over a weak Wi-Fi or cellular connection and want the recipient to see a preview sooner. It can also help when you send a large photo and the other person only needs to know what it shows right away. It is less noticeable on a fast connection. If image quality matters more than an early preview, leave Low Data Mode off so the full-resolution photo can arrive. Check Low Data Mode for the network you are using, since Wi-Fi and cellular settings are managed separately.

For more ways to use Messages, browse our iMessage tips and tricks or learn how to filter and find conversations in Messages. You can also change an iMessage conversation background.

Does the setting permanently reduce photo quality?

Apple describes it as sending smaller previews before full-resolution images arrive. With Low Data Mode on, only the preview is sent. That is why the setting is useful for a slow connection, but you should check Low Data Mode when the other person needs the original-quality image. With Low Data Mode off, the smaller preview is sent first, and the full-resolution image follows.

  • I tried the new Screen Time in iOS 27
  • How to Change iMessage Background

aioseo_meta_data.description: Send iMessage photo previews sooner on a slow connection. Turn on Send Low Quality Photo Previews in iOS 27 and learn how Low Data Mode affects quality.

keyPoints.title: Why Apple Added the Low-Quality Preview Option
keyPoints.explanation: This feature helps speed up image sharing on weaker connections by sending a compressed preview first, with the full-resolution photo downloading later.

keyPoints.title: How to Enable Send Low-Quality Photo Previews in Messages
keyPoints.explanation: You can activate this setting quickly through the Messages section in Settings, enabling faster photo sharing on iOS 26.

keyPoints.title: What Happens When You Use It
keyPoints.explanation: Recipients initially see a pixelated version of the photo, which is replaced by the high-quality image once fully downloaded, with potential quality reduction on non-Apple devices.

keyPoints.title: When to Use This Feature
keyPoints.explanation: Ideal for traveling abroad, sending multiple photos quickly, in areas with poor network, or when you want to conserve cellular data.

keyPoints.title: Quick Photo Sharing, Without the Wait
keyPoints.explanation: Enabling this feature makes sharing photos faster and more reliable in low-bandwidth situations, ensuring your images arrive sooner in conversations.

title.rendered: How to Switch Back to the Classic Phone App Layout in iOS 27

content.rendered:
The iPhone Phone app offers two layouts. Unified puts Favorites, recent calls, and voicemails in a single Calls tab. Classic brings back separate tabs for Favorites, Recents, Contacts, Keypad, and Voicemail. You can switch between them whenever you like.

Classic vs. Unified: what changes

In the Unified layout, the Calls tab brings favorite contacts, recent calls, and voicemails into one chronological view. Up to eight Favorites can appear at the top; tap Show All if you have more. The screen saves tab switching if you mainly check recent calls, but it puts the old destinations inside one scrolling view.

Classic separates those destinations across the bottom of the screen. Favorites opens your saved contacts, Recents shows call history, Contacts opens your address book, Keypad lets you dial a number, and Voicemail lists saved messages. Switching layouts changes how the Phone app displays them; it does not remove your contacts, favorites, or call history. If you mostly need voicemail, see our guide to using voicemail on iPhone.

Switch to Classic

Open the Phone app and go to Calls if Unified is selected, or Recents if you are already in Classic. Tap the Filter button in the upper-right corner, then choose Classic at the top of the menu.

The Phone app switches to its familiar tab bar. Tap Favorites, Contacts, Keypad, or Voicemail to go directly to that section; Recents keeps your recent calls in a separate list. You can still manage your favorite contacts if you want to change who appears there.

Switch back to Unified

To return to the single Calls view, open Phone > Recents, tap Filter, and choose Unified. The next time you open the app, you will see the Calls tab instead of Recents.

In Unified, open Filter to show missed calls, voicemails, or calls from unknown callers. Choose Calls in the same menu to return to the full Unified view. Spam filtering options depend on your carrier. You can still open a contact card, start a call, or listen to voicemail from the combined Calls screen. For other useful iPhone controls, see our roundup of settings to change after updating to iOS 27.

Why can’t I find the layout switch?

Make sure you are on the Calls tab in Unified or the Recents tab in Classic. The Filter button appears in the upper-right corner of either view. The Classic and Unified options are available on iPhone with iOS 26 or later, so an iOS 27 update does not remove the choice. The layout switch changes the Phone app view; it does not move or erase your contact cards or voicemails.

keyPoints.title: iOS 26's New Phone App Design
keyPoints.explanation: The Phone app in iOS 26 has a unified design merging Favorites, Recents, and Voicemail into one Calls tab, offering a modern but potentially less intuitive layout.

keyPoints.title: Switching Back to the Classic Layout
keyPoints.explanation: Apple allows users to revert to the traditional Phone app layout by tapping the three-line menu and selecting 'Classic,' providing familiarity for long-time users.

keyPoints.title: Comparison of Layouts
keyPoints.explanation: The Classic layout is easier for long-time users with dedicated tabs, while the Unified layout offers a modern look with all calls and voicemails in one place, catering to different preferences.

keyPoints.title: User Choice and Flexibility
keyPoints.explanation: Apple provides users the option to switch between layouts easily, ensuring everyone can choose the interface that best suits their usage habits.

keyPoints.title: Final Thoughts on Layout Preferences
keyPoints.explanation: Whether you prefer the speed and familiarity of the Classic layout or the sleek, modern Unified design, the choice is yours, and switching is simple.

title.rendered: What Is the Preview App on iPhone and iPad? How to Use It in iOS 27

content.rendered:
Preview is Apple’s built-in app for opening and working with PDFs and images on iPhone and iPad. You can scan paper into a PDF, fill out a form, sign it, rearrange pages, crop an image, and share the finished file without installing a separate editor for everyday tasks.

The iPhone and iPad versions arrived with iOS 26 and iPadOS 26 and remain available in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. Here’s where to find your files and how to use Preview’s main tools.

Open a PDF or image

Open Preview and choose a file from Recents, Shared, or Browse. Browse lets you locate documents in Files and iCloud Drive. You can also tap a PDF attachment in Mail to open it in Preview.

Tap a document to read it. Pinch to zoom, swipe to move through pages, and tap the page count to open PDF thumbnails. Use Search to find a word or phrase, then move between matches. Preview saves changes to the file as you work. Open the Actions menu beside the filename to rename, duplicate, move, or export a copy.

Scan paper documents into a PDF

On the Preview start screen, tap Scan Documents and point your camera at the page. iPhone can capture pages automatically; tap Auto to switch to manual capture if you want to press the shutter yourself. Scan each page, then tap Done to save them together as one PDF.

Before saving, tap a page thumbnail to crop or rotate it and adjust the scan’s color. If you already have a PDF open, you can also insert scanned pages into it from the page thumbnails. For more ways to use your camera as a scanner, see our guide to scanning documents on iPhone and iPad.

Fill out and sign a PDF form

Open the form and tap AutoFill or the form-filling button. Tap a field and type, or choose an AutoFill suggestion above the keyboard. Suggestions can use details saved in your Contacts card, so check the information before sharing the completed form.

To add a signature, tap the Add button, choose Add Signature, sign with your finger, then place the signature in the right spot. On iPad, you can write with Apple Pencil. If the PDF has no fillable fields, add a text box instead. When you finish, save the file or export and share a copy.

Mark up a PDF or image

Preview’s Markup tools let you draw, add text or shapes, and place a signature on a PDF or image. To highlight, underline, or strike through text in a PDF, select the text and choose the annotation you need. On iPad, Apple Pencil is useful for handwritten notes or a quick mark on a document.

You can also select and copy text from a PDF, which is handy when you need to quote a line in an email or another document. If you only need to sign and send a form, follow our detailed guide to creating a signature and signing documents on iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Add, remove, and rearrange PDF pages

Open the PDF and tap its page count to show thumbnails. Touch and hold a thumbnail to insert a blank page, add a PDF or image from Files, scan pages into the document, or delete the selected page.

To change page order, touch and hold a thumbnail and drag it above or below another page. Use the More menu to rotate a page, and the Crop tool to trim the visible area. You can insert pages from another PDF or image, so you can combine files without recreating the document. These controls are useful when someone sends a scan in the wrong order or you need to remove an unnecessary page before sending the file.

Crop and edit images

Open an image and tap Crop to trim its edges. The More or Actions menu also lets you rotate or flip an image, change its size, or remove its background. Preview is useful for these quick edits; it is not a replacement for a full photo editor when you need detailed color correction or layers.

If you need to edit a PDF on a smaller screen, our guide explains how to edit PDFs on iPhone and iPad.

Lock, compress, export, and share files

To password-protect a PDF, open it, tap the Actions menu beside its filename, and choose Lock. Enter and confirm a password. If you want to keep an unlocked original, duplicate the PDF first; locking applies to the file you open.

To create a smaller or differently formatted copy, open the Actions menu and tap Export. Choose a supported format such as HEIC, JPEG, PDF, PNG, or TIFF. When available, use the file-size slider to adjust the exported copy. You can then share a copy through Mail or Messages, or collaborate on a file using Preview’s sharing options. When collaborating, choose whether invitees can make changes or only view the file. You can also copy the file to the clipboard or print it from the Actions menu.

What’s different from Preview on Mac?

The iPhone and iPad app is built around touch and mobile tasks. Its start screen separates recent files, shared documents, and locations you browse. It includes camera scanning, form filling, signatures, page management, PDF locking, export and compression, and basic image edits. iPad also supports Apple Pencil for handwriting and markup. The Mac app has a desktop layout and its own editing controls, so menus and some workflows differ between platforms. Preview on iPhone is handy for document fixes and quick crops; use a dedicated editor for more involved photo adjustments.

An older version of this guide said mobile Preview could not lock PDFs or compress and export files. Those limitations are out of date: the current iPhone app supports these tasks. If you do not see Preview after updating, search for it on your device before downloading another PDF app.

keyPoints.title: Preview's New Availability on iOS and iPadOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Apple has brought its powerful Mac app, Preview, to iPhones and iPads with iOS 26 and iPadOS 26, enabling users to view, edit, and annotate PDFs and images directly on mobile devices.

keyPoints.title: Capabilities of Preview on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: The app allows users to view, markup, sign, autofill forms, combine, rearrange, delete pages, and scan physical documents using the camera, making it a versatile tool for mobile productivity.

keyPoints.title: Differences Between Preview on Mac and iOS/iPadOS
keyPoints.explanation: While the mobile versions retain essential tools like markup and background removal, they lack features like color adjustments, PDF locking, and in-app screenshot capture, which are available on Mac.

keyPoints.title: Exclusive Features on iPhone and iPad Preview
keyPoints.explanation: New features include scanning physical documents with the camera and Apple Pencil support on iPad, offering a more natural writing experience and expanding creative possibilities.

keyPoints.title: Device Support and Final Thoughts on Preview in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: The pre-installed Preview app supports iPhones and iPads running iOS 26 and iPadOS 26, expected to become an essential tool for document handling, streamlining tasks without third-party apps.

title.rendered: How to Use the Reminders App on iPhone and iPad in iOS 27

content.rendered:
The Reminders app can do more than hold a basic to-do list. Use it to schedule tasks, get alerts when you arrive somewhere or message someone, share chores with family, and keep grocery items organized. This guide covers the everyday tools in Reminders on iPhone and iPad, including the Apple Intelligence features available on supported devices.

Some advanced features require updated Reminders in iCloud. Apple Intelligence also depends on your device, language, and region, so you may not see every option described below.

Turn on iCloud sync

If you want the same reminders on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac, sign in to the same Apple Account on each device and turn on Reminders in iCloud. Open Settings, tap your name > iCloud > See All, then turn on Reminders.

Open the Reminders app and look for your lists under the iCloud section. If you use another account, such as a work or school account, its reminders may appear separately and some iCloud features may not be available.

Create reminders on iPhone and iPad

The app is the best place to create a task when you already know which list it belongs in. You can add a short title and save it right away, or open the details screen to schedule it before you move on.

  1. Open Reminders and choose a list, such as Today or one under My Lists.
  2. Tap New Reminder.
  3. Type a short title. Add a note if the task needs context.
  4. Tap the details button to add a date, time, location, or other information.
  5. Tap Done to save the reminder.

To make a reminder while using another app, open the webpage, email, or note, tap Share, then choose Reminders. Select a list and save the link or selected text. On a supported Apple Intelligence device, Reminders may suggest action items from the text. Review each suggestion and tap Add beside the ones you want, or use Include All. The Share button and available options vary by app.

Calendar is useful when you want to choose a date from the calendar itself. Tap Add, choose Reminder, enter a title, then set a date and optional time. Choose a Reminders list if you do not want to use the default list, then tap Done. The item appears in Reminders too, and you can complete or edit it from either app.

Siri can add a task when your hands are busy. Say, “Remind me to pick up the parcel tomorrow at 4 p.m.” Siri adds it to your default list unless you name another list in the request. To change that default, go to Settings > Apps > Reminders > Default List.

You can also add the Reminders control to Control Center for quick capture from any screen. Open Control Center, tap Add a Control, find Reminders, and add it. On a supported iPhone, assign Reminders to the Action button in Settings > Action Button, then press and hold the button to create a task.

On an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone, you can type a natural-language request such as “Feed the cat every evening at 5” and let Reminders fill in the timing. Apple lists iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max, and iPhone 16 models or later, as supported for Apple Intelligence in iOS 27. Feature availability varies by language and region, and usage limits may apply. If you are trying to remember to return a call, you can also set a callback reminder from the Phone app.

Add dates, locations, and details

Tap a reminder, then tap its Details or info button to edit it. You can add a note or URL, set a date and time, flag the task, choose a priority, and attach an image or scanned document. This is also where you can set a location, a message trigger, an early alert, or a repeat schedule.

Choose a due date and time when you need a precise alert. If you set an all-day reminder without a time, change its alert time in Settings > Apps > Reminders > Today Notification. This replaces the older fixed-time instructions you may see in outdated guides.

For an alert when you arrive at or leave a place, turn on Location, choose a suggested place, or search for another address. Reminders needs Location Services and Precise Location access for this to work. A location reminder is useful for a task like “Pick up the dry cleaning” when you reach the shop, rather than at a time when you may be somewhere else.

Turn on When Messaging, tap Choose Person, and select a contact to see the reminder the next time you message them. This works well for a question or item you want to bring up in a particular conversation.

Use Early Reminder when you want a heads-up before the due time. Pick one of the suggested intervals or set a custom lead time, then keep the main due date as the deadline.

To add a visual reference, tap Add Image and choose a photo or scan a document. For example, attach a picture of a product label to a shopping task or a scan of paperwork you need to submit.

To make a task recur, set its date first, tap Repeat, and choose a schedule such as daily, weekly, or monthly. Reminders create the next occurrence after you complete the current one, so you do not need to add the same task again.

Choose Priority to mark an item Low, Medium, or High. A flag is another way to mark an important task; flagged items also appear in the Flagged Smart List. For an alarm-style alert, turn on Urgent in the reminder details. The alarm can sound even when Silent mode or Focus is on, but Urgent requires iCloud Reminders, permission for Reminders to use alarms, and the device that Find My uses as your location. If you have not set a date or time, an Urgent reminder defaults to the next hour.

Break large tasks into subtasks

Subtasks keep a project or errand from becoming one long reminder. For a grocery run, for example, make “Shop for the week” the main task and add separate items for produce, pantry supplies, and household needs.

To create one, open a list and swipe right on a reminder, then tap Indent. You can also drag a reminder onto another reminder to make it a subtask. Swipe right and tap Outdent to move it back to the main list. Completing a parent reminder also completes its subtasks; moving or deleting the parent moves or deletes them too.

Organize lists and sections

Tap Add List to create a list. Give it a name, choose a color and symbol, select Standard as the list type, and tap Done. Make separate lists for work, home, travel, or any other set of tasks you want to keep apart.

To change a list’s name, icon, color, or type later, open it, tap More > Show List Info, make your changes, and tap Done. A Standard list can become a Groceries list here. Smart Lists use filters instead of storing a separate set of reminders.

Sections let you divide one list into smaller groups, such as “Before the trip” and “At the airport.” Open the list, tap More > New Section, and name it. Tap a section name to rename it, or drag a section to change its position. Swipe left on a section to remove it; deleting a section also deletes the reminders in it. To see sections side by side, tap More > View as Columns, then drag reminders between columns.

To group related lists on the Reminders home screen, tap More > Edit Lists > Add Group, enter a group name, select the lists to include, and tap Done. You can also drag one list onto another to create a group. To reorganize lists later, return to Edit Lists and drag them into a different order or group.

Move a reminder to another list by opening its details, tapping List, and choosing the destination. To move several at once, open a list’s More menu, choose Select Reminders, select the items, and tap the move control. You can also drag a reminder between lists when both lists are visible.

Keep frequently used lists near the top by touching and holding one, then tapping Pin. You can pin up to nine lists. Drag pinned lists into the order that works for you.

Use Smart Lists, tags, and grocery lists

Tags help you find related tasks even when they live in different lists. Add a tag such as Work or Shopping while creating or editing a reminder. A tag is one word, but you can use a hyphen or underscore to join words, and you can add more than one tag to a reminder.

Tap a tag in the Tag Browser at the bottom of the Reminders screen to see matching reminders. You can select more than one tag and choose whether the list should match any or all of them. If a tag is no longer used, it may not appear in the browser.

To tag several reminders together, open a list, tap More > Select Reminders, choose the items, and tap Add Tag. Select an existing tag or create one, then save.

To remove a tag from one reminder, edit that reminder and delete the tag. To rename or delete a tag across your lists, touch and hold the tag in the Tag Browser and choose Rename Tag or Delete Tag. Deleting a tag also removes it from Smart Lists that use it.

Smart Lists automatically collect reminders from your other lists. The built-in options include Today for overdue and due-today items, Scheduled for dated reminders, All for every list, Flagged, Completed, Assigned to Me, Groceries, and Siri Suggestions. Tap More > Edit Lists to show or hide the default Smart Lists. To make a custom one, tap Add List, choose Smart List under List Type, then set filters such as tags, dates, location, flag, or priority. Choose whether a reminder needs to match all or any of the filters.

For groceries, create a new list and choose Groceries as its type, or open an existing list’s Show List Info screen and change List Type to Groceries. As you add items, Reminders sorts many of them into categories such as Produce or Dairy. You can move an item to another category, and Reminders can remember the correction.

If you shop or enter items in another language, go to Settings > Apps > Reminders > Add Language under Grocery Categorization. Choose Set Automatically or select the languages you use. For a deeper walkthrough, see how to create and organize a grocery list in Reminders.

Share lists and assign reminders

Open a list and tap the Share button to invite people through Messages, Mail, or another option. Everyone needs to be signed in to an Apple Account and have Reminders turned on in iCloud. After they accept, collaborators can add or edit reminders and mark items complete; you can also control whether participants can invite others.

To assign a task, create or edit a reminder in the shared list and type @ followed by a person’s name, or tap the person button and choose someone. Use the Assigned to Me Smart List to see tasks assigned to you.

If the shared list becomes noisy, tap Collaborate > Manage Shared List to change activity notifications. You can choose to get alerts when someone adds or completes an item. You can stop sharing from the same management screen. If you want to reuse a packing list or routine, save a Reminders list as a template instead of sharing an editable list.

Complete, sort, and delete reminders

Tap the circle next to a reminder to mark it complete. You can also mark a reminder complete from its notification or from a Reminders widget. Completed items are hidden from the regular list. To review finished tasks, open the Completed Smart List or open a list’s More menu and choose Show Completed. You can undo a completion by tapping the checked circle again.

To change the order of a list, touch and hold a reminder and drag it. For an automatic order, tap More > Sort By and choose due date, creation date, priority, or title. Sorting is not available in every Smart List, and a shared list’s new order is visible to its collaborators.

If you added a task by mistake, swipe left on it and tap Delete. You can select several reminders from a list’s More menu and delete them together. Deleted reminders go to Recently Deleted, where you can recover them for 30 days.

To remove completed tasks, open the completed items, tap Clear, and choose which completed reminders to clear. This is different from marking a task complete: clearing removes it from the list.

To delete a whole list, open it, tap More > Delete List, or swipe left on it from the home screen. Review the confirmation first, since deleting a list also removes its reminders. Deleted lists can be recovered from Recently Deleted for 30 days.

Reuse templates and capture tasks quickly

If you repeat the same routine, open its list, tap More > Save as Template, name it, then choose whether to include completed reminders. When you need another copy, tap More > Templates, choose the template, name the new list, and tap Create. Editing a template does not change lists you already made from it. You can share a template link; people download their own copy. When you share a template, you can choose whether to include dates, tags, and locations, while attached images are removed.

A Reminders widget gives you a quick look at a chosen list on the Home Screen or Lock Screen. Touch and hold the Home Screen background, tap Edit > Add Widget, and choose Reminders. To change the list shown, touch and hold the widget, tap Edit Widget, and select a list. Tap an item in the widget to complete it without opening the app.

For one-off tasks, Siri, the Share Sheet, and the Control Center Reminders button are faster than opening the app. Apple Intelligence can also suggest reminders from selected text in apps such as Safari, Notes, or Mail on supported devices. For medication schedules, use Health > Browse > Medications. Health can notify you when it is time to log a dose; those alerts are separate from Reminders lists. See our guide to setting medication reminders on iPhone and Apple Watch.

If the Reminders app badge does not show tasks due today, open Settings > Apps > Reminders and turn on Include Due Today. The badge then counts overdue items and reminders due today.

title.rendered: Best Apple Watch to buy in 2026: Series 12 vs Ultra 4 vs SE 3

content.rendered:
If you’re looking at Apple’s latest Apple Watch lineup and wondering which model actually makes sense to buy in 2026, you are in the right place. This year, Apple introduced a new Health Sensing System, a Readiness score, and Apple Intelligence-powered experiences. Paired with watchOS 27 and longer battery life, all the latest models are one-of-a-kind.

In this article, I’ll share which is the best Apple Watch to buy in 2026 so you can pick the right Apple Watch for your lifestyle, budget, and personal needs. Whether you’re an outdoor adventurer, a casual user, a fitness enthusiast, or buying a watch for your child, there’s a model for you.

How to choose which Apple Watch is perfect for you

Choosing an Apple Watch isn’t just about buying the newest model. I’d first look at how you actually plan to use it.

1. Find your purpose

  • Health and fitness: If health tracking is your priority, the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are the most compelling options, as they include Apple’s all-new health features.
  • Everyday use: For notifications, workouts, sleep tracking, calls, messages, and general smartwatch features, the Series 12 offers a more traditional Apple Watch design without the extra bulk of the Ultra.
  • Outdoor adventures: If you hike, run trails, dive, camp, or spend time away from cellular coverage, the Ultra 4 is built specifically for those situations.
  • Budget: If you want an Apple Watch without spending flagship money, the SE 3 is the entry point in Apple’s current lineup.
  • Premium/luxury: Series 12 is available in aluminum, titanium, and a new ceramic option, while Ultra 4 comes in natural and black titanium. Apple also offers Hermès versions.

2. Look at the features

  • Health Sensing System: Series 12 and Ultra 4 use new optical and electrical heart sensors with the S11 chip. It can measure heart rate every five seconds throughout the day, while HRV can be measured up to 24 times more often than before.
  • Design and build: Depending on whether you prefer a lightweight or durable build, consider aluminum, ceramic, or titanium models. Also, look for design aspects that suit your style. You may change Apple Watch bands for different looks. 
  • Size: Getting an Apple Watch suitable for your wrist size is important as well. An accurate fit ensures you can access the best possible health monitoring. 
  • Battery life: Consider it seriously if you plan to use your watch for extensive fitness tracking or notifications throughout the day. If I were choosing based purely on battery endurance, the Ultra 4 is the one.

3. Check compatibility

The current Apple Watch models require an iPhone. Apple says the Apple Watch Series 12, Ultra 4, and SE 3 require an iPhone 11 or later running iOS 27 or later. Moreover, all Apple Intelligence features, like Siri AI, require pairing with an iPhone 15 Pro or later.

That means I wouldn’t buy one of these watches if you’re still using an older iPhone that doesn’t meet those requirements. Always check Apple Watch and iPhone compatibility before buying. 

4. Set your budget

  • Mid-range: Models like the Apple Watch Series 12 provide a fine mix of good features and prices. 
  • Entry-level/first-time buyer: With its essential features, the Apple Watch SE 3 is less expensive. 
  • Premium budget: The Ultra 4 is designed for those willing to capitalize on top-quality specifications and durability. 

5. Think about who will use it

When selecting a model, consider the target users, from fitness enthusiasts to tech lovers and luxury seekers. So, consider who will be using the watch. For example, the SE 3 is excellent for kids, whereas Series 12 is for elderly users due to its simplicity and health monitoring features. 

What is the best Apple Watch to buy now?

After Apple’s September 2026 refresh, I’d divide the current lineup this way:

  • Best for demanding outdoor use: Apple Watch Ultra 4
  • Best for most people: Apple Watch Series 12
  • Best budget option: Apple Watch SE 3

The important thing is that there isn’t a single Apple Watch that makes sense for everyone. The Ultra 4 gives you the most extensive outdoor and battery capabilities, while the Series 12 delivers the latest mainstream health and smartwatch features in a more conventional design.

Best for demanding outdoor use: Apple Watch Ultra 4

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is Apple’s flagship sports and adventure watch for 2026.

Key specs

  • Case: 49mm titanium
  • Display: Always-On wide-angle OLED, up to 3,000 nits
  • Chip: S11
  • Battery: Up to 50 hours; up to 84 hours in Low Power Mode
  • Charging: 0–80% in about 45 minutes
  • Water resistance: 100 meters
  • Health: Health Sensing System, high-frequency heart-rate tracking, higher-frequency HRV, Readiness, ECG, Blood Oxygen, sleep tracking, sleep apnea notifications, sleep score, and Vitals
  • Connectivity: Precision dual-frequency GPS, cellular with 5G, satellite features
  • Price: Starts at $799

If you’re the type who works out actively, goes on camping trips, or just wants a rugged, powerful watch, grab the Ultra 4. Apple has rebuilt its health sensing around the new Health Sensing System, which enables more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements. The new Readiness feature is particularly interesting for people who train regularly.

It also gets the S11 chip, improved step tracking, new Audio Intelligence features, and substantially longer battery life, up to 50 hours compared with Ultra 3’s 42 hours. Moreover, the Max Extended Workout mode offers up to 45 hours of battery life for long outdoor runs, walks, and hikes.

I’d also pay attention to its GPS capabilities. Apple says the Ultra 4 has the most accurate on-device GPS, based on its testing against dual-frequency GPS sports watches. With its rugged titanium design, sapphire crystal, brighter 3,000-nit display, 100m water resistance, diving features, satellite connectivity, and Action button, it’s a premium watch.

If I mainly want sports, adventure, durability, and battery advantages, I’d choose Ultra 4.

Pros

  • Extremely long battery life
  • 100-meter water resistance
  • Designed for diving and demanding outdoor activities
  • Satellite communication capabilities
  • New Health Sensing System and advanced Readiness tracking
  • 5G connectivity
  • New Audio Intelligence features

Cons

  • Much more expensive than Series 12 and SE 3
  • Large 49mm case won’t suit everyone
  • Many outdoor-focused features may be unnecessary for casual users
  • Heavier and more noticeable on the wrist than the standard models

Who should buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4?

  • Trail runners and serious runners
  • Hikers and campers
  • Divers and water-sports enthusiasts
  • People who regularly travel to remote areas
  • Athletes who want extended workout battery life
  • Anyone who specifically needs the Ultra’s rugged design and satellite capabilities

If your idea of an adventure is mostly walking around the neighborhood, I’d save the money and look at the Series 12 instead.

Check out on Amazon

Note: Even though Apple has phased it out, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 still remains a capable option with its watchOS 27 support and can be quite economical compared to Ultra 4. You may find it in some selected retail stores, but you should ensure that you buy an original Apple Watch

Best for most people: Apple Watch Series 12

For the majority of buyers, the Apple Watch Series 12 is the model I’d look at first. It gives you the newest mainstream Apple Watch experience without the size and price of the Ultra 4.

Key specs

  • Case sizes: 42mm and 46mm
  • Materials: Aluminum, titanium, and ceramic
  • Display: Always-On Retina wide-angle OLED, up to 2,000 nits
  • Chip: S11
  • Battery: Up to 24 hours; up to 38 hours in Low Power Mode
  • Charging: 0–80% in about 30 minutes
  • Water resistance: 50 meters
  • Health: Health Sensing System, high-frequency heart-rate tracking, HRV, Readiness, ECG, Blood Oxygen, sleep tracking, sleep apnea notifications, sleep score, Vitals, wrist temperature sensing
  • Connectivity: GPS and cellular options, with 5G
  • Price: Starts at $399 (GPS) and $499 (GPS + Cellular).

The Series 12 is like the sweet spot for most Apple Watch users. I like that Apple has kept the familiar everyday design while adding new finishes, including a ceramic case option, alongside aluminum and titanium. The aluminum models also feature Ceramic Shield 2, which Apple says is 60% tougher than the previous Ion-X glass.

Under the hood, Series 12 gets the S11 chip and a new Health Sensing System, enabling more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements and the new Readiness feature. It also brings Precision L1 GPS, 5G connectivity, and up to 24 hours of battery life. The new single-tap gestures make it easier to interact with the watch without repeatedly touching the screen.

Another upgrade I find interesting is Audio Intelligence. Series 12 can use features such as Sound Recognition, Live Rewind, Siri Recap, and Shazam. The watch also supports Siri AI through watchOS 27, bringing personal context understanding and broader world knowledge to the wrist.

With new colors, premium case options, improved durability, smarter health tracking, and the latest S11 chip, Series 12 is a capable everyday Apple Watch without the larger size, pricier, and rugged focus of the Ultra 4. If you already have a Series 9 or earlier, it’s the perfect upgrade. You may trade it in and receive the Series 12 at a discount.

Pros

  • Balanced size and weight for all-day comfort
  • New Health Sensing System and Readiness Score
  • 5G and fast charging make it snappy for daily life 
  • Affordable entry to premium features, especially Audio Intelligence

Cons

  • Battery life is nowhere near Ultra 4
  • No 100-meter water resistance
  • Not designed specifically for extreme outdoor use
  • Premium titanium and ceramic versions can become expensive

Who should buy the Apple Watch Series 12?

  • Most everyday Apple Watch buyers
  • People who want the latest health features
  • Fitness enthusiasts
  • Runners who don’t need Ultra-level battery life
  • People who sleep with their Apple Watch
  • Users who want a lighter, more conventional Apple Watch design
  • Buyers who want premium case-material options without moving to the Ultra

If I were buying an Apple Watch primarily for everyday wear, health tracking, notifications, sleep, and workouts, this is the model I’d compare most closely with the SE 3 before spending more.

Check out on Amazon

Best budget-friendly: Apple Watch SE 3

The Apple Watch SE 3 remains Apple’s entry-level option. It doesn’t have the complete sensor package of the Series 12 or Ultra 4, but it still gives you many of the Apple Watch basics at a significantly lower price.

Key Specs

  • Case sizes: 40mm and 44mm
  • Case: Aluminum
  • Display: Always-On Retina OLED, up to 1,000 nits
  • Chip: S10
  • Battery: Up to 18 hours; up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode
  • Charging: Up to 8 hours of additional battery life from 15 minutes
  • Connectivity: GPS and cellular options, with 5G
  • Health: Heart-rate tracking, HRV, sleep tracking, sleep score, sleep apnea notifications, Vitals, wrist temperature sensing, cycle tracking
  • Price: Starts at $249 (GPS) and $299 (GPS + Cellular).

The Apple Watch SE 3 is the easiest choice if you want the Apple Watch experience without spending flagship money.

It keeps the familiar lightweight design with 40mm and 44mm aluminum cases, while adding an Always-On Retina display, S10 chip, and 5G connectivity. You also get useful gestures such as single- and double-tap and wrist flick, making everyday interactions quicker without constantly touching the screen.

For health and fitness, SE 3 covers all the essentials along with safety features such as Fall Detection and Crash Detection. However, it doesn’t include the ECG, Blood Oxygen, hypertension notifications, or the full set of heart-sensing features available on Apple’s higher-end models, making the sensor package simpler.

What I like most about SE 3 is that Apple hasn’t made it feel like a stripped-down smartwatch. It still gets watchOS 27, Apple Intelligence-powered Siri AI features, fast charging, and up to 18 hours of battery life. The cellular version also supports 5G, which makes it more useful when I leave my iPhone behind.

If I mainly need notifications, workouts, sleep tracking, safety features, and basic health monitoring, SE 3 gives me the core Apple Watch experience at a much lower starting price.

Pros

  • Lowest starting price in Apple’s current lineup
  • Modernized with S10 chip, always-on display, and gesture controls 
  • Health and safety upgrades over older SE models 
  • Lightweight and comfortable for everyday wear and sleep
  • Siri AI support

Cons

  • No ECG and Blood Oxygen feature
  • Fewer advanced health sensors
  • Shorter battery life
  • 1,000-nit display compared with Series 12 and Ultra 4
  • Not intended for serious outdoor athletes

Who should buy the Apple Watch SE 3?

  • First-time Apple Watch buyers or those upgrading from older SE models
  • People on a tighter budget
  • Parents looking for an Apple Watch for their children
  • Users who primarily want notifications, sleep data, and fitness tracking
  • People who don’t need ECG or advanced health sensing

If you’re buying your first Apple Watch and don’t care about the newest health features, the SE 3 is the model I’d start with.

Check out on Amazon

Which Apple Watch model should you buy?

All Apple Watches have similar basic features and quality standards. However, depending on your needs, you may choose the powerful Apple Watch Ultra 4 or the affordable Apple Watch Series 12. 

It’s okay if you want an Apple Watch but cannot afford it. The Apple Watch SE 3 is excellent since not everyone requires blood oxygen and ECG monitoring. 

If you’re looking for something premium, consider the Apple Watch Hermès edition. It offers the same functionality as the Series 12, along with exclusive bands and watch faces. Also, Apple announced the Hermès edition for the Ultra 4 model. 

Series 12 vs Ultra 4: What’s the real difference?

Both watches now share several important technologies, including the S11 chip, Health Sensing System, higher-frequency heart-rate and HRV measurements, Readiness, Audio Intelligence, and Siri AI.

The biggest differences are the physical design, battery, durability, GPS, water resistance, and outdoor features.

Which Apple Watch should you avoid in 2026?

I wouldn’t recommend buying a very old Apple Watch simply because it is cheap. Models several generations old can miss newer health features, have shorter remaining software support, weaker battery health, and compatibility limitations.

If you’re buying new in 2026, I’d avoid the following models:

  • Apple Watch Series 8 or older
  • Apple Watch Ultra (1st gen)
  • Apple Watch SE (2nd gen or earlier)

If you find a refurbished Apple Watch like Series 11 or Ultra 3 model at a substantial discount, check its battery health, warranty, software compatibility, and which health features it actually supports before buying.

Bottom line

Apple’s 2026 Apple Watch lineup is easier to understand than it might initially seem.

  • Choose Apple Watch Ultra 4 if you need long battery life, rugged construction, advanced GPS, diving capabilities, satellite communication, and extended outdoor workout tracking.
  • Choose Apple Watch Series 12 if you want the newest mainstream Apple Watch with Apple’s latest health-sensing technology, Readiness, advanced health tracking, and new Apple Intelligence features.
  • Choose Apple Watch SE 3 if you want the core Apple Watch experience while keeping the price down.

The biggest change this year is that Apple’s newest health features aren’t exclusive to the Ultra. The Series 12 and Ultra 4 both use the new Health Sensing System, giving mainstream users access to higher-frequency heart-rate and HRV measurements and Readiness.

For me, that makes the Series 12 particularly interesting because the decision is no longer simply about buying the most expensive Apple Watch to get Apple’s newest health technology. The Ultra 4 earns its premium through its rugged design, battery endurance, GPS, water resistance, and outdoor capabilities.

And if those features don’t matter to you, the SE 3 gives you a much cheaper way into the Apple Watch ecosystem.

The best Apple Watch is ultimately the one that matches how you actually use your wrist every day, not necessarily the one with the biggest case or longest list of specifications. So, which Apple Watch fits your lifestyle best?

About Ava Biswas

  • Ava is a die-hard Apple aficionado and loves testing the latest tech gadgets.
  • She is always on the lookout for issues Apple users are facing, finds solutions, and crafts troubleshooting guides.

Experience

When not typing, you can find her exploring the latest Apple releases or pondering new tech innovations.

title.rendered: How to get the Champion Focus FNCS skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
The Champion Focus skin has returned to Fortnite via the Item Shop, after first being introduced on September 20 as an unlockable reward. Along with it, there are several other FNCS cosmetics from this year and previous years that are currently up for grabs as well.

This particular Fortnite skin was so far only claimable by those who ranked high in the FNCS Cup 2026. However, it is now selling for 1,000 V-Bucks for a limited window that ends on September 30 at 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. This skin can also be purchased together with its associated back bling, pickaxe, emote, and wrap as part of the FNCS Global Championship 2026 Bundle, which is priced at 1,600 V-Bucks.

In this article, you can find all the steps involved in getting the Champion Focus skin from the Fortnite Shop and also check out the other cosmetics that have rolled out in the same promotion.

Steps to claim the Champion Focus skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the section named “FNCS” and select the desired skin.
  3. Finally, select and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

All FNCS cosmetics in Fortnite

Apart from the Champion Focus skin, the Champion Surf Witch skin, which was the reward for the 2025 counterpart of the FNCS event, is also available in the Shop right now. In addition, other cosmetic items from the 2025 and 2026 FNCS lineup are also live for Fortnite players to buy.

1. Champion Focus

Price: 1,000 V-Bucks
Also available with: FNCS Global Championship 2026 Bundle

2. Champion Surf Witch

Price: 1,000 V-Bucks

3. Focused Emblem

Price: 200 V-Bucks
Also available with: FNCS Global Championship 2026 Bundle

4. FNCS Scythe

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: FNCS Global Championship 2026 Bundle

5. The Axe Of Champions

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks

6. Surf Slasher

Price: 500 V-Bucks

7. Laser Scan

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: FNCS Global Championship 2026 Bundle

8. Champion’s Focus

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: FNCS Global Championship 2026 Bundle

9. Witch Champion

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

The Fortnite Override season has been quite productive as far as in-game cosmetics and collabs go. We have already seen big-name franchises such as Sonic the Hedgehog, Marvel Comics, and The Walking Dead appear in the Shop tab, with more major IPs to join the list over the course of Chapter 7 Season 4’s final month.

As Fortnitemares, the horror-themed annual event in Fortnite scheduled for October 1, draws close, the game’s community has been buzzing with predictions and speculations. Among the Fortnite collabs previously teased or confirmed are Five Nights at Freddy’s and Obsession, whereas leaks are also pointing to Child’s Play and It also entering the fray during the Halloween-spanning event. However, which of the latter partnerships turn out to be real is anyone’s guess right now.

FAQs

Can I get the Champion Focus FNCS skin for free?

Not anymore. It was available for free for high-performers in the FNCS Cup until September 20, but it is now only available in exchange for V-Bucks via the Item Shop.

How many FNCS skins are available in Fortnite?

There are two FNCS skins available for purchase, namely the Champion Focus skin, which came out in September 2026 and the Champion Surf Witch skin from September 2025.

Does the FNCS bundle also include the Champion Surf Witch skin?

No, the FNCS bundle that is in the Item Shop only comes with the Champion Focus skin and its related cosmetics.

title.rendered: iPhone Duo code leak points to five new StandBy views

content.rendered:
A September 28 post by leaker pdfu points to five unannounced StandBy views in development for iPhone Duo. The post says localization strings in the iOS 27.1 simulator revealed the names, and that some views ran in a current renderer. Apple has not announced these views or said they will ship.

The names in the post are Home Camera, Home Modular, Flow, Fade, and Snoopy. They appear to be additional options for the foldable phone’s StandBy mode, but the leak does not explain what each one will do.

Home Camera and Home Modular hint at smart-home controls

Home Camera appears to be designed around one or more camera feeds. Home Modular may arrange controls for smart-home devices. Those interpretations would fit an iPhone Duo propped up on a desk or counter, where the screen can stay visible while the phone is open or standing on its own. The post does not confirm the exact layout, compatible cameras, or which Home controls might appear.

Flow, Fade, and Snoopy are even less clear. Their names could refer to visual themes or different information layouts, but there is not enough in the leak to identify their features. Snoopy may recall the character screensaver on Apple TV; that resemblance is speculation, not a confirmed connection. The post also says an app called Rushmore, which was meant to host some of the views, was missing from the simulator build. That suggests the work may still be incomplete.

Here’s a deep dive into StandBy mode on iPhone Duo.

Rushmore, the app meant to host the redesigned faces, is missing from the iOS 27.1 simulator.

But its localization strings reveal unreported faces, and I got some new faces running in the current renderer. 🧵 pic.twitter.com/lDQHOy5R0e

— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 28, 2026

How the leak compares with Apple’s StandBy plans

Apple has already confirmed that iPhone Duo will get an expanded version of StandBy mode. It can turn the phone into a clock, photo frame, or widget display, and Apple says it can work even when the phone is not charging. Apple has also announced Calendar and Weather faces alongside the existing Clock and Modular faces, plus a refreshed Photos view in its iPhone Duo announcement.

The code leak may point to options beyond those Apple has described, although Home Modular could overlap with the announced Modular face. It is also possible that the strings refer to experiments rather than finished features. Localization labels can appear before an interface is ready, and features in a simulator build can change or disappear before release.

Apple says iPhone Duo will be available starting October 23, with preorders beginning October 16. The company has not confirmed whether any of these five leaked views will be ready for launch or arrive in a later iOS update.

excerpt.rendered: Five possible StandBy views for iPhone Duo have surfaced in an iOS 27.1 simulator, including camera and smart-home options. The leak is not an Apple announcement.

title.rendered: Apple’s OLED MacBook Pro could bring a touchscreen and Dynamic Island

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly preparing a major redesign of the high-end MacBook Pro, with an OLED display, touchscreen, and a Dynamic Island-style feature around the camera. The details come from Bloomberg’s latest report on Apple’s upcoming products. Apple has not announced the MacBook or confirmed when it will arrive.

The rumors have taken shape over several reports. Bloomberg first described a touchscreen MacBook Pro in October 2025, then reported in February 2026 that Apple was working on a Dynamic Island-style interface. The newer report adds OLED to the expected redesign and places it among products Apple may introduce around the end of this year.

OLED could be the most visible change

The rumored models would replace the mini-LED displays in current MacBook Pro models with OLED. OLED pixels light individually, so parts of the screen can switch off to show black while nearby pixels stay bright. That can produce deeper blacks and stronger contrast, especially when a screen shows dark scenes beside bright highlights.

Apple has not confirmed the panel, brightness, refresh rate, battery impact, or display sizes. The OLED MacBook Pro reports also describe a thinner design; there is no final hardware to judge yet.

Touch would add another way to use macOS

Bloomberg says Apple is changing macOS around touch. The reports do not identify which apps, gestures, or controls Apple would change, or say whether keyboard and trackpad behavior would shift. The screen would add direct touch input to a MacBook Pro, whose built-in display has remained non-touch while the iPhone and iPad use touch as a primary input method.

It could make quick on-screen actions easier, but the reports do not show how the interface will work in everyday use.

The notch may give way to a Dynamic Island

The redesign may also replace the current camera notch with a smaller hole-punch cutout. Bloomberg has reported that a Dynamic Island-style interface would sit at the top center of the screen, bringing alerts and other activity into the space around the camera. Apple has not shown a mockup, and it is unclear how the interface would adapt to Mac apps or a larger display.

A late-2026 launch is possible, not confirmed

The latest report places redesigned MacBook Pro models in Apple’s late-2026 product plans, while Bloomberg’s earlier reporting described a window that could extend into early 2027. That leaves room for a launch this year, but it does not confirm an October event or a shipping date. Apple has not announced the redesign, its name, final specifications, or pricing.

title.rendered: Apple releases iOS 27.0.1 with fixes for iPhone 18 Pro bugs

content.rendered:
Apple released iOS 27.0.1 on September 28, the first bug-fix update for iOS 27. The update fixes three issues, including a Face ID problem that could make the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max restart unexpectedly.

Apple lists build 24A446 for the update. Two of the fixes are specific to iPhone 18 Pro models; the third addresses a touchscreen problem without naming a particular iPhone.

What iOS 27.0.1 fixes

Apple’s notes list three changes:

  • iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max may unexpectedly restart when Face ID fails to authenticate.
  • A color artifact may appear in 2x photos taken at f/1.48 under certain lighting conditions on a small number of iPhone 18 Pro models.
  • Opening Notification Center and Control Center at the same time may leave the touchscreen unresponsive.

The release notes do not explain what causes the camera artifact or how often it appears. Apple also leaves the affected iPhone models unspecified for the Control Center and Notification Center issue.

Face ID restart bug gets a public fix

When Face ID failed to recognize the user, affected phones could restart. Apple had told 9to5Mac that it was preparing a software update after reports of the behavior, and iOS 27.0.1 now includes the fix. Apple’s release notes do not say whether the restart could happen in other situations or explain the underlying cause.

The camera fix is narrower. Apple specifies 2x photos, an f/1.48 aperture, certain lighting conditions, and a small number of iPhone 18 Pro devices. That description does not indicate a general camera-quality change or a problem with all 2x photos.

The update also addresses a touchscreen freeze

The remaining fix concerns opening Notification Center and Control Center together. Apple says this could leave the touchscreen unresponsive, but does not describe how long it lasted or identify the devices affected. The update notes do not mention new features; iOS 27.0.1 is focused on correcting these reported problems.

To install it, open Settings > General > Software Update on your iPhone. If you need help with the process, see our guide on how to update an iPhone to iOS 27. Apple also released iPadOS 27.0.1 on September 28, with its notes describing general bug fixes.

excerpt.rendered: iOS 27.0.1 fixes three reported bugs, including unexpected restarts on iPhone 18 Pro models when Face ID fails. The update is available now in Settings.

title.rendered: New shows and movies coming to Apple TV in October 2026

content.rendered:
Apple TV is going all in this October with a stacked lineup of new shows and movies. Whether you’re into thrillers, heartfelt dramas, wild adventures, or documentaries that make you think, there’s something worth adding to your watchlist.

It can be hard to keep up with everything dropping each month, so I’ve done the digging for you. Here’s your no-nonsense guide to all the official Apple TV releases in October 2026, plus a quick peek at what’s coming up next.

Apple TV shows and movies releasing in October 2026 

Are you missing new Apple TV content? No more! Dive into the October lineup, featuring popular genres like comedy, drama, thriller, and even a documentary for TV geeks. Get ready to fill your popcorn bucket soon!

1. The Last First: Winter K2 

  • Cast: Nirmal Purja (Nims), Muhammad Ali Sadpara, Sajid Sadpara, John Snorri Sigurjónsson.
  • Director: Amir Bar-Lev
  • Genre: Documentary, Adventure
  • Release date: October 2, 2026

If you are waiting for Tenzing, here’s another tense, emotional mountaineering documentary. The Last First: Winter K2 takes you into the heart of the 2021 race to achieve the first-ever winter ascent of the world’s second-highest mountain.

What begins as a story of extraordinary courage and endurance gradually becomes an intimate look at ambition, ego, money, power, and the price of glory. I am excited to watch the spectacular mountain and the real drama that lies in the people trying to conquer it.

Check out on Apple TV 

2. The Sisters Grimm Season 2 

  • Cast: Ariel Winter, Leah Newman, Laraine Newman, and more
  • Showrunner: Amy Higgins
  • Genre: Animation, Fantasy
  • Release date: October 2, 2026

Sabrina and Daphne Grimm are back on Apple TV with The Sisters Grimm Season 2. Set one year after their parents’ mysterious disappearance, this season is focused on their further discoveries of the secrets of Ferryport Landing.

Season 2 promises another adventure-filled chapter for the Grimm sisters as they investigate the secrets surrounding their family and their unusual new home.

Check out on Apple TV

3. Small Prophets 

  • Cast: Pearce Quigley, Sir Michael Palin, Mackenzie Crook, and more
  • Creator: Mackenzie Crook
  • Genre: Comedy
  • Release date: October 7, 2026

Get ready for a hilarious comedy, Small Prophets, which follows Michael Sleep, a man whose life has been stuck in place since his girlfriend Clea vanished seven years ago.

When his father gives him an unusual recipe, Michael attempts to create magical spirits that can supposedly predict the future. I am looking forward to a great mix of comedy, magical realism, friendship, and mystery.

Check out on Apple TV 

4. Matchbox The Movie 

  • Cast: John Cena, Jessica Biel, Sam Richardson, and many more
  • Director: Sam Hargrave
  • Genre: Action, Comedy
  • Release Date: October 9, 2026

Matchbox: The Movie feels like a mix of Fast & Furious energy with a classic “friends reunited” story at its core. The story follows a group of childhood friends whose lives are thrown into chaos when their long-lost leader, Sean, suddenly returns. 

What starts as a reunion quickly spirals into a high-stakes chase across countries. There are explosive car chases, global locations, and intense action sequences, but underneath all that, it’s really about friendship, trust, and unfinished pasts.  

Check out on Apple TV 

5. Tenzing 

  • Cast: Genden Phuntsok, Tom Hiddleston, Willem Dafoe, Caitríona Balfe, and many more 
  • Director: Jennifer Peedom 
  • Genre: Drama, Adventure 
  • Release Date: October 16, 2026 

Tenzing tells the inspiring true story of Tenzing Norgay, the Nepalese-Indian mountaineer, aka Sherpa, who made history by becoming one of the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953.  

The film does not just revolve around the climb, but highlights Tenzing’s bravery, perseverance and all the sacrifices required for accomplishing one of the most difficult things ever done by humans. If you enjoy true stories about overcoming impossible odds, this is one to add to your watchlist. 

Check out on Apple TV 

6. Where’s Wanda? Season 2 

  • Cast: Heike Makatsch, Axel Stein, Lea Drinda, Leo Simon, and many more  
  • Director: Tobi Baumann, Christian Ditter  
  • Genre: Drama, Comedy 
  • Release Date: October 21, 2026  

When the Klatt family thought that things were finally settling down, once again things went out of control for them. In Where’s Wanda? Season 2, Wanda becomes a suspect in a murder case, and her family once again finds themselves in the midst of chaos and investigations.  

Packed with dark humor, unexpected twists, and plenty of family drama, I am waiting to see the new mystery unfold while laughing along the way. 

Check out on Apple TV 

7. Nocturne 

  • Cast: Liev Schreiber, Zazie Beetz, Stephen Graham, and more 
  • Director: Tim Van Patten
  • Genre: Crime, Thriller
  • Release Date: October 30, 2026  

Nocturne is a gripping crime thriller that starts off with an unexpected turn of events. A victim believed to be dead in a serial killing suddenly reappears, completely disrupting the whole investigation.  

The show then follows how a detective and an FBI agent uncover the truth and hunt down the ruthless criminal. If you enjoy dark mysteries, clever cat-and-mouse games, and suspense that keeps you guessing until the end, Nocturne looks like one to watch. 

Check out on Apple TV 

What’s coming to Apple TV after October 2026 

Apple isn’t slowing down in October and beyond. Here are a few titles already making waves:

1. Stick Season 2 

  • Cast: Owen Wilson, Peter Dager, Marc Maron, Rhea Seehorn, and more.
  • Created by: Jason Keller
  • Genre: Sports, Comedy
  • Release date: November 4, 2026

After finding an unlikely second chance through golf, Pryce Cahill is back, and this time, the stakes are bigger. Stick Season 2 continues the heartfelt sports comedy beyond golf and into ambition, friendship, and family.

The new season promises more laughs, emotional turns, and new characters as Pryce and Santi face the next stage of their journey.

Check out on Apple TV

2. 12 12 12 

  • Cast: Anthony Mackie, Jamie Dornan, Jack Kesy, and more
  • Director: Kari Skogland
  • Genre: Crime, Action
  • Release date: November 13, 2026

At the heart of 12 12 12 is an ambitious bank robbery targeting a vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich. The story follows a disgraced FBI agent and an American career criminal as they get involved in a cat-and-mouse chase game.

I am excited to watch this show because of its storytelling structure. Three timelines are covered within each episode: 12 months that go into planning the robbery, 12 hours of the robbery itself, and 12 days after that.

Check out on Apple TV

3. Being Heumann 

  • Cast: Ruth Madeley, Mark Ruffalo, Dylan O’Brien, Madeline Delp, and more
  • Director: Siân Heder  
  • Genre: Drama, Comedy
  • Release Date: November 13, 2026 

Another interesting true story set for release in 2026 on Apple TV is Being Heumann. It is about Judy Heumann, one of the most influential disability rights activists in American history.  

In 1977, together with hundreds of other protesters, she occupied a federal building demanding equal rights and accessibility to people with disabilities. It’s a powerful, uplifting film that shows how one person’s determination can spark a movement and change millions of lives. 

Check out on Apple TV 

4. Way of Warrior Kid

  • Cast: Chris Pratt, Jude Hill, Linda Cardellini, and many more
  • Director: McG
  • Genre: Action, Drama
  • Release Date: November 25, 2026

Way of the Warrior Kid is based on the bestselling book by Jocko Willink. You will get a story of Marc, an introverted 11-year-old boy who lacks self-confidence, has trouble at school, and even with physical activities. It’s designed to inspire younger audiences while still hitting adults with a strong message about discipline and personal growth.

Check out on Apple

5. Bad Monkey Season 2

  • Cast: Vince Vaughn, Natalie Martinez, John Malkovich, and more
  • Director: Marcos Siega, Colin Bucksey, and more
  • Genre: Comedy, Drama
  • Release date: December 2, 2026

Andrew Yancy is back in the Florida Keys, and somehow his life is about to get even more complicated. After the wildly eccentric mystery of Season 1, Bad Monkey Season 2 brings an entirely new case. This time, Yancy witnesses the murder of Florida’s finest fixer and gets pulled into an investigation.

I am excited about Season 2 because it’s an original story rather than a direct adaptation of another Carl Hiaasen novel. So, get ready for sun-soaked Florida, eccentric criminals, dark comedy, bizarre situations, and Vince Vaughn’s effortless sarcasm at the center of it all.

Check out on Apple TV

6. The Wanted Man 

  • Cast: Hugh Laurie, Thandiwe Newton, Fionn Whitehead, and more
  • Director: Jakob Verbruggen
  • Genre: Crime, Thriller
  • Release date: January 6, 2027

Apple TV’s upcoming crime thriller The Wanted Man shows a powerful organized crime boss whose 20-year reign comes crashing down after a betrayal within his own criminal empire.

Sent to the notorious Staplehurst prison, Felix must survive behind bars while plotting his escape, seeking revenge and fighting to reclaim control of his criminal empire.

Check out on Apple TV

Final take: Must-watch Apple TV releases this October 

Apple TV is clearly on a roll. Whether you’re up for a globe-trotting docuseries, a heartfelt thriller, or a sci-fi robot with emotional baggage, October 2026 is loaded with good stuff.

So gra b your snacks, make room in your watch queue, and don’t forget to explore the immersive Vision Pro experience if you’re lucky enough to own one.

Want to boost your Apple TV setup? Check out the best Apple TV 4K accessories to take your binge nights to the next level.

  • Top 7 shows to watch after Stranger Things
  • How to watch a Formula 1 race on Apple TV
  • Top 6 movies that actually capture that same feeling

title.rendered: Best Claude connectors in 2026: 13 useful app connections

content.rendered:
Claude connectors help most when they cut the shuffling between your inbox, Drive, Slack, and task board. Start with Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, then add a project or design app only if Claude needs that context too.

Anthropic now groups Skills, Connectors, and Plugins under Customize. For app access, choose Connectors. Each listing shows what Claude can read or change, so check it before connecting an account.

How to install and use a Claude connector

  1. Open Customize, choose Connectors, then click + and Browse connectors.
  2. Choose a service, review its capabilities, click Connect, and sign in to that account.
  3. In a chat, open + > Connectors and turn on the service you want to use.

Claude may suggest a connected app when it fits your request, but you can turn connectors on or off for each chat. Claude only gets the access your account already has. Team and Enterprise users may need an owner to enable a connector first, and some services let admins restrict actions such as sending messages or editing files. See Claude’s connector setup guide if your menu looks different.

Claude connectors for email, files, and calendars

If most of your work is in Google or Microsoft apps, connect that account first. Google’s three Workspace connectors can read data and take supported actions; Claude asks before acting by default. Gmail can see attachment details, but not attachment contents. Anthropic’s Google Workspace connector guide lists the available actions and limits.

1. Google Drive for searching and working with files

Google Drive can search and read Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDFs, and Office files. Ask Claude to compare two spreadsheets, find a decision in your notes, or save a file it created to Drive. The connector can also make supported file changes when your account allows them. Browse the Google Drive connector.

If you also use ChatGPT, its Google Drive integration can open and edit supported files beside the chat.

2. Gmail for finding email and drafting replies

Gmail is useful when you remember the subject of a conversation but not which message has the detail you need. Ask Claude to find the latest emails about a vendor quote, summarize the thread, or draft a reply. See the Gmail connector.

3. Google Calendar for finding a time that works

Calendar can check your availability, compare schedules, and create or update events. Try: Find three 30-minute slots next week when Maya and I are both free. See the Google Calendar connector.

4. Microsoft 365 for Outlook, Teams, and company files

One Microsoft 365 connection can search work content in SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, and Teams. Use it to find a project document and pull in the latest team discussion. You need a work or school account tied to Microsoft Entra. Personal Outlook.com, Hotmail, and Live accounts are not supported, and an admin must set up the connection for your organization. Admins also control which write actions are available. Check the Microsoft 365 connector before connecting a work account.

Connectors for conversations, notes, and projects

5. Slack for decisions buried in channels

Slack can search messages, threads, channels, files, and users. Ask it to find what the team decided about a launch date, then draft a short update for the channel. It can also send messages and create Slack canvases, so review the result before it goes out. Browse the Slack connector.

6. Notion for searching a team wiki

If your plans and meeting notes live in Notion, Claude can find a decision, update a page, or create a new one from a conversation. It can also create and update databases. See the Notion connector.

7. Asana for managing tasks and projects

Asana works well if your team tracks projects there. Claude can find tasks, summarize project status, and create or update assignments. Its interactive board can also appear in the conversation, so you can review tasks without switching apps. Try: Show me the overdue tasks in the product launch project. See the Asana connector.

8. Linear for issues and development work

Use Linear if your team tracks product or engineering work there. Claude can search issues, create or update tickets, check project progress, and review cycle work. It is a better fit than Asana if your day revolves around bug reports and development tasks. Browse the Linear connector.

9. Atlassian MCP for Jira and Confluence

Atlassian MCP connects Claude to Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Loom, and other Atlassian tools using your existing permissions. Ask it to find the project decision in Confluence and the open Jira issues tied to it. Admin settings control which changes Claude can make, so this is best for teams that already use Atlassian. See the Atlassian MCP connector.

Connectors for design and specialist work

10. Canva for creating and editing designs

Canva can search your designs, create new ones, fill templates, and export finished files. Use it when you want Claude to turn a campaign brief into a social post or presentation you can keep editing in Canva. Its interactive editor can open directly in a Claude conversation. Browse the Canva connector.

11. Figma for turning design context into code

Figma is a specialist pick for product designers and developers. Claude can inspect selected frames and components, use that context to draft code that matches your design system, or create a flowchart in FigJam. Figma also supports an interactive design view in Claude. See the Figma connector.

12. HubSpot for customer and sales context

HubSpot gives Claude access to CRM records such as contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and campaigns. Use it to prepare for a sales call, summarize open deals, or review campaign performance. It can update CRM records too, so connect it only if your work already runs through HubSpot. Browse the HubSpot connector.

13. GitHub for understanding a codebase

GitHub works differently from the directory connectors. You can add selected files and folders from a repository to a chat or Project, then ask Claude to explain a feature or an unfamiliar codebase. It does not pull in commit history, pull requests, or other repository metadata. Private repositories may need approval from an organization admin. Read the GitHub integration guide.

Which Claude connector should you connect first?

Choose the app where you spend the most time searching. For Google users, start with Drive, Gmail, or Calendar. For a Microsoft workplace, connect Microsoft 365. Then add Slack, Notion, or the project tool your team already uses. You probably do not need both Asana and Linear, or separate Teams and SharePoint connectors on top of Microsoft 365.

Avoid turning on every tool in every chat. If you keep 10 or more connectors active, Claude’s Tool access setting can switch to On demand to give the conversation more room. For longer jobs, connected apps also work in Cowork; Claude’s chat and Cowork experiences are merging. Mac users who want Claude to search local clipboard history can also try Paste MCP.
