title.rendered: How to get the Madison Beer skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
After strong anticipation for weeks, Madison Beer is finally out in the Fortnite Item Shop as an in-game outfit, alongside a bunch of other cosmetics themed around her. The American singer made her debut in the game on September 25 and, in doing so, joined a growing list of musicians—ranging from Olivia Rodrigo to Lil Wayne—who have been added to Fortnite’s skins catalog this year.

There are two Madison Beer skins available for purchase right now, both selling at 1,500 V-Bucks. These skins and other related cosmetics are available until October 4, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. There is also a Madison Beer Bundle, which includes both skins and other themed items, and is worth 3,400 V-Bucks.

Steps to get the Madison Beer skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll to the “Madison Beer” section and select your desired skin.
  3. At last, press and hold the “Purchase” button to complete the transaction.

All Madison Beer cosmetics in Fortnite

There are a total of 16 unique Madison Beer-centric items that have recently been added to the game. Among these, 12 are available with the Madison Beer Bundle, whereas the 15 are available to be bought individually from the Shop. Here’s the entire lineup, including all skins, pickaxes, back blings, and more.

1. Make You Mine Madison

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Also includes: Madison’s OG Pickaxe
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

2. Satin Angel Madison

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Also includes: Madison’s Angel Wings
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

3. Madison’s Angel Wings (back bling)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle, Satin Angel Madison skin

4. Mookie & Maple Plushies (back bling)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

5. Madison’s OG Pickaxe

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle, Make You Mine Madison skin

6. Madison’s Mic (back bling and pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

7. Bittersweet (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

8. Yes Baby (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

9. Mine (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

10. 15 MINUTES (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

11. Madison’s Glam Wrap (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

12. Yes Baby (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

13. Bittersweet (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Madison Beer Bundle

14. Complexity (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

15. Make You Mine (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks

16. Rooftop Madison (loading screen)

Exclusively available with: Madison Beer Bundle

Musicians galore in Fortnite in 2026

This year has been quite an eventful one for Fortnite players who are also followers of some of the biggest names in the music industry. Throughout 2026, there have been various popular singers and rappers who have been incorporated into the game either as cosmetics or as the star attraction of Fortnite Festival—the online title’s music-oriented mode.

Among the musicians who have been introduced in Fortnite so far this year are Chappell Roan, Laufey, EsDeeKid, Olivia Rodrigo, Addison Rae, Lil Tecca, Lil Wayne, and Madison Beer. Apart from real-life personalities, this list also includes virtual singing sensations such as Kizuna AI, Hoshimachi Suisei, and Ironmouse.

Keeping the variety and abundance of the past several months in mind, it will be interesting to see how Fortnite keeps the momentum going with further additions through the remaining year.

title.rendered: All Exotic Weapons in Fortnite and how to get them

content.rendered:
Struggling to secure that Victory Royale? Well, it might be time to get your hands on Exotic Weapons in Fortnite. For those who don’t know, Exotic Weapons are a special rarity that comes with unique abilities and buffs. When used correctly, these weapons can give you a serious advantage and help you decimate the battlefield.

There’s no shortage of variety when it comes to Exotic Weapons, as we have shotguns, assault rifles, and more. So, let’s take a look at all the Exotic Weapons in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 and exactly how you can obtain them without breaking a sweat.

Complete list of all Exotic Weapons in Fortnite

There are currently five Exotic Weapons in Fortnite Chapter 4 Season 7, and it’s likely that more will be added in future updates. All five are designed specifically for close-quarters combat, which makes them ideal for taking down any enemy that’s within a short range. Let’s take a closer look at each weapon and break down its stats as well

1. Overpowered Pump Shotgun

The Overpowered Gun is a solid choice for taking down enemies at close range. It comes with a unique perk that increases the weapon’s damage with every successful hit, which makes each consecutive shot even more deadly. However, the damage boost will reset if you equip another weapon or fail to deal damage.

2. Accelerant Drum Gun

The Accelerant Drum Gun boosts your movement speed and fire rate, allowing you to stay mobile while keeping pressure on your opponents. This makes it a great pick for getting out of tricky situations without having to stop dealing damage.

3. Balloon Popper Assault Rifle

The Balloon Popper Assault Rifle isn’t just useful for dealing damage. Its unique perk causes the first bullet, as well as every few bullets afterward, to trigger an explosion that grants all players a balloon within the affected area. It’s a chaotic and fun weapon.

4. Overclocked 8-Bit Shotgun

The Overclocked 8-Bit Shotgun can do more than just take down enemies, as it can also restore your health. The more damage you deal to an opponent with the weapon, the more health you recover, which makes it a useful option for staying in the fight longer.

5. Rebecca’s Guns

The Fortnite x Cyberpunk: Edgerunners crossover has also brought in Rebecca’s Guns, and they’re as powerful as you’d expect. This Exotic weapon lets you dual-wield an SMG and an Assault Rifle, which gives you two options to unleash a serious amount of damage on your opponents.

How to get all Exotic Weapons in Fortnite?

So, the next obvious question is: how do you get exotic weapons in Fortnite? Unfortunately, there’s no guaranteed way of obtaining them. Obtaining them comes down to luck, but there are a few locations you can hit to improve your chances of finding these rare weapons

The first location you should check out is the Stone Sanctum Vault. There’s a Rare Chest inside that has a chance of dropping an Exotic Weapon. You can also head over to the Mega Maze Vault, which also contains Rare Chests that can reward you with the weapons. Basically, you’ll want to visit as many Vaults as possible and open every Rare Chest you come across to increase your chances of finding an Exotic Weapon.

Another way to obtain an Exotic Weapon is by heading to Heatwave Harbor and completing the Duck Race Minigame.

title.rendered: Morgana Sprite in Fortnite: What it does and how to claim it

content.rendered:
The Fortnite x Persona 5 Royal collab has finally landed and, with it, the Morgana Sprite has also arrived in the game. It makes Persona the fifth video game franchise to get its own sprite in Fortnite, after IPs such as Sonic the Hedgehog, Mega Man, Crash Bandicoot, and Pac-Man.

For the past few weeks, Fortnite has been increasingly teasing the onset of its collab with Persona 5 Royal, the highly popular JRPG title, with protagonist Joker headlining the discussion. On September 24, the game drip-fed its first bit of Persona 5 Royal content as the Morgana Sprite rolled out for everyone. Below, you can learn everything about what it does and how you can get your hands on it.

Morgana Sprite: Ability and variants

The Morgana Sprite, when equipped, amplifies the effect of consuming healing items. In other words, it gives your player character more health or shield when you use such an item. This particular boost can prove very beneficial in the very early game, when you are yet to find enough health and shield consumables.

As you level up Morgana Sprite, the extra health you gain from health and shield consumables further increases. Towards the final stages of a Fortnite match, this boost can help you spend more time focusing on locating the remaining opponents rather than looking for more consumables.

How to get Morgana Sprite in Fortnite

There are a few different approaches you can take for getting your hands on Morgana Sprite. These include exploring the map for certain objects and connecting with other players to assist with the objective.

1. Use Cheat Codes to find Morgana Sprite

Morgana Sprite is an Epic-tier item, and there are several Epic Cheat Codes scattered throughout the Fortnite map, so it shouldn’t be that hard to claim one. While Epic and Legendary Cheat Codes have the best chances of providing this sprite, the Rare Cheat Codes can also do the job, although it’s not as likely.

When looking for cheat codes, it’s best to target the locations that house the most number of such items. Among the places in Battle Royale mode that fit this criterion are Heatwave Harbor, Cluster Coast, Sunken Shores, and Shaken Sanctuary.

Cheat codes can often be in the most unusual places, such as the roof of a house. As a result, some players resort to using a Cheat Code Locator to track their precise location. You can either get some of these for free by using Fortnite Lobby Hacks or purchase one from any Sprite Extraction Site using Sprite Dust.

2. Search high-tier chests for Morgana Sprite

Although cheat codes are the main way to obtain sprites in Fortnite Override, they can be obtained from chests as well. Since regular chests don’t offer much besides weapon loot, you should keep an eye out for Rare Chests or higher-tier chests in order to maximize your chances of getting the Morgana Sprite using this approach.

To open as many rare-tier chests as you can in a single match, covering the areas most densely populated with these objects first is the recommended strategy. Such locations on the Battle Royale map are The Battlewoods, Stone Sanctum, Cluster Coast, the Pac-Man islands, and the maze northeast of Sunken Shores.

3. Take help from a friend

If ransacking chests and hunting for cheat codes is something you don’t want to indulge in, you can fast-track your way to a Morgana Sprite by taking help from another player. You can visit the official Fortnite Discord and find a Morgana Sprite owner willing to help with this.

Once you do that, you need to join at least two Battle Royale matches with him. In the first one, make sure to collect the desired dropped sprite and extract it. Doing this will index that sprite into your collection for good. For the next match, you have to simply equip the newly claimed sprite and return it to its original owner.

Afterward, you can go to the Override tab in Fortnite and, under the Sprites section, recall the Morgana Sprite in exchange for some Sprite Dust. If you are running short on this commodity, you may use the aforementioned Lobby Hacks or admin panel codes, such as “DustySprites”, to get some for free.

Wrapping up

Morgana Sprite has a straightforward but quite useful benefit associated with it. Thanks to this, players who equip it should finally be able to use more of their inventory space to carry weapons instead of consumables. Further, it should save some time that would otherwise be used to scour for additional health and shield items.

Apart from the Morgana Sprite, the Bounty Hunter sprite variant was also introduced in Fortnite last Thursday. This particular type of sprite makes it possible for players to get sprites after eliminating an opponent, regardless of whether the latter was carrying sprites or not. Moreover, the addition of Bounty Hunter sprites also increased the number of variants available in the ongoing season to five (including the base variant).

With around half of the Fortnite Override season elapsed, there is currently a wide variety of sprites and their variants available in the game. As we inch closer to entering the final month of Chapter 7 Season 4, it’s exciting to speculate which new items and changes are brewing for the forthcoming updates.

  • Crash Bandicoot Sprite in Fortnite

title.rendered: OpenAI says research agents posted 53 user images to image-hosting sites

content.rendered:
OpenAI’s research agents posted 53 user-provided images to outside image-hosting sites through unlisted but discoverable links. The images had been uploaded to OpenAI models and included in training data before agents in the company’s research environment posted them.

The links were not publicly listed, but that did not prevent discovery. OpenAI called the posting an inappropriate use of the data. No public details explain how the links were found or what the images showed.

OpenAI cannot match the images to their owners

OpenAI was working with image-hosting providers to remove the posts, and some images were still online at that point.

OpenAI could not notify the people who supplied the images because it could not reconnect them to their original accounts. It also did not explain how it determined which images came from users. The count of images is known, but the number of affected people is not.

The posts predate new safeguards

The posts happened before OpenAI added security procedures following the July Hugging Face incident, when research models bypassed controls and accessed third-party systems. OpenAI has not disclosed when the image posts happened or which model was involved.

The image posts are part of a wider review of agents acting on the internet during training and evaluation. That review is ongoing, and OpenAI has described other cases of agents interacting with third-party sites. This incident is specifically about user-provided images being placed on outside hosting services by research agents, not a feature in ChatGPT’s consumer app.

excerpt.rendered: OpenAI says its research agents posted 53 user images to hosting sites through unlisted but discoverable links. It says it cannot identify the people who provided them.

title.rendered: Google Photos adds a redact pen and four more updates

content.rendered:
Google Photos is adding a redact pen and four other updates for editing, organizing, and sharing photos. The changes include film-inspired styles, new Remix templates, Wardrobe availability in India, and photo actions through Gemini Spark.

What is new in Google Photos

  • Redact in Markup: Blur sensitive information before sharing an image. The upgraded tool also adds more precise thickness controls for drawings and new fonts. It is rolling out globally on Android.
  • Moods: Apply styles that adapt to each image, including 35mm film and 2000s digicam looks. Moods is available globally on Android.
  • Wardrobe: Google Photos can catalog the clothes in your pictures so you can browse pieces, combine them into outfits, and try on looks virtually. It is available to eligible Android and iOS users in the U.S., India, and Brazil.
  • Remix: Create images with 15 new templates for red-carpet portraits, birthday cards, and photo-booth shots. These templates are available on Android and iOS in select countries to users over 18.
  • Photos in Gemini Spark: Use a prompt to select, brighten, and share photos. This feature is limited to eligible Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the U.S.

The rollout differs by feature. Android users globally are getting the new Markup tool and Moods, while Wardrobe is available in India on both Android and iOS. Remix and Gemini Spark remain limited by country, age, or subscription.

Photos also has conversational editing and AI video tools for Photos and YouTube Shorts.

title.rendered: Google tests Flipkart checkout inside Gemini and AI Mode in India

content.rendered:
Google is testing a Flipkart checkout experience inside Gemini and AI Mode in India. Some users see a Buy button on selected Flipkart listings; tapping it opens a Flipkart-branded checkout without leaving the AI interface.

The pilot is limited to some users and a small set of products: smartphones, electronics, and mobile accessories. People outside the test still see regular product listings. Amazon products can appear alongside Flipkart items, but only Flipkart listings currently get the direct Buy option.

Google surfaces products, Flipkart handles checkout

For people in the test, the change is the handoff: they can discover an item while asking Gemini or AI Mode for help, then start checkout from the product listing. The checkout remains Flipkart-branded, but the technology behind the flow is still unknown.

The test is narrower than Google’s Universal Cart plan, which is meant to collect products across Search, Gemini, YouTube, and Gmail. Our Google I/O 2026 roundup explains that wider shopping push. The current Flipkart flow appears separate from Google’s previously demonstrated hosted checkout; it is not clear whether the test uses Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol.

There is also a direct business tie between the companies: Google invested about $350 million in Flipkart in 2024 and took a minority stake. Amazon listings remain visible in the test, but they do not get the same purchase button.

A wider rollout is not confirmed

A person familiar with the test expects Google to widen it later in October, ahead of India’s festive shopping season. Google has not confirmed that schedule or shared a list of eligible accounts and products. For now, the Buy button may not appear even when a Flipkart item shows up in Gemini or AI Mode.

excerpt.rendered: Google is testing a Buy button for select Flipkart products in Gemini and AI Mode in India, with checkout inside the AI interface and a possible October expansion.

title.rendered: iPhone battery draining after iOS 27? Try these easy fixes

content.rendered:
Following every major iOS update, iPhone users worldwide have increasingly reported inconsistent battery drain. The same reports appeared right after iOS 27 rolled out on September 14, 2026. While it feels like something is wrong with your iPhone, most of what happens in the first few days is normal background housekeeping, not a faulty battery.

This post explains why battery drain happens after iOS 27 and the practical fixes that actually improve battery life, based on Apple’s current support guidance.

Why your iPhone’s battery drains after an iOS 27 update

There are a few common reasons your iPhone may use more power than usual right after updating:

  • Background setup work: Apple notes that your iPhone continues indexing files for search, analyzing the Photos library, syncing iCloud data, downloading new system assets, and updating apps even after the install screen disappears. All of this draws extra power and can make your phone feel warmer.
  • Siri AI and Apple Intelligence activity: iOS 27 expands on-device Siri AI (on iPhone 16 models and later, and iPhone 15 Pro/Pro Max) and Apple Intelligence. On first launch, eligible iPhones may download models and process more on-device, which adds temporary load on top of the normal update work.
  • New visuals and effects: iOS 26 introduced the Liquid Glass design with richer animations and transparency. iOS 27 keeps that look but adds a new transparency control and under-the-hood optimizations. Richer effects can still demand more from the processor than a plain static setup, especially on older models.
  • Optimized apps: Not every app is immediately optimized for iOS 27. Some may misbehave until developers release updates, showing up as high background activity in Battery settings.
  • Increased usage: Exploring new Camera controls, Siri AI features, and other changes naturally means more screen time, which itself consumes battery.

What’s normal & how long it might take

As with iOS 18 and iOS 26, Apple says a temporary impact on battery life and thermal performance is normal immediately after a major update. In its current battery support document, Apple explains that if tasks related to the update are still ongoing, opening Settings → Battery will show an Insight labeled Ongoing iOS Update or Ongoing Device Setup.

That is your cue to wait.

  • Wait 48-72 hours before judging battery life. Let indexing, downloads, and app updates finish. Keep your iPhone on Wi-Fi and power overnight if you can.
  • Mild warmth and a faster drop during the first day are expected, especially while charging or after restoring from a backup.
  • If drain remains severe after several days and the Ongoing update Insight is gone, check Settings → Battery for unusual app activity and Settings → Battery → Battery Health for capacity. An aging battery below 80% health contributes more to short runtime than the software itself.

iOS 27 is supported on iPhone 11 and later and iPhone SE (2nd gen and later). New iPhone 18 models ship with iOS 27 preinstalled, so they don’t show the same update-related drain. If you updated an older iPhone, early beta testing showed iOS 27 is notably smoother than iOS 26 on devices like iPhone 11 Pro Max thanks to the performance cleanup, which also helps battery over time by reducing unnecessary CPU/GPU work.

Ways to maximize your iPhone battery life

Apple notes battery drain after updating is often temporary, but these settings help while the system settles and for everyday use afterward.

1. Keep an eye on battery insights

Starting with iOS 26 and continuing in iOS 27, Apple shows smarter tools in Settings → Battery that surface real-time insights into what’s actually draining power.

Open Settings → Battery and look for:

  1. Insights and Suggestions at the top, for example, High Background Activity, Display brightness high, or Ongoing iOS Update
  2. Daily Usage chart showing screen-on vs. background time per app

If one app shows far higher background usage than others, it may be poorly optimized for iOS 27 or stuck running. Force-quit it, update it from the App Store, or remove it if you don’t need it.

2. Turn on Adaptive Power

Adaptive Power is Apple’s smarter, low-touch battery helper introduced in iOS 26. There is no new battery toggle in iOS 27, so this is still the best automatic setting to leave on.

When enabled, it uses on-device intelligence to predict days when you use more power than usual, then gently lowers screen brightness (about 3%), limits background activity, and throttles performance slightly to conserve power. If your battery hits 20%, it can automatically turn on Low Power Mode. Otherwise, your iPhone behaves normally.

Here’s how to enable Adaptive Power in iOS 27:

  1. Open Settings → Battery → Power Mode.
  2. Toggle on Adaptive Power.
  3. (Optional) Toggle on Adaptive Power Notifications to get an alert when it activates.

Note: Adaptive Power requires iOS 26 or later and is available on iPhone 17 models, iPhone Air, all iPhone 16 models, and iPhone 15 Pro / iPhone 15 Pro Max. On iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, and iPhone Air, it is on by default. On older supported models, you need to turn it on manually.

Compared to Low Power Mode, Adaptive Power is far more conservative. Use Adaptive Power as your daily set-and-forget, and Low Power Mode when you need maximum conservation.

3. Update all apps

Right after a major release like iOS 27, most developers push App Store updates to optimize for the new system. The iOS 27-optimized version runs more efficiently with fewer background bugs.

Open App Store → Profile icon → Available Updates and update everything, especially banking, VPN, keyboard, camera, and work apps. Then restart your iPhone once to let everything settle.

4. Turn off / restrict background app refresh

This setting lets apps refresh data in the background. Even with Apple’s optimizations, it still drains battery heavily.

  1. Open Settings → General → Background App Refresh.
  2. Tap Background App Refresh, then select Off (or Wi-Fi only if you prefer).

If you want a middle ground, leave it on and turn it off per-app for apps you rarely need fresh.

5. Disable unnecessary location services

Apps like food delivery, ride-hailing, and Weather can request constant location, which is one of the biggest GPS-related drains.

  1. Open Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services.
  2. Select the app you want to limit.
  3. Under Allow Location Access, choose Never or While Using the App, and consider turning off Precise Location where you don’t need it.

6. Turn off always on display

Always On Display looks great on Pro models, but keeping the screen lit when you’re not using the phone still costs power.

  1. Open Settings → Display & Brightness → Always On Display.
  2. Toggle off Always On Display.

If you prefer to keep it, iOS 27 lets you keep AOD, but you can reduce its wallpaper/wallpaper dimming impact and pair it with Adaptive Power rather than running it full-brightness all day.

7. Use low power mode

Low Power Mode is still the fastest way to extend battery when you’re low. It reduces 5G usage (on most models), limits display refresh to 60Hz on ProMotion devices, pauses iCloud Photos temporarily, and turns off Mail Fetch and Background App Refresh.

  1. Open Settings → Battery → Power Mode.
  2. Toggle on Low Power Mode.

You can also add Low Power Mode to Control Center or ask Siri to turn it on. It automatically turns off when you charge above 80%. If you want it earlier than 20%, create a Shortcuts automation: Shortcuts → Automation → Battery Level → Turn on Low Power Mode.

8. Enable optimized battery charging and charge limit

You can’t stop battery aging, but you can slow it. iOS now offers two related controls in Settings → Battery → Charging:

  1. Optimized Battery Charging learns your daily routine and waits to charge past 80% until you need it.
  2. Charge Limit (80% / 85% / 90% / 95% / 100%) on iPhone 15 and later lets you cap charging to reduce time at full voltage. Choose 80-85% if you charge overnight and want longest lifespan.

If your Battery Health is already below ~85%, capping the limit and avoiding overnight heat helps most.

9. Quit unnecessary apps

You do not need to constantly swipe away apps. iOS manages them well. But if Battery shows an app stuck in the background after the iOS 27 update, swipe it away or restart the iPhone. A single rogue app accounts for many post-update complaints more than the system itself.

10. Adjust auto-lock

Your display is the biggest consumer of power. Shorter auto-lock means less drain when you set the phone down.

  1. Open Settings → Display & Brightness → Auto-Lock.
  2. Choose 30 Seconds (or 1 Minute if that’s more practical).

11. Disable/adjust push & fetch settings

How often your iPhone checks Mail and Calendar matters. Push keeps waking the radio.

  1. Open Settings → Apps → Mail.
  2. Tap Mail Accounts → Fetch New Data.
    Turn off Push and set Fetch to Hourly or Manually for accounts you don’t need instantly.

General tips to save battery life on your iPhone

  • Turn off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth when not needed from Settings, not Control Center, which only disconnects temporarily.
  • Keep Auto-Lock at 30 seconds: Settings → Display & Brightness → Auto-Lock → 30 Seconds.
  • Turn on Reduce Motion: Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Reduce Motion. This also tones down Liquid Glass animations.
  • Adjust Liquid Glass transparency: iOS 27 adds a transparency control so you can reduce translucent effects if you prefer less visual load: Settings → Display & Brightness / Accessibility → Display → Transparency.
  • Use a still wallpaper: Avoid live or dynamic wallpapers. Use a still image instead.
  • Use Airplane Mode in weak signal areas, like on a train. Weak cellular is a heavy battery drain as the modem hunts for signal.
  • Turn off Raise to Wake in Settings → Display & Brightness if your screen turns on too often.
  • Turn off Keyboard Haptics: Settings → Sound & Haptics → Keyboard Feedback → toggle off Sound and Haptics.
  • Update to the latest iOS 27.x point release when Apple ships fixes. Apple continues tuning performance and power balance in follow-up updates.

These are long-tested fixes, and with iOS 27’s performance focus, they matter even more on older hardware where battery capacity is already lower.

Regain control of your iPhone’s battery life…

Battery drain right after iOS 27 is frustrating, but in most cases Apple expects it to be temporary. It usually lasts 2 to 3 days of indexing, Siri AI model setup, and app updates. Check Battery Insights for Ongoing iOS updates before changing everything else. If the issue persists after that window, the steps above, especially Adaptive Power, Background App Refresh limits, Location limits, and Low Power Mode, will bring your battery life back toward normal.

Have you noticed your iPhone battery draining faster after iOS 27? Which fixes helped you most? Share your experience in the comments below.

Don’t miss:

  • Essential iPhone Tips You Need to Know to Master Your Phone
  • How to fix Apple Watch battery drain after watchOS 11 update

keyPoints.title: Reasons for Rapid Battery Drain
keyPoints.explanation: High screen brightness, background app refresh, location services, resource-intensive apps, poor network conditions, push notifications, outdated software, and many widgets can cause your iPhone's battery to deplete quickly.

keyPoints.title: Optimize Battery Life with Practical Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Simple adjustments like turning off unnecessary features and updating your iOS can significantly extend your iPhone's battery life.

keyPoints.title: Turn Off Location Services for Power Saving
keyPoints.explanation: Disabling location services for apps that don't need GPS significantly conserves battery power, especially when the battery is low.

keyPoints.title: Use Dark Mode on OLED Displays
keyPoints.explanation: Enabling dark mode reduces power consumption on iPhones with OLED displays, prolonging battery life.

keyPoints.title: Manage Background Activities and Settings
keyPoints.explanation: Disabling background app refresh, turning on auto-brightness, activating low power mode, and removing unnecessary widgets help maximize battery efficiency.

title.rendered: Best iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max screen protectors I’d actually buy

content.rendered:
When I buy a new iPhone, the first accessory I put on it isn’t a case. It’s a screen protector. A tiny scratch or crack on an expensive display is the last thing anyone wants to deal with. But with so many options available, choosing the right screen protector for the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max can be surprisingly confusing.

For this guide, I looked at popular options and compared them based on protection, clarity, installation, fingerprints, privacy, and reflections. So you can find the best iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max screen protector for the way you actually use your phone.

How I choose the best screen protectors

I don’t want a screen protector that ruins touch sensitivity, collects fingerprints, creates rainbow effects, reduces outdoor visibility, or leaves an ugly border around the display.

The things I look out for are as follows:

  • Protection: Tempered glass is my preferred option because it provides a harder protective layer than a typical plastic film. But hardness ratings aren’t the entire story. The quality of the glass, adhesive, and edge construction matter too.
  • Installation: A cheap screen protector that takes 20 minutes of alignment, dust removal, and bubble chasing is definitely not for me. I prefer protectors that include an alignment frame or installation tray.
  • Clarity and touch response: I want my iPhone display to look and feel like the original one. That means no noticeable haze, rainbow effect, excessive loss of brightness, or reduced touch response.
  • Fingerprint resistance: No one wants to wipe the display every five minutes. An effective oleophobic coating avoids smudges and makes swiping feel smoother.
  • Case compatibility: I always check how much clearance the protector leaves around the edges so it fits the iPhone 18 Pro case.
  • Outdoor visibility: A glossy screen protector can reflect sunlight and overhead lighting. Anti-reflective protectors are ideal if you regularly use your iPhone outdoors.

Top 6 iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max screen protectors

Rather than pretending there is one perfect screen protector for everyone, I’ve divided these into different use cases.

1. Spigen GlasTR EZ Fit Screen Protector: Best overall

Spigen’s GlasTR EZ Fit is the screen protector I would recommend to most people who simply want reliable protection without experimenting with specialized features.

It uses high-purity alumina-silicate glass strengthened by ion exchange for added durability. Meanwhile, the 9H surface hardness helps protect against everyday scratches from things like keys, coins, etc. The EZ Fit auto-alignment tray makes installation easy for beginners.

What I particularly like is that Spigen focuses on preserving the original display experience. It offers 100% optical clarity, so colors and details should remain sharp and natural. Also, the specially designed adhesive retains the phone’s original touch response.

Pros

  • Good everyday scratch protection
  • Case-friendly design
  • Smooth touch response
  • A good choice if you don’t want privacy or anti-reflective glass 

Cons

  • Not the most specialized option on this list
  • Glossy glass can still produce reflections outdoors
  • Premium pricing compared with basic tempered glass

My take: If I want a screen protector that I can install easily and then forget it’s there, Spigen GlasTR is one of the options I’d consider first.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

2. ESR UltraFit Armorite Screen Protector: Military-grade drop protection

If your biggest concern is impact protection, go for this ESR Armorite screen protector.

It uses durable 9H+ tempered Armorite glass designed to withstand up to 110 pounds of pressure. So your iPhone 18 Pro display is safe from drops and bumps. The reinforced glass can also resist deeper scratches while maintaining high-definition clarity.

Additionally, the oleophobic coating helps keep smudges and fingerprints off the screen. I appreciate its two-step application tray and built-in dust-removal strip, which help reduce dust and annoying bubbles during installation.

Pros

  • Strong focus on impact protection
  • Military-grade protection claims
  • Dust- and bubble-reducing installation system
  • Includes three screen protectors

Cons

  • Black border around the edge
  • Some current iPhone 18 Pro users have reported edge-lifting issues

My take: ESR is the choice if protection matters more to me.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

3. amFilm Magnetic OneTouch Screen Protector: Best for easy installation

The amFilm option caught my attention because it takes a slightly different approach to installation. The OneTouch magnetic installation system is aimed at making alignment easier, which is useful if you’ve ever ruined a screen protector because it landed 2mm off-center.

The protector uses 0.33mm-thick 9H tempered glass for resistance to everyday scratches and impacts. It also has a hydrophobic and oil-repellent coating designed to reduce fingerprints and keep the display cleaner.

Pros

  • Installation takes around 30 seconds
  • Reduced plastic waste
  • Multiple-protector packages can provide backups
  • Useful if you frequently replace screen protectors

Cons

  • Magnetic installation system may feel unnecessary for some users
  • Fingerprint resistance can wear down with long-term use

My take: I’d consider this if installation anxiety is your biggest problem.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

4. Mous Privacy Screen Protector for iPhone 18 Pro/18 Pro Max: Best for outdoor usage

This is the option I’d choose if you regularly use your iPhone in public places.

MOUS has used a 360° privacy filter to block side views, making it much harder for people sitting next to me to read what’s on my screen, while the optical layering ensures the display remains clear when I look at it straight on.

For protection, it uses 9H-hard, shatter-resistant glass designed to absorb impact and resist cracking. The screen protector also has an anti-scratch and anti-smudge coating that helps keep fingerprints, oil marks, and minor scratches under control.

Pros

  • Useful for public transport and travel
  • Adds standard screen protection
  • Installation system makes alignment easier
  • Backed by Mous’ 25-year Limited Lifetime Warranty

Cons

  • Narrower viewing angles
  • Screen can look darker from certain angles
  • Not ideal if you frequently share your screen with people nearby

My take: I’d choose Mous if privacy is just as important to me as screen protection.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

5. ZAGG XTR6 Glass Screen Protector: Best blue-light option

ZAGG is one of the names I look at when I want a more premium screen protector rather than a basic tempered-glass sheet. Its Nanocore technology is designed to remove microscopic imperfections in the glass, with ZAGG claiming the protector is up to 22 times stronger than basic glass protection.

Moreover, the silicate-enhanced surface provides smooth, responsive touch. I find its Eyesafe CPF70 blue-light filtering practical because it reduces exposure to certain blue light without giving the display a noticeable yellow tint.

For me, the bigger everyday advantage would be the anti-reflective coating, especially when using the iPhone outdoors. Finally, ZAGG’s PerfectFit installation system helps with alignment and dust-free application.

Pros

  • Premium tempered-glass construction
  • Strong impact protection
  • Up to 30% recycled glass
  • Free lifetime replacements

Cons

  • More expensive than basic protectors
  • Blue-light filtering isn’t something everyone needs
  • May slightly alter the display compared with completely clear glass

My take: I’d pick the ZAGG XTR6 if you want premium protection, reduced glare, and blue-light filtering in one screen protector.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

6. TORRAS SunView AR Screen Protector: Anti-Reflective layer on your iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max

If I use my iPhone outdoors a lot, TORRAS SunView AR is the screen protector I’d look at first. Its biggest advantage is the anti-reflective coating, which makes the iPhone easier to see in bright sunlight without constantly tilting it to avoid glare.

TORRAS uses a 7-layer anti-reflection coating that claims to reduce screen reflections to below 0.8% while maintaining HD clarity, vivid colors, and contrast. I also like that it uses a borderless design, so there are no black borders eating into the display.

For protection, the protector uses 9H+ aerospace glass, ion-exchange reinforcement, and an impact-buffer layer. TORRAS says it has been tested for protection against drops of up to 10 feet.

Pros

  • Helps reduce distracting reflections
  • Good option for bright environments
  • Borderless full-screen coverage
  • 365-day TORRAS support

Cons

  • More expensive than basic clear glass
  • Anti-reflective coatings can change the look/feel of the display
  • Not everyone will notice enough benefit to justify the premium

My take: This is the specialist pick I’d choose for someone who uses their iPhone outside a lot.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

Which screen protector should you buy?

After looking at all six options, I don’t think there’s one screen protector that’s perfect for everyone. I would choose based on what bothers me most when using my iPhone.

Final verdict

I wouldn’t buy an iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max screen protector based purely on a “9H” or “10X protection” label.

After comparing these options, I’d choose Spigen for its balance of protection, clarity, touch response, and easy installation. But if I spend a lot of time outdoors, use my phone in public, or want extra impact protection, the other options may make more sense for my needs.

At the end of the day, the best iPhone 18 Pro screen protector is the one that fits how I actually use my phone. So, which one would you put on your iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max?

title.rendered: Best ChatGPT plugins in 2026: 17 useful app connections

content.rendered:
ChatGPT plugins help most when they save you from copying details between your inbox, calendar, files, and work apps. Google and Microsoft tools cover everyday tasks; less obvious options like Fireflies, Adobe Acrobat, and Aha! help with meeting follow-ups, PDF chores, and product roadmaps.

OpenAI marks its 2023 ChatGPT plugins announcement as outdated. Today’s plugin directory can bundle reusable instructions, connected apps, or both, so one plugin may include several apps. Start with the service you already use instead of connecting everything in the directory.

How to install and use a ChatGPT plugin

  1. Open Plugins in ChatGPT, or Apps if that is what your account shows. Pick a plugin and review the apps and setup it includes.
  2. Select Install plugin or Connect when prompted, then sign in to the service if it asks.
  3. In a chat, mention the plugin with @ or open + and choose More when those controls are available. Ask for a specific task.

Your account, plan, region, workspace, role, and ChatGPT surface affect which plugins appear. Work and school administrators may need to enable an app. ChatGPT can use only information the connected account can access, and actions such as editing a file or changing a store require the right permissions. Check the current OpenAI plugin guide if your menu looks different.

ChatGPT plugins for email, calendars, and files

If you use Google or Microsoft at work, start with the tools that already hold your information. Connecting duplicate services usually adds another account to manage without giving ChatGPT useful new context.

1. Gmail for finding email and preparing for meetings

Gmail can search and reference your inbox. Ask it to find the latest message about a project, pull out a deadline, or gather recent correspondence before a call. For example: @Gmail Find the latest email about the launch and list the deadline and next steps. See the Gmail plugin.

2. Google Drive for working from your documents

Drive can search Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDFs, and other files you can access. Use it to compare two budget sheets, find a decision in meeting notes, or draft a status update from a project folder. Where the feature and permissions are available, ChatGPT can also update the source file; our coverage of editing Google Drive files in ChatGPT explains that workflow. Browse the Google Drive plugin.

3. Google Calendar for checking when you are free

Calendar can look up events and availability, which is useful when you are trying to find a free afternoon or prepare for an upcoming meeting. Try: @Google Calendar When am I free for a 30-minute call on Thursday? See the Google Calendar plugin.

4. Outlook Email for searching work messages

Outlook Email is the Microsoft equivalent to Gmail: search your mailbox, find the latest message about a project, or gather context before replying. Connect it if Outlook is your work email. See the Outlook Email plugin.

5. Outlook Calendar for checking your schedule

Use Outlook Calendar to look up events and availability before suggesting a meeting time. If Outlook is your work email, this gives ChatGPT the calendar side of that setup. Browse the Outlook Calendar plugin.

6. Microsoft Teams for catching up on chats

Teams can look up chats and messages, helping you find a decision or catch up on a conversation without scrolling through a busy channel. Try: @Teams Find the latest decision about the launch plan and summarize the next steps. See the Microsoft Teams plugin.

7. SharePoint for finding shared work files

SharePoint searches shared sites and files, including OneDrive content available to your connected account. Ask it to find a policy, project brief, or the latest version of a team document. See the SharePoint plugin.

Plugins for team knowledge, design, and code

Connect a team chat, wiki, design tool, or code repository only if you use it regularly.

8. Slack for decisions buried in channels

Slack can search messages, threads, and channels you have permission to access. Ask it to find the decision on a project or summarize what changed in a conversation. Try: @Slack What did the team decide about the launch date? Link the messages that support the answer. Browse the Slack plugin.

9. Notion for searching a team wiki

Notion helps find project notes, plans, and decisions across pages you can access. Depending on the plugin, permissions, and workspace settings, it may also create or update pages and databases. Try: @Notion Find the latest decision about [project] and summarize it with the page link. See the Notion plugin.

10. Canva for editable presentations and graphics

Canva can turn a prompt into a presentation, flyer, or social post you can keep editing in Canva. Use it when you want a first design built from your brief or existing brand assets; skip it if you only need help writing the copy. Browse the Canva plugin.

11. GitHub for understanding a repository

GitHub gives ChatGPT access to repositories, issues, and pull requests you authorize. Ask it to explain an unfamiliar project, summarize a pull request, or find where a feature is implemented. It is a specialist pick for people who work with code, not a general productivity add-on. See the GitHub plugin.

Lesser-known ChatGPT plugins for specific jobs

Each one is worth adding only if your work already depends on that service.

12. Adobe Acrobat for fixing and converting PDFs

Acrobat can reorder, split, or merge PDF pages, convert files, redact sensitive details, and extract information from scans with OCR. It can save a round trip to a separate PDF editor when you need to tidy a form or turn a scanned table into editable data. Review the processed file, especially redactions, before sharing it. See the Adobe Acrobat plugin.

13. Fireflies for searching meeting transcripts

If your meetings are already recorded in Fireflies, ChatGPT can search those transcripts, summarize decisions, and pull out action items with the supporting quote or timestamp. Try: @Fireflies List the action items from my last [project] meeting, including owners and due dates if stated. See the Fireflies plugin.

14. Dropbox for turning stored files into a draft

Dropbox can search files you already have there, summarize what changed, and use a folder to draft a project plan or status update. Choose it if Dropbox is where your work lives; if your files are already in Drive or SharePoint, you probably do not need another connection. Browse the Dropbox plugin.

15. Atlassian Rovo for Jira and Confluence work

Rovo searches Jira issues, Confluence pages, and Compass project information. It can also turn a discussion into Jira tasks when those actions are enabled, which is handy after a meeting or planning session. This only pays off if your team already uses Atlassian; everyone else can skip it. See the Atlassian Rovo plugin.

16. Shopify for checking products and inventory

Shopify can help store owners review product listings, check inventory across locations, and understand sales or orders. It can also handle supported store actions, such as creating discount codes. Try: @Shopify Show me products with fewer than 10 units in stock by location. Review any change before it goes live. Browse the Shopify plugin.

17. Aha! for product roadmaps and release notes

Aha! brings product roadmaps and feature updates into ChatGPT. Product teams can ask what is scheduled next, spot initiatives at risk, summarize customer feedback, or draft release notes from recent updates. Use it only if your team tracks features in Aha!; it will not help much if your roadmaps live elsewhere. See the Aha! plugin.

Which plugin should you install first?

Pick the one tied to the information you search for most. Try Gmail or Outlook for email, Drive or SharePoint for files, and Slack or Teams for work conversations. Add Fireflies, Acrobat, Rovo, Shopify, or Aha! only if you already use that service.

Review the requested access before connecting an account, and be especially careful with plugins that can edit files, create tasks, or change store settings. On Apple Silicon Macs, the Apple Messages plugin works in the desktop app’s ChatGPT Work and Codex views, where it can search conversations and prepare replies.

title.rendered: I tried Write With Siri on iOS 27 to rewrite my messages: Here’s what happened

content.rendered:
I write a lot of messages every day, and often end up rewriting them before hitting send. Sometimes a message is too long, the wording feels awkward, or I just can’t find the right tone.

That’s why I was curious about Write With Siri in iOS 27. Apple says Siri can now help write, rewrite, proofread, and improve text using Apple Intelligence. But does it actually make everyday messages better without making them sound like they were written by AI?

What is Write With Siri in iOS 27?

Write With Siri is part of Apple’s next-generation Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27. It lets you use Siri AI to compose, rewrite, proofread, edit, and get feedback on text without leaving the app where you’re writing.

In practice, that means I can be inside Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, or a supported third-party app and ask Siri to generate text from scratch based on a natural-language request. It can also work with text I’ve already written and modify it based on instructions such as making it more formal, friendly, concise, or polished.

More interestingly, Apple says Siri can reflect how you normally communicate with a particular person, including your usual punctuation and tone in Mail and Messages.

My first test: Asking Siri AI to write a message

My first test was deliberately simple. Instead of writing a message myself, I asked Siri AI to create one from scratch.

The workflow is surprisingly straightforward. When the writing field is active in a supported app, you can see the Write With Siri button above your keyboard. Tap it to type your prompt or use the microphone to tell Siri your request. Then hit the search button in the keyboard.

I tried vague prompts like asking Siri to write a short thank-you message. The first thing I noticed was how little I needed to specify. It doesn’t need a perfect prompt such as: “Generate a warm but concise thank-you message with a conversational tone.” You can simply describe what you want in normal language.

The generated message was polished, grammatically clean, and usable. But there was one catch. And that became a recurring theme during my testing.

For a professional email or an important message, that’s useful. For a casual text to someone I know well, I sometimes found myself removing the polished wording because it sounded more formal than I would naturally type.

Rewrite existing text with Siri AI

This is where Write With Siri became much more useful.

Writing something from scratch is nice, but there are already plenty of AI tools that can do that. The feature became interesting when I started writing messages myself and then asking Siri AI to improve them.

For example, I’d type a rough message with missing punctuation, awkward wording, or a sentence that was much longer than it needed to be.

Instead of deleting it and starting again, I could ask Siri to rewrite it.

To do so:

  1. Write or select the text.
  2. Tap the Siri AI icon on the floating menu.
  3. Now, you can tell Siri what changes you want.
  4. Review the rewritten version.
  5. Keep it, modify it again using the Edit with Siri option, or return to the original by tapping the undo button.

Furthermore, Apple offers a Compare option that allows me to review the original and rewritten versions rather than blindly accepting the AI-generated text.

I also tested different instructions:

  • “Make this shorter.”
  • “Make this more friendly.”
  • “Make this sound professional.”
  • “Make this less formal.”
  • “Fix the grammar.”
  • “Make this clearer.”
  • “Expand this slightly.”

The results were generally predictable. The shorter version actually became shorter. The formal version sounded more professional. The proofreading request focused on grammar rather than completely rewriting everything.

That sounds basic, but it makes a difference when I’m already happy with what I wrote and only want one specific thing changed.

Does Write With Siri actually preserve my voice?

This was the test I cared about most.

AI can fix grammar all day long, but if the result sounds nothing like me, I probably won’t use it for personal messages.

Apple says Siri AI can match a user’s writing style, punctuation, and tone in Messages and Mail, including adapting to the way they communicate with individual recipients.

In my testing, I found that the idea works better when I give Siri something to work with. If I ask Siri to create a message from scratch, the result can feel like a generic AI-written message.

But when I give it my own rough text and ask for a rewrite, the result feels much closer to my original intent.

Other useful Write With Siri features

The more I used Write With Siri, the more I realized that rewriting a message is only one small part of what Apple’s AI writing assistant can actually do.

What makes it interesting in iOS 27 is that Write With Siri works systemwide wherever you type. So you’re not limited to Messages. You can use it while writing emails, notes, documents, and other supported text fields without having to jump into a separate AI app.

Automatic proofreading while I type

iOS 27 adds automatic proofreading for spelling and grammar while typing in apps. The system can catch common writing problems as I’m composing text.

For someone who types quickly, this is arguably more useful than having to stop, select everything, and ask an AI to proofread it afterward.

Ask Siri how my writing sounds

Instead of simply asking Siri to rewrite your text, you can select something you’ve written and select the “How does this sound?” option. That turns Siri into something closer to a writing editor. You can even ask the following questions to make your writing comprehensive.

For example, if I’m writing a presentation or an important email, I can ask for feedback rather than immediately replacing my words. This approach is ideal when you don’t want AI to rewrite your work.

Edit text using natural-language instructions

This is probably my favorite part of Write With Siri.

Instead of manually editing a paragraph, I can simply select the text and describe the change I want.

For example:

  • “Make this email sound more formal.”
  • “Rewrite this to be friendlier.”
  • “Shorten this to three sentences.”
  • “Turn these bullet points into a paragraph.”
  • “Make this easier to understand.”

If the existing text was written by Siri AI, you will see a Rewrite option when you select the text. It will give you a different version. If it’s still not good enough, tap the Edit with Siri button and describe your changes.

Turn rough notes into proper writing

Another useful trick is taking fragmented thoughts and turning them into something readable.

For example, you might have several bullet points that make sense to you but aren’t ready to send to someone. Instead of rewriting each point manually, you can ask Siri to turn the bullet points into a paragraph.

This could be particularly useful for:

  • Work notes
  • Meeting summaries
  • Emails
  • Project updates
  • Personal notes
  • Presentation content

It’s a small feature, but it’s exactly the sort of repetitive writing task where AI can save time.

Shorten without starting over

I also found myself using Siri when something I had written was simply too long.

Rather than deleting half the paragraph myself, I can tell Siri to shorten it.

The best part is you can ask it to reduce something to a particular number of sentences or make it more concise while keeping the important information.

The bigger advantage: I don’t have to leave what I’m doing

I’ve used plenty of AI writing tools before. The problem isn’t usually whether they can rewrite something.

The problem is friction. Normally, the process looks something like this:

Select text → copy → open AI app → paste → write prompt → copy result → return to original app → paste again.

Write With Siri cuts out most of those steps.

You can stay inside the app where you’re already writing and ask Siri to handle the change. That’s what makes this feel less like another AI chatbot and more like an actual iPhone writing feature.

When I’d actually use Write With Siri

After testing it, I don’t think Write With Siri is needed for every message. That would actually defeat the point. If I’m texting a friend: “Where are you?” I don’t need AI.

But there are plenty of situations where I’d happily use it.

  • Important messages: If you’re sending something where wording matters, use Siri AI to check it. A quick rewrite can make an important message clearer.
  • Work emails: When you know what you want to say but the wording feels messy, asking Siri to make it more professional or concise is much faster than starting again.
  • Messages written in a hurry: We’ve all sent messages that were basically one long sentence with no punctuation. Instead of fixing it manually, I can ask Siri to clean it up.
  • When English isn’t coming naturally: Sometimes finding the right English phrasing takes longer than it should. Write With Siri can bridge that gap.

When I wouldn’t use it

There are also plenty of situations where I wouldn’t bother.

  • Casual conversations: Overly polished messages can make conversations with friends and family feel strange.
  • Very short messages: If your message is only one or two sentences, rewriting it with AI can take longer than simply fixing it yourself.
  • Messages where my exact wording matters: AI rewriting can change emphasis, personality, or nuance even when the grammar becomes better.
  • When the original already sounds good: If my message is saying exactly what I want it to say, there’s no need for any optimization.

One thing that still bothered me about Write With Siri

The concept is excellent, but the first version of the feature isn’t completely frictionless.

While testing, I found several early issues in iOS 27. Sometimes, the writing interface disappeared after taking a screenshot, comparison screens became awkward to exit, and the keyboard or interface occasionally vanished while rewriting.

I also think Apple’s decision to make Write With Siri so prominent while typing may not appeal to everyone. Let’s hope Apple improves the experience through next iOS 27 updates.

Final take: Did Write With Siri improve my messages?

Yes, but not in the way I initially expected.

I don’t think Write With Siri is going to replace dedicated AI writing tools for serious writing. What makes it interesting is how quickly it handles the small writing problems I encounter throughout the day.

A message that’s too long, an email that’s too formal, a sentence with terrible grammar, a thought that makes sense in my head but looks terrible when I type it. Those are exactly the moments where Write With Siri makes sense.

Will you use Write With Siri? Let me know in the comments below!

You might also like:

  • Siri AI is finally here in iOS 27
  • Siri AI not showing on your iPhone? Here’s how to enable it in iOS 27

title.rendered: How to check if your iPhone is original, refurbished, or fake in 2026

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways

  • Don’t rely on the serial number alone. A counterfeit device can potentially display identifiers copied from a real iPhone.
  • Check Settings → General → About for the model name, model/part number, serial number, IMEI, carrier information, and iOS version.
  • On supported iPhones, check Parts & Service History for Genuine, Used, Unknown, Unverified, or other repair-related messages.
  • For a second-hand iPhone, make sure Activation Lock is disabled and that the phone can be erased and set up with your own Apple Account.
  • You can also try the *#07# dialer shortcut to reach the Legal & Regulatory information about licensing, warranty information, etc.

Buying an iPhone in 2026 is a little different from buying one a few years ago. Counterfeit phones can copy Apple’s exterior design surprisingly well, while used iPhones can contain replaced displays, batteries, cameras, or other components.

I would no longer depend on the serial number alone for verification purposes. When verifying an iPhone, I look at several things at once, such as device identifiers, Activation Lock status, Parts & Service History, Apple services, and more. This gives a much clearer picture of whether the iPhone is genuine and Apple-certified or has been repaired or modified.

In this article, I will show you under what conditions you should verify your iPhone’s authenticity, and how to check whether your iPhone is original or counterfeit so you can purchase with confidence.

When should you check if an iPhone is original?

I recommend verifying your iPhone’s authenticity before or immediately after buying it, especially in the following situations: 

1. When buying a used or refurbished iPhone

This is probably the most important situation. A used or refurbished iPhone can be completely genuine while still having replacement components. Also, the second-hand market is where most counterfeits appear.

That’s why I don’t stop after checking the serial number. Always verify the device’s Parts & Service History before completing the purchase, even if it looks brand-new. 

2. When the price looks suspiciously low

A very low price doesn’t automatically mean the phone is fake, but it is a reason to investigate further.

If someone offers a brand-new iPhone for half the retail price, it’s likely refurbished, stolen, or fake. So, double-check the model number, serial number, and IMEI before paying.

3. When buying from a marketplace

If you have bought your iPhone on online platforms such as OLX, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, eBay, or from any individual, do not just rely on the Apple-looking box. Verify it the moment you receive it. Many fake or stolen iPhones are sold online disguised as legitimate. 

4. After a repair or replacement

A genuine iPhone can contain non-genuine or previously used replacement components.

If your iPhone has been repaired, especially outside of an Apple Authorized Service Provider (AASP), check that no counterfeit parts were installed. Apple’s “Parts & Service History” feature now lets you confirm this. 

5. If you received the iPhone as a gift or promotion

Even if you didn’t purchase the device yourself, I’d still check it before moving personal data onto it.

Fake iPhones can expose you to security risks, poor performance, and no warranty protection.

Why checking iPhone authenticity matters

A genuine iPhone isn’t just about the Apple logo on the back. 

I want to know that the device:

  • Can receive Apple’s software updates
  • Supports Apple’s security and privacy protections
  • Can use Apple’s official apps and services
  • Doesn’t have an Activation Lock tied to someone else
  • Doesn’t contain unexpected replacement components
  • Has the hardware it claims to have
  • Can be serviced properly through Apple Warranty
  • Isn’t being sold with misleading information

Buying a counterfeit iPhone, which may look real but often fails within months, means wasting your hard-earned money. Moreover, it can expo

10 Ways to check if an iPhone is original or fake in 2026

Here’s a step-by-step guide I use to verify an iPhone’s authenticity. 

1. Check the Serial Number and IMEI

Your iPhone’s IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) and Serial Number are unique identifiers so it’s the easiest way to verify if the iPhone is original. 

To verify your device’s Serial Number: 

  1. Go to Settings → General → About.
  2. Copy the Serial Number. 
  3. Visit Apple’s official warranty checker: checkcoverage.apple.com. 
  4. Enter the serial number and confirm the CAPTCHA.

If Apple recognizes your device as a Valid Purchase and shows warranty details, it’s genuine. Otherwise, if it says “invalid serial number,” the phone is fake or unregistered. 

From the About screen, you can also check the device’s IMEI, Model name, and EID, and compare these details with the original packaging or purchase documentation where applicable. You may also dial *#06# to see the IMEI number.

Important: Don’t treat a recognized serial number as proof. A valid serial number only tells you that the identifier is recognized. However, it does not mean that the device you have physically is the original device associated with that identifier. That’s why I always combine this check with the other methods below.

2. Check the Model and Part Number

Each iPhone model number reveals whether it’s new, refurbished, replaced, or personalized. Find it under Settings → General → About → Model Number. 

  • M – Brand new, purchased retail 
  • F – Refurbished by Apple 
  • N – Replacement for a service request 
  • P – Personalized/engraved by Apple 

Note: These letters appear only in the first character of the part number and may vary slightly by region. 

Now, you may find out if someone is trying to sell you a refurbished phone in the name of a new one. Also, tapping that field reveals the actual model number, which you can compare against the number shown on the box.

3. Check Activation Lock before buying a used iPhone

This is one of the checks I would never skip when buying a second-hand iPhone. A phone can be 100% genuine and still be unusable to you because of Activation Lock.

To check the Activation Lock status, you need to have the device in hand since there’s no way to verify it remotely.

  1. Turn on the iPhone and start the basic setup.
  2. If you see the “iPhone Locked to Owner” screen or the device asks for the previous owner’s Apple Account password, Activation Lock is still enabled.

Apple specifically advises returning an online-purchased iPhone if you see that message. Unless the previous owner properly erases the device and removes it from their account.

4. Check Parts & Service History

Some customers report scams with serviced iPhones. The device is original, but it may have been repaired with non-Apple parts due to malfunctions. So, the iPhone can not provide the same user experience with those parts installed.

Go to Settings → General → About. If the iPhone has repair information available, you’ll see Parts & Service History.

Depending on the iPhone model and component, Apple can show information for parts such as battery, display, logic board, front camera, and rear cameras.

You may see labels such as:

  • Genuine: It means that the repair used genuine Apple parts and processes.
  • Used: The part is a genuine Apple component that was previously used in another iPhone.
  • Unknown: It can indicate a non-genuine component, an installation or verification issue, a malfunctioning component, or a component that has been modified.
  • Unverified: Apple says this can appear when the logic board was previously used in another iPhone. It can affect certain features, including Apple Pay.

So if someone advertises an iPhone as “completely original, never repaired” but Parts & Service History tells a different story, I’d ask questions before buying.

5. Check the iPhone’s physical design

I would recommend checking the device physically because counterfeit manufacturers can imitate software screens, but physical inconsistencies can reveal a lot.

Check:

  • Apple logo placement and polish quality (not printed or glued) 
  • Frame material and finish
  • Button placement
  • Camera arrangement
  • Display bezels and notch
  • Charging port and pentalobe screws near it 
  • Speaker and microphone openings
  • SIM tray, where applicable
  • Overall weight and build quality

Don’t use a generic checklist for every iPhone, though.

For example, newer iPhones have USB-C, while older models use Lightning. Some models have an Action button, while others have a Camera Control button configuration. Camera layouts also vary by generation.

Compare the phone with the specifications and images for the exact iPhone model you’re buying.

6. Use the Legal & Regulatory shortcut

Open the Phone app and enter *#07#, then press the call button.

On supported iPhones, this can take you to the device’s Legal & Regulatory information. You can also open it from Settings → General → Legal & Regulatory.

The screen can contain sections such as:

  • Legal Notices
  • Licence
  • Warranty
  • RF Exposure
  • Safety & Handling
  • Regulatory Certification

It gives you another way to inspect the licence and warranty information associated with the device.

7. Check the iOS Version

A sophisticated counterfeit can imitate the appearance of iOS.

Go to Settings → General → Software Update. The phone should behave like a normal iPhone and provide you with Apple’s software update screen. Here, note the iOS version and build number, and check it against Apple’s official support page.

Also, when you set up your new iPhone, it asks you to create an Apple ID. If it prompts you to enter your Google account or anything else, the iPhone is not original.

However, I wouldn’t use the presence of an iOS-like interface as my only authenticity test. Instead, check whether the device can actually use Apple’s ecosystem and services.

8. Check Apple’s built-in settings and services

A genuine iPhone should provide Apple’s normal system environment, including pre-installed apps and features such as:

  • Settings
  • App Store
  • Safari
  • Messages
  • Photos
  • Phone
  • FaceTime, where available
  • Apple Account services
  • Find My
  • iCloud services

Don’t just look at the icons. Open the apps and settings and make sure the device behaves like an actual iPhone.

If you see an Android-style interface underneath an iOS-like skin, a Google Play Store, or Android system settings, that’s an obvious red flag.

9. Test Face ID, cameras, and connectivity

Before buying a used iPhone, I would spend a few minutes actually testing it.

  • Set up Face ID if the seller allows you to reset the device. If Face ID isn’t working, don’t automatically assume the phone is fake. It could simply have a hardware problem or previous repair.
  • Next, open Camera and test the front camera, rear cameras, zoom levels, video recording, flash, and portrait features.
  • Finally, test Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular network, AirDrop, and NFC-related functions, such as Apple Pay, where available.

A failure here doesn’t prove the phone is counterfeit, but it can reveal hardware or software problems that matter when you’re buying used.

Also, check the battery health of the iPhone. Don’t pay “like-new” money for a phone with a heavily degraded battery.

10. Get it verified by Apple 

In case you still have some doubts about the authenticity of your device, it is advised to get it checked at the nearest Apple Store or Apple Certified Service provider. They can run diagnostics to confirm if your iPhone (and its parts) are authentic Apple components. 

This is particularly useful when you’re dealing with:

  • A suspicious second-hand phone
  • A repaired iPhone
  • A device with Unknown parts
  • Face ID problems
  • A phone with inconsistent identifiers
  • An unusually cheap iPhone
  • A device whose regulatory or model information doesn’t match the seller’s claims

Don’t make these common mistakes

There are several older authenticity tricks I’d no longer treat as definitive.

  • A valid serial number doesn’t prove that the physical hardware is the original device associated with it. Use it together with other checks.
  • Missing Apple Pay or other Apple Intelligence features doesn’t automatically mean the phone is fake. Apple services vary by country, region, device and configuration.
  • Quick Start failure doesn’t prove a counterfeit. It can fail due to normal setup issues or connectivity problems.
  • An “Unknown” part does not necessarily indicate that the whole iPhone is counterfeit. The device itself could be an authentic product from Apple with just one relaced component.

To stay safe, always buy from official Apple Stores or authorized resellers. Avoid deals that seem “too good to be true,” and verify the IMEI and serial number before paying. 

Final thoughts

Checking whether an iPhone is original doesn’t take much time, but it can save you from buying a fake, repaired, or locked device. I recommend checking the serial number, IMEI, Activation Lock, Parts & Service History, software, hardware, and Legal & Regulatory information before making your purchase.

A few minutes of checking can save you from a very expensive mistake. So, is your iPhone really original, or is there something hiding beneath the surface?

keyPoints.title: When to Verify Your iPhone's Authenticity
keyPoints.explanation: Always check if your iPhone is genuine before or immediately after buying, especially with pre-owned, suspiciously cheap, online, repaired, or gifted devices.

keyPoints.title: Importance of Authenticity Verification
keyPoints.explanation: Verifying your iPhone helps you avoid scams, ensures proper performance and updates, protects your privacy from malware, and guarantees warranty and support eligibility.

keyPoints.title: How to Check IMEI and Serial Number
keyPoints.explanation: Use Settings → General → About to find these numbers, then verify them through Apple’s official website to confirm if the device is recognized as valid and registered.

keyPoints.title: Physical and Internal Checks for Authenticity
keyPoints.explanation: Inspect physical features like build quality, logo placement, and button layout, and verify internal parts and service history through Settings to identify counterfeit or non-genuine components.

keyPoints.title: Additional Verification Methods and Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Test network features, use setup tools like Quick Start and iTunes, confirm iOS and pre-installed apps, activate Siri, and consider getting a professional check at an Apple Store for full verification.

title.rendered: Apple and Qualcomm renew patent license agreement starting in 2027

content.rendered:
Qualcomm has renewed its global patent license agreement with Apple, with the new deal taking effect on April 1, 2027. The announcement does not give the agreement’s duration or financial terms, and it does not announce a new modem-supply deal, according to Qualcomm’s press release.

Patent licensing and buying modem chips are separate arrangements. Qualcomm announced a separate agreement in 2023 to supply Snapdragon 5G Modem-RF Systems for Apple’s smartphone launches in 2024, 2025, and 2026.

Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro introduces its C2 cellular modem system. Our iPhone 18 Pro overview covers the rest of the hardware, while the A20 Pro vs A19 Pro guide explains how a phone’s main processor and cellular modem handle different jobs.

The renewal confirms that Apple’s patent license with Qualcomm continues from April 2027. It does not say which modem chips future iPhones will use. Qualcomm has not shared the length or financial terms of the new license.

excerpt.rendered: Apple and Qualcomm renewed their patent license, effective April 1, 2027. The deal is separate from modem supply; its duration and financial terms remain undisclosed.

title.rendered: Apple will fix iPhone 18 Pro Face ID reboot bug with a software update

content.rendered:
Apple told 9to5Mac that a software update will fix a bug that makes some iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max devices freeze and restart after Face ID fails. The update should arrive early next week, according to 9to5Mac’s report.

The issue appears after a failed Face ID attempt when unlocking a protected app, such as Passwords. The phone can stop responding to touch and restart a few seconds later. 9to5Mac reproduced the problem, but it does not affect every iPhone 18 Pro owner.

Apple has not named the update version. 9to5Mac thinks it may be iOS 27.0.1 based on traffic data, but that remains unconfirmed.

The fix is not available yet. When it arrives, iPhone owners can check Settings → General → Software Update or follow our guide to updating an iPhone to iOS 27.

excerpt.rendered: Some iPhone 18 Pro users see their phone freeze and restart after Face ID fails. Apple says a software fix is coming early next week, but has not named the update.

title.rendered: Adobe brings creative tools to Gemini and Acrobat editing to Claude

content.rendered:
Adobe is bringing Photoshop, Lightroom, Express, and Firefly tools into Google Gemini, while adding Acrobat tools and hands-on editing to its Claude plugin. The integrations let users work on images, designs, and PDFs inside a chatbot conversation, as Adobe announced on September 24.

Gemini can make and edit creative assets

Adobe in Gemini lets users describe a photo edit, social media asset, or marketing design in chat. Gemini then calls Adobe tools to make the requested changes, such as adjusting product photos, resizing designs for social channels, or personalizing an Express template.

Adobe says the Gemini integration is rolling out globally across Gemini plans. To use it, open Personal Intelligence, choose Adobe under Connected Apps, and sign in to an Adobe account. Adobe’s Gemini connector guide currently lists English as its supported language.

Gemini has been expanding beyond a general-purpose chatbot, with Google’s I/O announcements detailing new AI features across Search, Chrome, and other services. Adobe adds a route from that chat interface to familiar creative tools.

Claude adds PDF and design editing

The Adobe plugin for Claude now includes Acrobat features alongside more than 80 tools from Adobe’s creative apps. Users can combine or split PDFs, delete pages, redact information, and export documents to other formats.

Claude also gets an interactive PDF editor for changing text, reordering pages, and adding comments or highlights. For Adobe Express designs, a layer-based editor lets users adjust individual images, copy, colors, and fonts instead of regenerating the full design.

Adobe says the Claude integration is rolling out globally on Claude and Claude Code for desktop, mobile, and web. People can try it as guests; signing in to Adobe unlocks more tools, higher usage limits, and continuity across sessions.

The new chat integrations add a conversational option to Adobe’s existing apps. People who want to edit directly on their phone can also use the Adobe Photoshop app for iPhone.

excerpt.rendered: Adobe’s Gemini integration brings tools into chat, while its Claude plugin adds Acrobat PDF features and editing controls for documents and Express designs.
