title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro vs Google Pixel 11 Pro: Which phone should you buy?

content.rendered:
The iPhone 18 Pro is the better fit if you already use an Apple Watch or Mac, or want its advanced video formats. The Google Pixel 11 Pro costs $100 less in the U.S. and adds Google’s camera and Gemini tools. Its 5x optical telephoto and 10x optical-quality zoom give it more reach on paper than the iPhone’s 4x optical and 8x optical-quality options, but neither spec sheet tells us which phone takes better zoomed photos.

The timing matters: Pixel 11 Pro has been on sale since August 25, while iPhone 18 Pro reaches stores September 18. Pixel has independent reviews; the iPhone has not had retail testing yet. If you’re deciding mainly on battery, camera quality, or sustained performance, wait for the first head-to-head tests.

iPhone 18 Pro vs Pixel 11 Pro: quick comparison

These are the U.S. list prices for each phone’s 256GB model. Brightness and battery figures come from different manufacturer tests, so treat them as specifications rather than direct wins.

Design and display: Pixel is lighter, iPhone is shorter

Both phones have a 6.3-inch screen and the same listed width. The Pixel is 7g lighter and 0.35mm thinner; the iPhone is 2.7mm shorter. Those are small differences, so try them in a case if weight or pocket fit matters to you.

Their materials differ. Apple uses an aluminium unibody with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back. Google pairs an aluminium frame with Gorilla Glass Victus 2 on both sides and a matte rear panel. Those glass names tell you what covers each phone, not which one is more likely to survive a drop.

On paper, the Pixel panel is denser at 495ppi versus 460ppi and has a higher listed peak brightness: 3,600 nits versus Apple’s 3,000-nit outdoor peak. Apple lists an anti-reflective coating; Google lists an anti-scratch screen shield. Both support adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz, so scrolling and animation should feel smooth. The brightness figures use different test conditions, though, and don’t settle which screen is easier to read outdoors.

In its display test, Tom’s Guide measured the Pixel at 2,860 nits. An Android Central reviewer also flagged the Pixel’s low-frequency PWM dimming, which may bother people sensitive to screen flicker. If OLED displays have caused you discomfort before, try the Pixel in person. No one has published a comparable retail iPhone 18 Pro test.

Cameras: Pixel has a longer native telephoto lens; iPhone adds aperture control

The Pixel’s dedicated telephoto camera starts at 5x optical zoom, compared with 4x on the iPhone. But both phones crop in further while advertising “optical-quality” reach: Pixel lists 10x and iPhone lists 8x. Google’s 120x Pro Zoom is digital, as is Apple’s zoom beyond 8x. Those high numbers help frame a faraway subject, but they aren’t a promise of clean detail. In TechRadar’s Pixel review, 120x results became hit-or-miss and more artificial as the reviewer pushed past about 30x.

The iPhone’s standout photo change is its variable-aperture 48MP main camera. It can switch among f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4, automatically or through manual controls. Opening the aperture lets in more light; closing it keeps more of a group or landscape in focus. The phone also gives you controls for shutter speed and white balance, plus ProRAW capture. This is more direct control on paper, but review samples will show how much it improves everyday photos.

Magic Capture is the Pixel’s standout tool for quick action, such as a child running or a pet jumping. Google says it analyses around 400 frames with on-device intelligence and Gemini, then saves a well-timed 12MP photo, applies edits such as crop and unblur, and keeps the video too. Android Central’s reviewer praised it after using it repeatedly. Camera Looks lets you adjust the image style before shooting. Google also says Instant Night Sight takes low-light photos up to 4.5 times faster than on Pixel 8, 9, and 10 models, though that doesn’t tell us how its night shots compare with the iPhone. Both phones can shoot close-ups: the Pixel has Macro Focus on its autofocus 48MP ultrawide, while the iPhone supports 48MP macro photos.

For video, the iPhone has the stronger list of creator formats: 4K Dolby Vision at up to 120fps on its main camera, Apple Log 2, and ProRes RAW. Recording ProRes at 4K120 requires an external drive, so that top-end mode isn’t a casual point-and-shoot setting. Pixel records standard 4K at up to 60fps and offers 8K24/30 through Video Boost, along with a teleprompter and tools for editing social clips. The 8K mode runs through the cloud rather than saving a finished 8K video right away. Google Photos backup is required, the recording is capped at 10 minutes, and boosting can take time. The Video Boost instructions say the initial clip is 1080p SDR. That’s a different workflow from the iPhone’s 4K recording formats, which are available directly in the camera app.

Pixel has a 42MP autofocus selfie camera with a wider field of view and 4K60 video. The iPhone’s 18MP Centre Stage camera can keep you framed during calls, and it supports tap-to-zoom and Dual Capture. Megapixels alone can’t tell us which takes more natural selfies; that will take side-by-side samples from a retail iPhone.

Performance: everyday speed looks fine on Pixel; gaming tests raise questions

The iPhone’s A20 Pro has a six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, and hardware ray tracing. Apple also added a vapour chamber and claims up to a 40% sustained-performance gain over the iPhone 17 Pro. Pixel 11 Pro runs Google’s Tensor G6, which powers its camera processing and on-device Gemini features.

In TechRadar’s review, a 512GB/16GB Pixel handled ordinary multitasking, streaming, and casual games well; the base model has 12GB of RAM. More demanding graphics are less settled: Tom’s Guide’s benchmarks show stronger CPU scores than the previous Pixel generation, but no comparable GPU improvement, and a separate gaming test on the Pixel 11 Pro XL found limited gains over last year’s model. Since that was the larger XL model, it doesn’t establish how the regular Pro handles heat over time. iPhone 18 Pro hasn’t reached reviewers yet, so no fair speed or gaming contest is available.

For messaging, photos, maps, and everyday games, neither phone should feel short on power. If you buy a flagship mainly for long gaming sessions or benchmark-leading performance, wait for retail tests instead of treating Apple’s chip claims or Google’s benchmark charts as a final verdict.

Software and AI: choose the assistant and ecosystem you want to live with

iPhone 18 Pro ships with iOS 27 and Apple’s Siri AI, which entered beta on September 14. Siri is meant to understand personal context and what’s on your screen, but Apple says language and region support vary; English is first, and Siri AI isn’t available on iOS in the EU at launch. Many Apple Intelligence tasks run on the device, while more complex requests can use Private Cloud Compute.

Pixel 11 Pro comes with Android 17 and Gemini Intelligence. Google says Gemini can handle supported multi-step tasks across more than 40 apps. Pixel tools include Circle to Search, Live Translate for supported videos, and Gemini-powered camera features. Rambler removes filler words from voice dictation, while proactive cards can surface relevant details such as a flight update. Google lists these features in its Pixel 11 overview; availability depends on language, country, age, app, and sometimes subscription. For a broader platform comparison, see how iOS 27 and Android 17 differ.

Your existing devices may matter more than either assistant. Apple Watch works only with iPhone, and Google’s Pixel Watch doesn’t support iOS. Pixel can send files to Apple devices through Quick Share and AirDrop compatibility, but the iPhone recipient has to set AirDrop visibility to “Everyone for 10 Minutes.” Apple’s Move to iOS setup can transfer much of your data when switching. This Android-to-iPhone transfer guide explains what moves over. To send files from Android to Apple, use AirDrop-compatible Quick Share.

Battery and charging: Pixel has real-world test results; iPhone does not yet

Google advertises 30-plus hours for Pixel 11 Pro. In Tom’s Guide’s continuous 5G browsing test, it lasted 13 hours and 25 minutes. Android Central’s 45W charging test reached 51% after 30 minutes, while Google’s own estimate is up to 55% in that time with a 30W-or-higher PPS charger. TechRadar’s reviewer said the Pixel got through a full day even with heavy video streaming or gaming, but needed an overnight charge.

Apple estimates up to 24 hours of typical use, 36 hours of local video playback, or 33 hours of streamed video for iPhone 18 Pro. Its fast-charge claim is up to 50% in around 15 minutes with a separately sold 60W-or-higher AVS adapter. MagSafe can reach 50% in 30 minutes with a 35W-or-higher adapter, and both MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging reach up to 25W. Google claims up to 55% in around 30 minutes with a separate 30W USB-C PPS charger; Pixelsnap/Qi2.2 wireless charging also goes up to 25W.

These runtime figures aren’t a fair head-to-head: Google and Apple use different definitions and test methods. The Pixel has retail battery tests already; the iPhone’s numbers are Apple’s estimates from preproduction testing. Neither phone includes a wall adapter, so add a compatible one to your budget if you don’t already own one. Wait for the same lab to test both before choosing based on battery life.

Durability and software support: Google publishes the clearer timeline

Both phones carry an IP68 rating. Apple specifies a maximum depth of 6 meters for 30 minutes, while Google doesn’t list a matching depth figure. IP68 isn’t a promise against every kind of water damage, and neither phone has a matched drop or scratch test. If a cracked screen would be expensive to replace, a case is still a sensible buy.

Google commits the Pixel 11 Pro to seven years of Android OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates, counted from its first U.S. Google Store availability in August 2026. Apple hasn’t announced a fixed support period for iPhone 18 Pro. Google’s promise is easier to plan around, but it doesn’t prove Apple’s phone will stop receiving updates sooner.

Price and availability: Pixel costs less, iPhone offers more storage

The Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099 for 256GB in the U.S.; iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for the same storage. These are list prices before trade-ins, carrier deals, tax, or limited-time offers. Apple’s options go up to 2TB, while Pixel tops out at 1TB, which may matter if you keep a large photo and video library on the phone. Both U.S. models are eSIM-only, so check carrier support if you usually swap physical SIM cards. Apple’s iPhone specs say that directly; Google lists the Pixel as eSIM-only in its Store FAQ, but gives conflicting physical-SIM wording elsewhere on the same page. Confirm the exact Pixel variant if a SIM tray is essential.

Pixel is available now. iPhone 18 Pro goes on sale September 18 in its first markets, with some regions following September 25. If you need a phone today, the Pixel is the ready-to-buy option. If you can wait a few days, the iPhone’s retail reviews should make the camera and battery trade-offs easier to judge.

Which phone should you buy?

  • Buy the Pixel 11 Pro if you want Android now, use Gemini or Google’s camera tools, want a 5x optical lens, or value a published seven-year update policy. It also saves $100 at the U.S. starting price.
  • Buy the iPhone 18 Pro if you own an Apple Watch or Mac, want up to 2TB of storage, or plan to shoot and edit video with Apple Log 2 or ProRes formats.
  • Wait for iPhone 18 Pro reviews if you don’t have a platform preference and care most about photo quality, gaming performance, or battery life. The Pixel’s zoom and price are concrete advantages, but the iPhone hasn’t had the retail testing needed to call an overall winner.

In case you missed:

  • iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra comparison
  • iPhone Duo vs Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra comparison
  • Apple A20 Pro vs A19 Pro
  • Best iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max screen protectors

excerpt.rendered: The iPhone 18 Pro favors Apple’s ecosystem and pro video, while the Pixel 11 Pro offers 5x optical zoom, Gemini, seven years of updates, and a lower U.S. price.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro battery replacement now costs $129 out of warranty

content.rendered:
Apple has raised the U.S. out-of-warranty battery service fee for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max to $129. The new figure appears in Apple’s iPhone repair price table, up $10 from the $119 fee for the iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone 17 Pro Max.

The battery fee is the same for both Pro models

Apple lists the following U.S. out-of-warranty service estimates for the new Pro iPhones:

The battery is the only repair in the table that costs the same on both models. Apple says it will inspect the device before confirming the final service fee. Taxes may apply, mail-in service may add a shipping charge, and Apple Authorized Service Providers can set their own prices.

The increase follows last year’s iPhone 17 repair pricing, which listed a $119 battery replacement for the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max. Apple had kept that fee unchanged from the iPhone 16 Pro generation.

Apple has not explained the $10 increase

Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro models use updated battery designs, and the company rates the U.S. eSIM-only versions for up to 36 hours of video playback on the iPhone 18 Pro and 45 hours on the Pro Max. Apple has not said whether the new battery designs, parts, or service process are behind the higher replacement fee.

For the wider hardware picture, this iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max guide breaks down the new models’ battery and charging claims.

That distinction matters because the $129 price is a service estimate, not a published explanation of Apple’s repair costs. It also applies to the U.S. table. Repair prices and taxes can differ in other countries.

AppleCare+ can remove the battery fee

Apple says battery service is included at no extra charge for an AppleCare plan when the battery’s capacity drops below 80%. Normal battery wear is not covered by Apple’s standard limited warranty, so owners without qualifying coverage will see the out-of-warranty price instead.

Before booking a repair, check the battery health and coverage status. This guide to checking whether an iPhone battery needs replacing explains what to look for beyond the percentage shown in Settings.

The new $129 fee is still lower than replacing a phone that otherwise works well, but it makes the cost of keeping an iPhone 18 Pro for several years a little higher. Buyers outside the U.S. should use Apple’s local repair page for the price that applies to them.

title.rendered: WhatsApp is rolling out a new way to search messages on iPhone

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is finally making one of its most-used features easier to access on iPhone. The messaging app has started rolling out a new in-chat search button, giving users a quicker way to find old messages within a conversation. The feature follows several weeks of beta testing and is now reaching some iPhone users.

WhatsApp has been testing the search shortcut

The new search button isn’t completely unexpected. Early last month we reported that WhatsApp began testing the feature in its iOS beta, where the search shortcut appeared in the bottom-right corner of the in-chat interface.

Until now, searching within a conversation required several steps. I had to open the chat, tap the contact or group name at the top, choose the search option from the chat information screen, and then enter my query after being returned to the conversation.

That works, but it feels unnecessarily complicated when all I want to do is find one old message. The new shortcut removes that detour.

The button now appears while scrolling up

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has moved beyond testing and is officially rolling out the feature to users. Interestingly, the final version doesn’t appear in exactly the same place as the button shown during beta testing.

Now, the search shortcut appears at the top when users scroll up through a conversation. Tap the button, enter a keyword, and WhatsApp can search through the conversation without forcing me to navigate through multiple menus first.

When you return to the latest messages at the bottom, it disappears. That makes much more sense than permanently adding another icon to an already crowded interface.

The shortcut is also being made available across different types of conversations, including individual chats, group chats, and channels.

The rollout is gradual

As usual, the feature isn’t appearing for every iPhone user immediately. WhatsApp is gradually rolling it out, so even if you don’t see the new search button yet, that doesn’t necessarily mean anything is wrong with your app.

excerpt.rendered: The in-app search button removes a few annoying steps from finding your old WhatsApp chats.

title.rendered: iOS 27 made iPhone Parental Controls a lot smarter: Here’s what parents need to know

content.rendered:
For years, parental controls have felt like digital duct tape. Using Family Sharing, parents could set a few restrictions, limit screen time, and hope for the best. Meanwhile, kids were navigating an internet that has become faster, smarter, more addictive, and in many cases, more dangerous.

With iOS 27, Apple has expanded parental controls beyond simple screen-time limits. The new system lets parents manage app and website access, set flexible schedules and category-based time allowances, control who children can communicate with, and add approval steps before children visit new websites or connect with new contacts.

Here’s everything you need to know about the new child safety features in iOS 27.

The real problem was never screen time

The debate around kids and technology has been stuck in the wrong place for years. Parents have been obsessing over how many hours children spend on devices while ignoring a more important question: What are they actually doing during those hours?

A child might spend an hour on a homework app and another hour on a social platform. Treating both activities as identical simply because they consume the same amount of time doesn’t give parents much useful context.

iOS 27’s new controls reflect this by adding category-based allowances, schedules, website approvals, and communication controls alongside traditional Screen Time.

Ask to Browse adds approval before new websites

The standout feature in iOS 27 is called Ask to Browse. Instead of allowing unrestricted web access, children must request permission before visiting new websites in Safari. Parents receive the request in Messages and decide whether the site should be accessible.

Apple says Ask to Browse is turned on by default for Child Accounts under 13. Parents can also pre-approve websites.

Some people will immediately call this overprotective. They’re wrong. Nowadays children aren’t just stumbling onto inappropriate websites anymore. They’re encountering AI-generated content, manipulative recommendation systems, misinformation, scams, extremist content, and communities designed to keep them engaged at any cost.

Giving an 11-year-old unrestricted access is risky. Ask to Browse introduces friction. And sometimes friction is exactly what safety looks like. However, for children who are ready for broader browsing, Limit Adult Websites provides a less restrictive alternative that filters adult content.

Apple is moving from reactive parenting to preventive parenting

Most parental controls activate after something has already gone wrong, such as:

  • The child installs the wrong app.
  • A stranger sends a message.
  • An inappropriate image arrives.

Parents discover the issue later.

Apple is trying to flip that model. iOS 27 has redesigned the initial child-account setup experience. Parents can choose only the essential system apps, use a recommended set, or select the apps they consider appropriate. Apps can then be added over time as the child is ready for more access.

This works alongside Ask to Buy, which still lets parents approve eligible app downloads, purchases, and in-app purchases.

You may like: What is the Hide Location feature in iOS 27?

Time Allowances are smarter than traditional app limits

Parents have long had the option to block apps after a certain amount of usage. The problem? Real life doesn’t work that neatly. Sometimes a child genuinely needs more time for homework, communication, or creative projects.

Apple’s new Time Allowance system lets parents control the time their kids spend in apps across categories, including Entertainment, Games, and Social Media. It will show limits suggested by experts based on your child’s age. They can also grant additional app access when needed without dismantling their entire Screen Time setup.

Along with it, iOS 27 introduces Screen Time Schedules to manage which apps are available during periods such as Before School, School, and After School, and lets you create different routines for weekdays and weekends.

Parents can also allow certain apps and contacts at all times, so important communication or other selected services remain available even when a category allowance has been reached.

Communication Safety now covers gore and violent content

One of the most significant updates is Apple’s expansion of Communication Safety. The system already helped detect and intervene when sensitive and explicit images were shared.

Now, it can blur images and videos containing detected gore or violent content in Messages and FaceTime for users under 18. The child encounters a safety intervention before viewing that potentially disturbing material.

That’s a bigger deal than it sounds. The modern internet isn’t just exposing children to sexual content. Violence has become normalized across social platforms, messaging apps, and viral content feeds.

iOS 27 also lets parents manage contacts for Phone, Messages, and FaceTime. A parent can require permission before a child connects with someone new, and the approval request can be reviewed from the parent’s device.

The redesigned Screen Time puts controls closer to the surface

Let’s be honest. Screen Time for the child’s account was basic. The data was there, but the insights weren’t.

Apple has redesigned the parental Screen Time experience to provide an at-a-glance view of a child’s device usage and most-used apps. Parents can use quick actions to adjust access in the moment instead of digging through multiple settings screens.

For example, parents can quickly pause or change access during meals, outdoor activities, or other periods when they want the device to take a back seat.

More requests can now arrive directly in Messages

The new approval workflow brings several child requests into one place. Depending on the settings, a child can request a new app or purchase, access to a new Safari website, additional device time, or permission to communicate with a new contact. Parents can approve or decline eligible requests from Messages or directly on the child’s device.

What parents should take away

iOS 27 doesn’t replace conversations, trust, or active parenting, but it gives families considerably more control over the digital environment around a child. Apple’s latest child safety features go beyond simply counting minutes by adding controls for websites, apps, schedules, app categories, communication, and sensitive content.

The most useful change for many families is the ability to start with a narrower set of apps and websites and gradually expand access. Parents can also make one-off approvals without completely changing the underlying setup.

If you’re setting up these controls now, update every device in the Family Sharing group to the latest iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27, where applicable. Then review the child’s allowed apps and websites, communication contacts, Time Allowances, and daily schedules.

You can even get help from Apple’s dedicated Child Safety website.

title.rendered: macOS 27 Golden Gate is here: Everything new you need to know

content.rendered:
Apple has officially released macOS 27 Golden Gate, bringing a mix of new AI features, design changes, and useful updates to the Mac. The biggest addition is Siri AI, which can understand personal context, work with what’s on your screen, and perform tasks across supported apps.

Along with Siri, macOS 27 adds Visual Intelligence, improves Liquid Glass, brings new features to Safari and Photos, and makes everyday tasks like searching, managing files, and using multiple displays easier. Here’s everything new in macOS Golden Gate, including the features I think are actually worth trying.

Liquid Glass gets a much-needed refinement

Last year’s Liquid Glass redesign was Apple’s biggest visual change to macOS in years. Golden Gate doesn’t throw it away. Instead, Apple gives me more control over it and fixes some of the things that made the original design feel inconsistent.

A new Liquid Glass slider in System Settings > Appearance lets me adjust the interface’s transparency. I can choose between an ultra-clear interface that lets more of the background show through, a more opaque tinted appearance for better readability, or something in between.

Apple has also changed how Liquid Glass handles complicated backgrounds. Transparency now diffuses complex content more effectively, while darker edges, brighter highlights, and updated window shadows make it easier to distinguish the active window.

Other changes include:

  • Standardised toolbars across apps, making headings and groups of controls easier to read.
  • Window corners also look more consistent and aren’t as dramatically rounded as they were in Tahoe.
  • Sidebars no longer float inside the windows; instead, they extend edge-to-edge.
  • Apple has also brought back colored sidebar icons, which disappeared with Tahoe.
  • App icons use additional Liquid Glass layers for more detail and sharpness across light, dark, tinted, and clear modes.

Apple is also using HDR to add more depth to the interface and has introduced new Golden Gate wallpapers and screen savers, giving the release its own visual identity.

Siri AI brings a new way to use your Mac

This is the biggest change in Golden Gate, and it goes far beyond the old Siri I was used to.

Apple has rebuilt Siri around its newer Apple Intelligence models to provide the following features:

  • Personal context: Siri can search across information from Mail, Messages, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Photos, and Files. Apple’s semantic search index allows Siri to understand what that information means rather than looking for exact keywords.
  • Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what I’m currently looking at. For example, if you see an unfamiliar image in Safari, you can right-click it and ask Siri what it is or search for more information.
  • App Actions: It can perform actions in supported apps, including creating Calendar events, working with Reminders, drafting messages, and performing other app actions. You can also combine multiple tasks in one request.
  • Search or Ask in Spotlight: Spotlight has become Siri’s home on the Mac. Press Command + Space to search on Mac, or use the Search or Ask interface to ask Siri a question. Siri responses can be expanded and support follow-up questions.
  • Write with Siri: It can draft text from scratch, rewrite something, change the tone, shorten text, turn bullet points into paragraphs, correct grammar and spelling, and give feedback on your writing.

The dedicated Siri app

macOS 27 also gets a standalone Siri app.

In the app, you can start new conversations, revisit previous chats, and search your Siri history. The best part is it lets me pin conversations I want to return to.

The Siri app syncs conversations across compatible Apple devices, so I can start a conversation on one device and continue it elsewhere.

Custom Siri voice and better dictation

On Macs with an M3 chip or later and at least 12GB of memory, Apple offers a more powerful on-device model to adjust Siri voice’s pace and expressivity.

The same on-device model also improves systemwide dictation, with better natural-language understanding and fewer mistakes with spelling, punctuation, and capitalisation.

Siri AI is initially available in English, with additional languages planned. Mac users in the European Union can also access Siri AI.

Visual Intelligence finally comes to the Mac

Visual Intelligence was already useful on the iPhone, but I think it makes even more sense on a Mac because so much of my day is spent looking at documents, webpages, images, charts, and schedules.

Apple gives macOS 27 dedicated shortcuts for Visual Intelligence, including Command + Shift + Space. You can also use the screenshot interface to select an area of your display. Once selected, Siri can summarise or translate text and answer questions about what you’re seeing.

There are some particularly useful new capabilities too. Visual Intelligence can extract multiple events from a schedule, import contact details from a business card, turn a barcode in an image into a Wallet pass, and provide nutritional insights from a photo of food. Bill splitting is also supported in the U.S.

Apple Intelligence is now woven throughout macOS

Siri and Visual Intelligence are the stars, but Golden Gate’s bigger story is how deeply Apple Intelligence has been woven into individual apps.

Photos gets much better AI editing

The Clean Up tool gets a major upgrade. It can now handle more complicated backgrounds and reconstruct missing areas more effectively. It has three new modes: Fast, High Quality, and Auto.

Extend lets me expand the borders of a photo using generative AI, whereas Reframe goes further by using spatial information captured with compatible photos to adjust the perspective of a person or object.

The new Photos app features also add one-click video-frame saving, one-to-five-star ratings, slideshows from any album or collection, better Shared Albums with full-resolution sharing, Android and Windows contributions, and emoji reactions.

Safari can organise my browser chaos

Safari uses Apple Intelligence to organise open tabs into topics. If I’m researching a new laptop while also planning a trip, Safari can group the relevant pages into separate groups instead of leaving me with one enormous collection of tabs.

Then there’s Create an Extension. You can describe the Safari extension you want, and Apple Intelligence can generate it. Safari also gets Notify Me, which can monitor a website for changes. I can tell Safari what to watch for, such as concert tickets going on sale or a product coming back in stock, and choose how often it checks.

Mail gets smarter

Mail’s search has been rebuilt to rank results by relevance and intent, rather than simply matching keywords and recency. So if you search for a retailer because you want to find an order, Mail can prioritise the order email instead of showing a pile of promotional messages.

Smart Replies can also better reflect my writing style, while contextual suggestions can be provided to third-party apps. Mail can surface actions for Calendar, Maps, and Wallet based on information inside messages.

Shortcuts finally become approachable

I’ve always thought Shortcuts was powerful but unnecessarily intimidating for casual users. Golden Gate addresses that with Describe a Shortcut.

Instead of assembling actions manually, you can tell Shortcuts what you want in normal language. For example, I tried this prompt: “Every morning, show me my first meeting, today’s weather, and my Reminders.”

Apple Intelligence selects the necessary actions and builds the workflow. You may use Describe a Change to refine it through additional instructions or manually edit the finished Shortcut.

Home, Passwords, Calendar, and more

The Home app can now provide a summary of all the events detected by the camera, including recognising faces, pets, vehicles, packages, grouping similar events from multiple cameras together, and natural language searching through the recording history.

Supported HomeKit Secure Video cameras can also record in up to 4K, while energy-monitoring accessories can display consumption in Home. Apple’s AI-powered Home features require a 2TB iCloud+ plan or higher.

The Passwords app can use Safari and Apple Intelligence to automatically update eligible weak or compromised passwords.

Calendar and Reminders understand natural-language descriptions, with Reminders automatically extracting details such as dates, times, and locations.

Genmoji and Image Playground become more flexible

Genmoji gets an improved creation interface. You can start with text, an existing emoji, a photo, or a person, then use Describe a Change to modify individual elements instead of starting over. The result is more consistent, and the best part is that I can change the style from the default 3D cartoon appearance to something like a drawing or sketch.

Image Playground is also much more flexible. It can now generate images in virtually any style, including photorealistic images, and I can select specific parts of an image to modify using natural language.

Golden Gate also makes everyday Mac tasks faster and easier

Some of my favourite changes are the ones that don’t require me to learn anything new.

Messages gets less flashy but very practical improvements. Failed messages can retry automatically, photos and videos can continue sending after a connection problem, and Tapback notifications are also consolidated. Apple Music gets improved AutoMix transitions and refreshed artist pages.

Apple Notes app gains trackpad handwriting and sketching, Markdown copy and paste, divider lines, and Section Links. Maps gets more detailed Flyover imagery, Podcasts gets a better video experience with Picture-in-Picture and downloads, and the Phone app gets Call Context, which can surface relevant information from Mail when I’m calling a business.

iPhone apps running through iPhone Mirroring can now be resized larger. External-display handling is more consistent, with macOS able to restore window positions, Spaces, and display assignments when switching between monitors.

AirDrop transfers are faster, network file browsing is quicker, and Shortcuts actions and app intents are indexed more quickly so they can launch faster from Spotlight.

If you use an iPad as a Mac display through Sidecar, you get better touch support, including tapping controls, scrolling, and system gestures. Apple has also added a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture to Safari, Mail, News, Podcasts, and Calendar.

macOS 27 adds more serious parental controls

Apple has expanded new parental controls across Mac, iPhone, and iPad.

Parents can choose which apps children can access, approve downloads through Ask to Buy, and use Ask to Browse to require approval before a child visits a new website. There are also controls for who children can communicate with through Messages, FaceTime, and Phone.

Communication Safety now expands its protection to blur graphic violence and gore in Messages and FaceTime for users under 18.

Time Allowances let parents set limits for categories such as Entertainment, Games, and Social Media, while Daily Schedules control which apps are available at particular times.

Screen Time now gives parents insight into usage time and allows them to make instant changes.

macOS 27 compatibility and release date

Apple has made macOS 27 Golden Gate available to the public since September 14, 2026. It is available through System Settings > General > Software Update.

There is one major compatibility change: Intel Macs are no longer supported.

Golden Gate works on Apple Silicon Macs, including:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)
  • MacBook Air with Apple Silicon (2020 and later)
  • MacBook Pro with Apple Silicon (2020 and later)
  • iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)
  • Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)
  • Mac Studio (2022 and later)
  • Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)

macOS Golden Gate is also the last version with full Rosetta 2 support, so developers still relying on Intel-based Mac software have another reason to move toward native Apple silicon versions.

My take on macOS 27 Golden Gate

The easiest way to describe Golden Gate is that Apple isn’t just making the Mac look different; it’s trying to make the Mac understand more.

Siri can understand personal context and take actions. Visual Intelligence can understand what’s on my screen. Spotlight can be a place to ask questions rather than simply find files. Safari can organise my research and monitor websites. Photos can reconstruct parts of an image. Shortcuts can turn plain-English instructions into automation.

But I don’t think the smaller changes should get lost underneath all the AI headlines.

Better Mail search, faster AirDrop, improved network file browsing, more reliable external-display setups, better Messages syncing, swipe-to-refresh, improved Sidecar touch controls, and smarter file naming are exactly the kind of features that can make a Mac feel better every day without demanding my attention. That’s what makes macOS 27 Golden Gate interesting to me.

Which macOS 27 feature are you most excited to try first?

About Ava Biswas

  • Ava is a die-hard Apple aficionado and loves testing the latest tech gadgets.
  • She is always on the lookout for issues Apple users are facing, finds solutions, and crafts troubleshooting guides.

Experience

title.rendered: Best iPhone Duo screen protectors: 5 options I’d consider before buying

content.rendered:
When I first looked at the iPhone Duo, the screen protector was one of the accessories I immediately started thinking about. With a regular iPhone, you can just pick a good tempered glass protector and move on. The iPhone Duo is different because it has two displays of different sizes, so protecting it requires a little more thought.

Fortunately, there are a few screen protectors for the iPhone Duo that are available right now. Below, you will find my top picks that stand out for different reasons, from premium tempered glass and privacy protection to matte and budget-friendly choices.

iPhone Duo availability: Pre-orders start October 16, 2026, and the phone becomes available October 23, 2026.

How to choose the right screen protector for your iPhone Duo

I wouldn’t buy an iPhone Duo screen protector based only on its advertised hardness rating. The foldable design changes what I would look for.

1. Check whether it protects the outer or inner display

Compatibility is the first thing I would check before placing an order.

The iPhone Duo has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch folding display. The two screens aren’t interchangeable, and a protector designed for the outer display obviously cannot be used on the folding panel.

Some products are designed for the outer screen, while others are for the inner display. For example, the ZAGG option below is explicitly listed as an outer/front screen protector, while Ferilinso offers an inner-screen protector.

2. Don’t treat the inner display like a normal iPhone screen

Apple says the inner display uses multiple ultra-thin layers and adhesives designed to let the layers move as the phone folds. That makes me more cautious about applying a generic tempered-glass protector to the folding display.

If I were to get a screen protector for the iPhone Duo, I would look specifically for a flexible film designed for its inner display, not one meant for other foldable phones.

3. Look for precise alignment

A slightly crooked protector is much more noticeable on a large display. Dust trapped underneath is also annoying, especially when you’re spending this much on a phone.

This is why I like installation trays. Spigen’s GlasTR EZ FIT Pro, for example, includes an auto-alignment tray designed to make installation easier.

4. Decide whether you want clear, privacy, or matte protection

I would choose the screen protector based on how I actually use my phone.

  • Clear glass: Best if you want the original display to look as close to Apple’s design as possible.
  • Privacy glass: Useful if you frequently use your phone in public places.
  • Matte or anti-reflective glass: Better if reflections bother you.

The iPhone Duo’s inner screen already has a nano-texture finish designed to reduce glare, so I would be particularly careful about adding another layer that changes the display’s appearance.

5. Don’t ignore touch sensitivity

A screen protector shouldn’t make the iPhone Duo feel noticeably different.

Apple’s displays support ProMotion up to 120Hz and Haptic Touch, so it would be preferable to have a screen protector that does not interfere with the touch input.

6. Make sure it is case-friendly

I always check this before buying a screen protector because a perfect installation can still become a problem if the phone case pushes against the edges.

This is particularly important with the iPhone Duo because the device has a completely different folding construction from a traditional iPhone.

Best iPhone Duo screen protectors you can buy

Here are the five iPhone Duo screen protectors I would put on my shortlist right now.

1. Spigen GlasTR EZ FIT Pro: Best overall for the outer display

If you are looking for a simple, tempered-glass protector without experimenting too much, Spigen GlasTR EZ FIT Pro would be one of my first choices.

It uses its AluminaCore glass construction, advertises 10H+ surface hardness, and comes as a two-pack. It also includes the company’s EZ FIT Pro alignment tray.

What I particularly like here is the installation system. For a premium phone like the iPhone Duo, I’d rather spend a little more and get a protector that is easier to align than fight with bubbles and crooked edges.

Pros

  • 100% optical clarity claimed by Spigen
  • Oleophobic coating
  • Case-friendly design
  • Cleaning and installation accessories included

Cons

  • More expensive than budget alternatives
  • Primarily suited to the outer display

My take: This is the one I’d consider first if your priority is clear protection and easy installation.

Check out on Amazon

2. Ferilinso Inner Screen Protector: For the folding display

The Ferilinso Inner Screen Protector is essential in my iPhone Duo accessories list because it targets the iPhone Duo’s inner display. I find it interesting that the film is claimed to withstand rigorous folding tests and to auto-repair minor scratches.

You also get three 9H+ tempered-glass protectors for the outer display, featuring 2.5D rounded edges, laser-cut precision, scratch-resistant construction, and an oleophobic nano-coating. The company says the coating reduces fingerprints and oil residue by up to 98%.

The bundle also includes a camera lens protector, which is useful if you want to protect several parts of the phone at once.

Pros

  • Three-pack
  • Bubble-free installation for both displays
  • Case-friendly design
  • Camera lens protector included

Cons

  • May slightly change the original display feel or appearance
  • The inner protector may peel off or show a crease

My take: Get this if protecting the inner display is your main concern.

Check out on Amazon

3. ZAGG Glass Elite Privacy: Best privacy screen protector for iPhone Duo

If you use your iPhone in cafes, airports, trains or offices, a privacy screen protector can be more useful than simply buying the hardest possible glass.

The ZAGG Glass Elite Privacy is designed specifically for the iPhone Duo’s front/outer screen. It uses a two-way privacy filter that limits viewing from side angles. ZAGG also claims up to five times stronger impact protection than basic glass, along with scratch resistance and its ClearPrint smudge-resistant coating.

Pros

  • Aluminosilicate tempered glass
  • Bubble-free, easy installation design
  • Maintains touch sensitivity
  • Replacement for life

Cons

  • Privacy filtering can reduce viewing angles
  • May make the display look slightly darker than a standard clear protector
  • More expensive than basic tempered glass

My take: I’d choose this if privacy is more important than maximum display brightness and clarity from every angle.

Check out on Amazon

4. JETech 3D Anti-Reflective iPhone Duo screen protector: Reduce glare and smudges

The JETech 3D 9H+ Anti-Reflective Front Screen Protector takes a different approach. Instead of focusing primarily on privacy, it features a magnetron-sputtered optical coating to reduce reflections and glare, making the display easier to see in bright light.

The screen protector offers full-screen coverage, including the curved edges. Moreover, the 9H+ tempered glass resists everyday scratches, wear, bumps, and accidental drops.

JETech also adds an electroplated anti-fingerprint coating that repels oil and water, making smudges easier to wipe away while maintaining responsive touch.

Pros

  • 3D full-coverage design
  • Anti-fingerprint treatment
  • Two protectors included
  • Installation tool included

Cons

  • Matte/anti-reflective finish may slightly change the display’s original look
  • Not ideal if glossy clarity is your priority

My take: This is the one I’d keep in mind if reflections annoy me more than privacy concerns.

Check out on Amazon

5. TOCOL screen protector: Best budget-friendly option

Finally, there’s TOCOL, which I’d consider if I don’t want to spend too much on a screen protector.

The iPhone Duo version is advertised as a two-pack with 9H+ tempered glass, 8-foot military-grade shatterproof protection, anti-scratch treatment, and a case-friendly design. It also uses a bubble-free installation system designed specifically for the Duo.

Pros

  • More affordable than premium alternatives
  • Two-pack provides a spare
  • Case-friendly design
  • Automatic installation system

Cons

  • Fewer premium features than Spigen or ZAGG
  • The budget positioning may mean a less refined overall experience

My take: Go for this one when you want basic protection without spending too much.

Check out on Amazon

Which iPhone Duo screen protector would I choose?

If I were buying my iPhone Duo on launch day, I wouldn’t automatically choose the same type of protector for both displays.

My approach would be:

Things I would check before installing any iPhone Duo screen protector

There’s one mistake I would avoid with the iPhone Duo: treating its folding display exactly like the screen on an ordinary iPhone.

Apple has engineered the inner display specifically for folding. It uses a custom nano-texture finish, multiple thin layers, and adhesives designed to enable movement while folding.

So before installing an aftermarket protector, you should check three things:

  1. Is it explicitly made for iPhone Duo?
  2. Does it specify the correct display—inner or outer?
  3. Does the manufacturer provide instructions specifically for the Duo?

I’d also clean the screen carefully before installation. On a large display, even a tiny speck of dust can be the first thing I notice every time I unlock the phone.

Also, don’t press aggressively around the fold or attempt to flatten, peel, or manipulate the inner display beyond the manufacturer’s instructions.

My final verdict

The iPhone Duo is an unusual phone, so I don’t think there’s a one-size-fits-all answer for screen protectors.

Apple has already given the Duo substantial built-in protection: Ceramic Shield 2 on the outer display, a scratch-resistant coating and a nano-texture surface on the inner display.

That’s why I wouldn’t buy a screen protector just for the sake of having one. Always choose it based on which part of the phone you want to protect and whether you’re willing to change how the display looks or feels.

Are you planning to use a screen protector on your iPhone Duo, or trust Apple’s built-in protection?

title.rendered: 4K Video Downloader Plus review: A clean way to save online videos

content.rendered:
Saving one online video is easy enough. Keeping high-quality videos, playlists, subtitles, and audio organised is where browser tools start to feel clumsy. 4K Video Downloader Plus moves the whole job into a desktop app, with more control and fewer questionable download buttons.

It is available for Mac, Windows, and Linux, and the permanent free version covers occasional downloads. Unlike a platform-specific tool, it combines video, audio, subtitle, playlist, and file-management options in one place.

You can download 4K Video Downloader Plus for free and upgrade only if its daily limits or premium feature restrictions get in your way.

4K Video Downloader Plus review: Pros, cons, and key details

4K Video Downloader Plus suits people who save online videos regularly and care about file quality, formats, subtitles, or larger collections. It offers much more control than a basic web downloader while keeping the first download approachable.

Pros

  • Clean interface with a quick copy-and-paste workflow
  • Downloads in resolutions up to 4K and 8K when available
  • Useful format, audio, subtitle, playlist, and channel controls
  • Smart Mode removes repetitive setup
  • Permanent free tier is enough for occasional use

Cons

  • Free downloads have daily quantity limits
  • AI processing, automatic subscriptions, and other advanced tools require higher plans
  • Supported-site reliability can change when platforms update

4K Video Downloader Plus interface and download experience

The main window revolves around one obvious action: copy a video link and select Paste Link. The app analyses it, presents the available quality and format choices, and lets you choose where the file should go. It is a familiar workflow, but putting it inside a proper desktop app makes it feel safer and more predictable than jumping between web downloaders.

The interface does not force every setting into view. A casual user can accept the recommended options and move on, while someone building an offline collection can choose the resolution, format, audio track, subtitles, frame rate, and destination folder.

Supported websites, video quality, and file formats

4K Video Downloader Plus handles media from services such as YouTube, X (Twitter), Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Vimeo, Twitch, SoundCloud, and more. This broad coverage is useful if your saved media comes from several sites rather than one streaming platform.

4K Video Downloader Plus can save videos in MP4 or MKV at resolutions ranging from standard HD to 4K and 8K. The source still sets the limit; a 1080p upload will not become 4K, but the app preserves the best quality that is actually available.

It also covers the details that become important after the first few downloads:

  • Audio-only downloads: Extract audio as MP3, M4A, or OGG instead of keeping the full video.
  • Subtitles: Save available subtitles as SRT files, including multiple languages where provided.
  • Playlists and channels: Queue larger collections instead of feeding the app one link at a time.
  • Multiple audio tracks: Keep original or dubbed tracks when the source provides them.
  • Special video formats: Download supported 3D and 360-degree videos for offline playback.

What are the best features of 4K Video Downloader Plus?

Choosing the same format, resolution, subtitle language, and folder for every file gets old fast. Smart Mode lets you save those preferences once and apply them automatically to future downloads.

Smart Mode is the feature worth turning on first. Set MP4, your preferred quality, and a destination folder, and later downloads can start with little more than a pasted link.

The built-in browser lets you find media and start downloads without constantly switching between the app and a separate browser. Eligible paid plans also let you sign in to supported services for private or protected media that your account already has permission to view.

Users who follow regularly updated channels or playlists can subscribe to them in the app and automatically save new uploads. The built-in proxy can also help when a supported service is blocked by a network or unavailable in a region. These features require an appropriate premium plan, and availability and local rules still apply.

Version 26.1 also added AI audio processing. From the same workspace, Pro users can remove background noise or echo, isolate vocals or speech, and strip music from a downloaded file. These tools will not replace a full audio editor, but they are handy for cleaning up an interview, preparing a voice track, or making a quick karaoke version.

Download performance and file management

Download speed depends on the source website, resolution, connection, and file size. The practical performance advantage comes from the workflow: the app analyses links, queues downloads, and keeps completed files in one manageable list.

You can sort and filter downloads, control individual items or groups, and import or export download records. This matters once you move beyond occasional clips and start handling playlists, courses, reference videos, or several audio files at once.

Skip 8K unless you genuinely need it because the files can consume storage surprisingly quickly. Platform support can also break temporarily when video services change how they deliver or protect media, so keeping the app updated is important.

4K Video Downloader Plus free vs paid plans

The Starter tier is permanently free, with no payment details or short trial countdown. Its main restriction is a daily quantity limit, making it best for occasional use rather than large libraries.

The current premium options are straightforward:

Prices and promotions can change, so check the final purchase page before paying. For most people, the free plan is the right starting point. Personal offers better long-term value once the daily limits become annoying, while Pro makes sense only if you need its automation, AI processing, or commercial license.

The current desktop release requires macOS 12 or later, Windows 11 or later, or 64-bit Ubuntu 22.04 with GNOME or later. Native Apple Silicon and Intel installers are available for Mac.

Is 4K Video Downloader Plus worth it?

Yes, if saving online media is something you do regularly. 4K Video Downloader Plus brings quality controls, audio extraction, subtitles, playlists, repeat-download presets, and file management into one clean desktop app. It feels like a proper utility rather than a website you visit only when every other option fails.

Occasional users should stay with the free tier. You can use it to download YouTube videos one at a time, download full playlists, save a Facebook video, or extract Instagram Reel audio. The desktop app earns its place when you want consistent quality, repeatable settings, and organised downloads.

The main limitation is outside the app’s control: video platforms change frequently, and support can occasionally break until an update arrives. You should also download only content you own, have permission to save, or are otherwise authorised to use.

Verdict: 4.5/5.

4K Video Downloader Plus combines a friendly interface with enough depth for demanding downloads. The free version is genuinely useful, and the paid plans add convenience without turning the basic experience into a demo.

title.rendered: Apple A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: 7 biggest upgrades you need to know

content.rendered:
I have come to a stage where Apple’s yearly chip upgrades are difficult to judge by the name alone. An A20 Pro seems like a straightforward successor to the A19 Pro, but once I got to know about the actual improvements, I realised Apple has got much more under the hood.

The A20 Pro is the first 2nm iPhone chip, featuring a 7-core GPU, wide memory bandwidth, a dual Neural Engine, and new CPU cores. This makes it one of the greatest improvements Apple has made to its mobile silicon in recent times.

So, how big is the change that you will experience? I have analysed the A20 Pro vs A19 Pro across performance, gaming, AI, memory, efficiency, and thermal performance to see what has really changed and whether the A20 Pro is a good enough reason to upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: Specs at a glance

Before getting into the interesting stuff, here’s how the two Apple Silicon generations compare.

The interesting part is that Apple didn’t simply increase the CPU core count. Both chips have six CPU cores. However, in order to improve performance, Apple decided to redesign the CPU cores, push up clock speeds, and redesign many elements around them.

And that is only the beginning.

2nm vs 3nm: The biggest A20 Pro upgrade

When it comes to choosing just one upgrade for the A20 Pro, then it has to be the move from 3nm to 2nm.

The A19 Pro was manufactured using a 3nm-class process, while the A20 Pro moves to TSMC’s N2 2nm process. This lets Apple fit more transistors into a similar die area while providing 18% faster performance and 30% lower power consumption, compared to the A19 Pro.

Besides that, M-class packaging design puts memory and the silicon die in a side-by-side position. This leads to an improvement in the heat dissipation capabilities of the A20 Pro.

Why does 2nm matter on an iPhone?

This is because smartphone CPUs have an inconvenient challenge: They require desktop-level performance without desktop-class cooling.

I can mount a huge cooler on a desktop processor. Apple won’t be able to put it into their iPhone. That’s why efficiency is so important.

The A20 Pro’s 2nm foundation gives Apple more room to increase performance without increasing power draw and overheating. And Apple has used that extra headroom across the CPU, GPU, memory subsystem, and AI hardware. Ultimately, you get better battery life and speed.

CPU performance: How much faster is it?

The A20 Pro retains a six-core CPU, but Apple has introduced two new Super cores and four new efficiency cores. The Super cores can reach up to 4.93GHz, compared with roughly 4.26GHz on the A19 Pro’s Everest performance cores. Apple describes the new cores as desktop-class and says they are up to 20% faster.

And the benchmark numbers back up the idea that this isn’t a minor CPU refresh.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: Benchmark Comparison

An early Geekbench 7 result represented improvements of about 23.3% in single-core and 27.1% in multi-core in that particular comparison.

The A20 Pro also has a clear edge over Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in CPU performance, particularly in single-core workloads. In Geekbench 6, the latter typically scores around 3,588 and 10,207, respectively. That puts Apple ahead by roughly 50% in single-core and 29% in multi-core, according to these reported results.

What about real-world performance?

Having owned an A19 Pro iPhone before, I would not expect the A20 Pro to instantly give me a 25% improvement in basic operations. The A19 Pro is already very fast.

But the difference will be much more noticeable if the workload makes the CPU work for a longer period of time:

  • Video editing
  • Photo processing
  • 3D applications
  • AI workloads
  • Gaming
  • Large file processing
  • Heavy multitasking

So yes, the A20 Pro CPU performance has improved substantially. But I think that the more interesting part is how Apple will use the additional performance over a longer period.

GPU and gaming performance

The A19 Pro has already received a major GPU upgrade, with Neural Accelerators built into each GPU core and a larger 32 MB cache. This improved hardware ray tracing and graphics performance and enabled direct handling of complex on-device AI workloads.

The A20 Pro gets a meaningful graphics upgrade on this.

Apple has moved from the A19 Pro’s 6-core GPU to a 7-core GPU. The new GPU also includes Neural Accelerators designed to accelerate AI-related workloads, while Apple claims the A20 Pro delivers up to 40% faster graphics performance than the A19 Pro.

This makes the A20 Pro very appealing for gaming purposes.

But I wouldn’t judge the GPU upgrade solely by a short benchmark. A smartphone can render a very high frame rate for just a few minutes, after which it starts to struggle because of overheating. This is why I believe the A20 Pro’s GPU update looks even more exciting when combined with its thermal architecture.

For demanding games, the improvements should matter most in:

  • Higher and more stable frame rates
  • Better ray-tracing performance
  • More demanding graphics settings
  • Longer gaming sessions
  • Reduced performance degradation from heat
  • Better handling of graphics-heavy AI features

Early Geekbench graphics results also show a performance gain of approximately 38-40% for the A20 Pro’s full 7-core GPU, although such tests shouldn’t be considered a general benchmark of gaming performance.

If I were buying an iPhone to play demanding games, I’d pick the A20 Pro without any doubts. Though the A19 Pro itself has some good capabilities, its successor has more graphics hardware and sustainability.

Memory: A20 Pro gets a wider highway

This is probably the A20 Pro upgrade that most people will overlook. Both generations can have 12GB of LPDDR5X-9600 memory; hence, the impression is that there is not much change from the earlier version.

But the memory interface is wider. The A19 Pro uses a 64-bit memory interface, reaching up to 76.8 Gb/s bandwidth. The A20 Pro reportedly moves to a 96-bit interface, thus supporting 115.2 Gb/s memory bandwidth, which is 50% better.

I like to think of memory bandwidth as a highway. The amount of RAM is roughly how much cargo I can keep available, whereas Memory bandwidth is how quickly I can move that cargo around. Adding more lanes becomes useful when I start moving huge amounts of data, especially for GPU, AI, and graphics workloads.

That’s why this upgrade matters for:

  • AI processing
  • Graphics rendering
  • Gaming
  • Video editing
  • Large image processing
  • Multitasking
  • On-device machine learning

And it helps explain why Apple can improve performance without simply throwing more CPU cores into the chip.

Neural Engine and AI performance

AI is no longer just an additional feature at Apple, and the A20 Pro is a clear example of this.

While the A19 Pro features a 16-core Neural Engine, the A20 Pro comes with two Neural Engines, which results in 32 Neural Engine cores. Moreover, the A20 Pro has Neural Accelerators in the GPU system.

According to Apple, these Neural Accelerators will provide 2x faster performance in FP8 operations. This matters because Apple is now focusing more on executing AI on the device itself.

Instead of sending every AI request to a cloud server, more processing can happen locally using Apple’s new Foundation Models. That can improve responsiveness and privacy while reducing the need for a constant internet connection.

The A20 Pro’s AI hardware should therefore be useful for:

  • Apple Intelligence
  • Generative AI
  • Image generation
  • AI-assisted photo editing
  • Voice processing
  • On-device language models
  • Real-time image and video processing

In my view, it looks like the A20 Pro has been built to handle not only the Apple Intelligence features the current iPhone has, but also future features Apple might want to introduce.

Thermal performance: Where A20 Pro could make the biggest real-world difference

This is my favourite A20 Pro upgrade because it addresses a genuine problem: heat.

The A20 Pro also changes how Apple packages the chip for sustained performance. Unlike past Apple processors, which used PoP (Package-On-Package), the A20 Pro will have WMCM (Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module) packaging, placing the memory beside the main chip instead.

This will make sure that the heat can now have a clear route out of the CPU and GPU and not get trapped around the hottest part of the chip. In practice, that should help the A20 Pro reduce thermal throttling and maintain higher performance for longer.

Apart from that, Apple has also upgraded the iPhone 18 Pro by including a vapour chamber three times the size of its predecessor. The wider surface area distributes heat and helps it dissipate faster. With all of these, the A20 Pro is able to give 40% better sustained performance compared to the A19 Pro.

This could benefit:

  • Long gaming sessions
  • 4K and high-resolution video editing
  • ProRes workflows
  • 3D rendering
  • AI processing
  • Photography processing
  • Other sustained workloads

And this is where I think the A20 Pro could feel more different from the A19 Pro than the raw benchmark numbers suggest.

Modem and connectivity improvements

The A20 Pro generation also changes what’s happening beyond the processor itself.

The iPhone 18 Pro generation introduces Apple’s C2 modem to the Pro lineup, replacing the Snapdragon X80 modem used in the previous Pro generation. According to Apple, the C2 is capable of delivering 50% faster uploads and 15% lower power consumption and uses mmWave 5G (only in the USA).

The A20 Pro generation also continues Apple’s move toward in-house connectivity hardware. The N1 wireless chip handles technologies including Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread.

For me, the important part isn’t simply that Apple has replaced one modem with another. It’s the possibility of tighter integration of Apple’s own silicon for better power consumption, connectivity, and system-level performance.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: Should you upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro?

After analysing all the aspects, it was clear that the A20 Pro is really a great upgrade.

However, this does not necessarily mean everyone owning an A19 Pro must go out and get an iPhone 18 Pro. If you already own an iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone 17 Pro Max, I wouldn’t upgrade just for everyday speed.

The A19 Pro is already ridiculously fast. If you utilise your iPhone 18 Pro primarily for messaging, web-browsing, social media interaction, photography, and media streaming, you will hardly notice any difference.

I’d consider the upgrade much more seriously if I:

  • Play demanding games regularly
  • Edit videos on my iPhone
  • Use AI-intensive features
  • Want the best possible graphics performance
  • Keep my iPhone for four or five years
  • Care about sustained performance
  • Want Apple’s latest modem and connectivity hardware

For someone buying a new Pro iPhone anyway, though, I’d take the A20 Pro over the A19 Pro every time.

Final thoughts

The A20 Pro is more than just a faster version of the A19 Pro. Apple has practically upgraded every single aspect of the performance equation. Here you have 2nm process, new CPU architecture, larger GPU, increased memory bandwidth, improved AI architecture, and even better thermal management.

For me, the biggest advantage is that Apple isn’t just chasing higher peak performance; it is trying to keep the A20 Pro running fast for longer and able to sustain it.

Is the A20 Pro’s extra power enough to make you upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro? Let me know in the comments below!

title.rendered: Build and Kill Zombies codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Build and Kill Zombies Codes on October 05, 2026

Build and Kill Zombies is a Roblox game where you build your own vehicles and then do whatever it takes to mow down hordes of zombies. However, building the best vehicles in the game requires the right weapons, seats, Hacker Tones, tanks, and plenty of cash. Luckily, the developers have released several codes that let you get your hands on these items for free! So, let’s take a look at all the active Build and Kill Zombies codes and help you build the ultimate zombie-destroying machine.

All working Build and Kill Zombies codes

  • ZEUS: 50 Lightning Tokens
  • IAMPRO: 5,000 Cash
  • COMMUNITY: 1k Cash 1 Small Engine 1 Small Tank
  • CashDrop: 500 Cash
  • MOREFRIENDS: 2 Passenger Seats

Expired or unverified Build and Kill Zombies codes

1X1X1X1, HACKER

How to redeem Build and Kill Zombies codes

The next question you might be wondering is: how do you redeem Build and Kill Zombies codes? Well, it’s quite a simple process –

  1. Fire up Build and Kill Zombies on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Tap on the Shop button.
  4. Paste a working code in the community codes section.
  5. Click Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed a code, the rewards will automatically be added to your inventory in the game.

Where to find more Build and Kill Zombies codes

Build and Kill Zombies doesn’t have a fixed timeline when it comes to dropping reward codes. So, if you’re looking to grab more items, it’s a good idea to keep an eye on the official Build and Kill Zombies Discord server.

The developers can release new codes alongside new updates, events, or milestones, which you can track through the Build and Kill Zombies game page.

Be sure to bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated with the latest codes as they’re released. If you’re into shooting games and want more free rewards, check out the latest Beat the Anime Boss codes, Gym League Codes, Command An Army codes and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

title.rendered: Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude

content.rendered:
Anthropic is folding Claude Cowork into the main Claude chat experience. In its September 16 announcement, the company says users will be able to ask a quick question or hand over a larger task from the same conversation, without first choosing between Chat and Cowork.

The change is rolling out to Pro and Max subscribers over the next few weeks on Claude’s web, desktop, and mobile apps. Team and Free plans will follow, while Enterprise administrators will receive at least 30 days’ notice before their organizations move over.

One conversation can handle quick questions and bigger tasks

The new experience lets Claude decide what a request needs. A conversation can stay short, or turn into research, a report, a spreadsheet, or a presentation that Claude works on after you step away.

Anthropic’s Help Center guide says existing chats, tasks, projects, artifacts, connectors, and skills come with the account when it moves to the new experience. Once the change reaches an account, users cannot switch back to separate Chat and Cowork options.

Docs, Slides, and Design move into the conversation

Anthropic is also adding Claude Docs and Claude Slides, while Claude Design can now work inside regular conversations. The company says all three are in beta on paid plans. Users can edit the results, share them by link, or export a presentation as a PowerPoint or PDF.

The useful part is the handoff. Someone can start with a question, ask Claude to gather information, and finish with a document or slide deck in the same thread. The app can also use connected services such as Google Drive, Gmail, Microsoft 365, and Slack while it works.

What happens during the rollout

There is no switch to turn on. If your message box still shows separate Chat and Cowork choices, Anthropic says your account has not moved yet. If a task runs in the cloud, it can continue after you close your laptop. Tasks that need local files or computer apps still require Claude Desktop to remain open.

The change also makes Claude Cowork’s iPhone and web access more central, since users can check progress or answer questions from a phone while a task continues. Claude Code remains a separate coding environment, including workflows covered in Claude Code’s iOS Simulator support on Mac.

The practical shift is simple: users no longer need to decide where a task belongs before they start typing. The new unified experience is arriving gradually, and the older Chat and Cowork choices will disappear only when Anthropic moves each account over.

title.rendered: iOS 27.2 beta 1 adds a redesigned Health app, FaceTime Dual Capture, and an EU privacy update

content.rendered:
Apple has released iOS 27.2 developer beta 1, build 24B5084k. Apple’s developer release listing dates the seed to September 16, 2026. The beta brings a redesigned Health app and Group FaceTime Dual Capture, while Apple’s release notes add a privacy-related change for users in the European Union.

Developers with beta access can install the update from Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates, then choose iOS 27 Developer Beta. It is still pre-release software, so the feature list can change as Apple continues testing.

Health app and FaceTime changes lead the beta

The redesigned Health app Apple previewed earlier this month is now active in the beta. The official Health announcement describes a new Insights tab, a Longevity tab, and Apple Intelligence-powered health guidance. The beta gives developers an early look at that redesign, although Apple has not said that every part of the final experience is locked.

Group FaceTime also gains Dual Capture. On supported iPhones, it can show the front and rear camera views at the same time, keeping your face in a small window while you show the other person what is in front of you. Apple’s FaceTime camera guide says the feature is available on iPhone 17 or later.

The wider release includes far more than this beta. Our iOS 27 features guide covers the Siri AI, Liquid Glass, Photos, Wallet, and child-safety changes Apple announced for iOS 27.

Apple’s release notes add an EU tracking prompt change

Apple’s iOS 27.2 beta release notes say AppTrackingTransparency now supports an alternative expanded prompt and yearly re-prompting for users in the EU. Apple says the alternative prompt is required in France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and Romania.

The same notes list two known issues: personalized summaries may not generate as expected in the Health app’s Insights tab, and the Describe a Shortcut feature may return an error. Those are useful warnings if you are installing the beta to try the new Health experience.

The first iOS 27.2 seed arrives after the late iOS 27.0 testing cycle, including iOS 27 beta 7 coverage. Apple has not announced a public release date for iOS 27.2, so the current build is best treated as an early look at the next round of changes.

title.rendered: WhatsApp may soon let iPhone users add a third account

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is preparing to raise the iPhone’s in-app account limit from two to three, according to WABetaInfo’s September 15 report. The feature was spotted in WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.37.10.15, but it is still under development and is not available to beta testers yet.

The change would build on WhatsApp’s recent two-account rollout for iPhone. Meta’s March announcement gave iPhone users a way to keep work and personal numbers in the same app without logging out or carrying two phones.

The third account would use the same account list

WABetaInfo says users would see an "Add account" option even after two profiles are already active. The third number could be added from the account list in Settings or through the Switch accounts option.

Each account would keep its own chat history, notifications, privacy settings, backup, and media. App Lock would also work separately for each profile, so securing one account would not automatically change the others. The account selector would continue to show a profile name, photo, and phone number, with a checkmark beside the active account.

Three accounts would help people with three phone numbers

Two slots cover the usual work-and-personal setup. A third slot could help people who keep a separate number for a business, side project, family, or another role. It could also reduce the need to use WhatsApp Business as a workaround or keep a second phone nearby.

The idea follows WhatsApp’s move to two accounts on one iPhone. If you need the current two-account setup, our updated guide to using two WhatsApp accounts on iPhone covers the available options.

The third account is not available yet

WABetaInfo says the feature was found in the 26.37.10.15 beta, but the three-account option itself is not ready for testing. Installing that build will not guarantee access, and WhatsApp has not shared a public release timeline.

For now, iPhone users can officially manage up to two accounts inside WhatsApp. The third slot is a planned expansion, not a feature you can turn on today.

excerpt.rendered: WhatsApp may let iPhone users add a third account alongside their existing two. The option is still under development and not available to beta testers yet.
